  dynamics library does this today, so the lane is parity, not an advantage.
- *Kill gate.* KILL-SYNTH-TRAJOPT.

#### 25.21.3 Bounded exact linkage synthesis [F]

**What it is.** Constructive design of parallel legs, ankles, steering linkages and small closed chains from
precision poses, in exact arithmetic, inside the real limits of the symbolic sibling. FACT
(`frankensympy/crates/fsym-solvers/src/real_rur.rs`, `fsym-polys/src/groebner.rs`): the real solver is capped at
8 variables, 64 equations, 4,096 terms, total degree 256, 4,096-bit coefficients, 2 × 10⁸ work units and
512 MiB, for zero-dimensional ideals only; Gröbner bases are capped at 1,024 basis polynomials and 10⁶ pending
pairs; there is no homotopy solver. Unbounded whole-robot Gröbner synthesis is therefore not built.

**Three steps.**

1. *Three-pose planar dyads.* Given three positions P₁, P₂, P₃ of a moving pivot in rational coordinates,
   eliminate the crank radius from ‖Pᵢ − O‖² = ‖P₁ − O‖²: the fixed pivot O solves the rational 2×2 system
   2·(Pᵢ − P₁)·O = ‖Pᵢ‖² − ‖P₁‖², i = 2, 3. Degenerate cases split by determinant rank. With a lug-pair catalog
   and pivot keep-in regions this enumerates dyads exactly.
2. *Finite higher-order templates.* Five-pose Burmester problems and planar four- and five-bar templates are
   posed as loop-closure polynomials in half-angle charts, with a Rabinowitsch saturation s·δ(x) − 1 = 0 to
   exclude zero-length and collinear roots. Only zero-dimensional systems inside the caps are submitted; a
   system outside them is refused (`FROB-REF-857`), not truncated.
3. *Circuit, branch and clearance certificate.* Real roots are isolated by interval contraction. One assembly
   circuit must traverse all target poses in order, with the reciprocal of the loop-closure Jacobian determinant
   bounded along the way, no self-collision, and the required reach. A tolerance box around the dimensions
   carries the certificate to as-built units.

The algebra is textbook; the certificate is the value. Step 3 exists because **a root of the synthesis equations
is not a mechanism.** Take ground pivots O₂ = (0, 0) and O₄ = (4, 0), crank O₂A of length 1, coupler AB of
length 4 and rocker O₄B of length 3: a crank-rocker. The distance from A to O₄ ranges over [3, 5] and never
reaches 1 or 7, so A, B and O₄ are never collinear and the sign of (B − A) × (O₄ − A) is constant on each
assembly circuit. At crank angle 0 the closure equations give B = (11/3, ±√80/3); at crank angle π they give
B = (11/5, ±12/5). A design whose precision poses are (crank 0, B above) and (crank π, B below) satisfies every
synthesis equation and cannot be driven from one pose to the other without disassembly. The circuit certificate
is the constant nonzero sign, proved over the crank interval by enclosure.

**Output.** A linkage as a `.fmodule` (§14) with its port contract, plus certificates of kinds `interval-box`
and `partition` for the circuit, branch, clearance and tolerance claims.

- *Known answers.* P₁ = (0, 0), P₂ = (2, 0), P₃ = (0, 2) give O = (1, 1) and radius² = 2; collinear positions
  give determinant zero and a refusal; five finitely separated poses give at most four real Burmester pairs
  (FACT, classical; Appendix H); the crank-rocker circuit defect above.
- *Pilot before funding.* 240 template instances (three-pose dyads with a lug catalog and keep-in regions),
  comparing the lane with multi-start numerical optimization of the same dimensions under the same circuit and
  clearance checks. Falsifier: a certified linkage binds or changes circuit on the referee; or more than a
  quarter of the template instances fall outside the caps.
- *Ceiling.* Three-position synthesis has closed-form circumcentres, so no speed claim is made against a
  competent baseline; the claim is the certificate.
- *Kill gate.* KILL-SYNTH-LINKAGE.

#### 25.21.4 Numerical continuation [M], on the CPU

**What it is.** For mechanism families whose synthesis or kinematics systems exceed the exact caps (four- and
six-bar path synthesis, Stewart–Gough forward kinematics, 6R inverse kinematics, parallel ankles), solve one
generic complex instance of the family once, then treat each new specification as a parameter homotopy
H(z, t) = F(z; (1 − t)·p₀ + t·p₁) and track only the solution paths.

**Decisions inside the lane.**

- *CPU, double precision.* Path tracking wants `f64`; Metal has no double precision; the GPU is not its home.
  An adaptive predictor–corrector with endgames, and recovery of ill-conditioned paths in extended precision.
- *Start systems by monodromy with a trace test*, not by a polyhedral start system, whose one-time cost for
  large families is unpriced. The generic solve is a ledgered, cached artifact with its own budget.
- *Certification outside the proof kernel.* Each claimed root gets a Smale α-test,
  α(f, z) < (13 − 3√17)/4 ≈ 0.157671, evaluated in exact rational or interval arithmetic by the checker:
  quadratic convergence of Newton's iteration from z to a root within twice the Newton step, distinctness by
  disjoint balls, non-reality by disjointness with the conjugate ball, and reality by the robust test of C-34
  (α(f, z) < 0.03 with ‖z − Re z‖ < 1/(20·γ(f, z))). An α-test proves a nearby nonsingular root and nothing about
  roots that were not found.
- *Labels.* `Complete` only when the certified count equals an independent generic count from a trace test, with
  no lost paths and no positive-dimensional components. Otherwise `Partial(certified_n, lost_n)`. A `Partial`
  result can support inclusion of the designs it found and can never support an exclusion.

**Scale of the problem** (FACT, Appendix H; to be re-read). The nine-point four-bar path-synthesis problem has
1,442 cognate triples, 4,326 solutions, against 286,720 paths for the best multihomogeneous homotopy; a six-bar
case in the literature needed a solution set of about 1.5 million; Stewart–Gough forward kinematics has 40
solutions and 6R inverse kinematics 16.

- *Pilot before funding.* Stewart–Gough forward kinematics on the CPU: recover 40 certified roots for ten
  generic parameter sets by parameter homotopy from one monodromy solve. Falsifier: any lost path that the trace
  test does not flag, or a `Complete` label on a run that missed a root.
- *Ceiling.* It answers "all isolated solutions" for one family at a time; nothing on the critical path needs
  it, and random mutation plus the exact lane covers the plan's reference robots.
- *Kill gate.* KILL-SYNTH-CONT.

Paper-scale pilots were run during planning, with protocols frozen before execution and independent rechecks of
the main results. They are in the planning reproduction bundle (Appendix H gives its location and digest; paths
below are inside it; its runner replays the standard-library checks with `python3 -B verify.py` and the full set
with `--all`). Every row is FACT, Appendix K, about a small program on a small model.

| Pilot | Path in the bundle | What it measured | Result | What it implies here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Static stance family | `mor/repro/P01-*` | Two exact classifiers of body–load feasibility; projected against lifted robust program | 11,520 of 11,520 states agree; 2,254 feasible allocations reconstructed; 114 of 2,304 bodies cover the mission; 102 of 102 conventional-solver spot checks agree; both programs return half-width 3/14 m in one solve each; a support-polygon-plus-capacity screen wrongly accepts 1,596 bodies | The family query is sound and useful; it has no speed advantage over a standard lifted program |
| Stance falsifier | `mor/repro/P01-*` | The same body under equal passive springs | (175, 115, 85, 25) N against a 160 N rating, where the active allocation peaks at 155 N | The authority model is part of the claim |
| Material probe | `mor/repro/P02-*` | Generated probe, programmed expert and direct measurement over 900 deterministic cases and four laws | Three-law probe 675 of 675 in class and 0 of 225 on the withheld law; expert equals generator; direct dwell 900 of 900 | Probe verdicts are conditional; direct measurement is the stronger comparator; no speed claim |
| Pad family | `mor/repro/P02-identification-family.*` | Minimum certified mass for a 75 N pull | 300 g and 240 g at centred nominal readings only; an admitted reading drops the three-compact bound to 73.79 N | Certificates are bound to their reading set |
| Sensor aliasing | `mor/repro/P03-*` | Exact Bayes success with repeated binary reads | 27/32, 459/512, 3807/4096; a shared error bit stays at 3/4; a stop-at-gap-two rule reaches 9/10 in 16/5 expected reads | Error dependence and deadlines decide sensor budgets |
| Docking, two gains | `mor/repro/P04-*`, `P05-*` | Exact three-tick docking with one velocity packet | Both gains dock with an on-time packet; ε < (U + 1/2)/4; 561 cells: 344 admitted, 217 excluded, nine on the boundary; all 561 late-packet cells excluded; 51 linear programs agree | Observation timing decides feasibility; a conventional scenario tree gets the same answer |
| Docking, three gains | `followups/docking_support.*` | Add gain 33/32 | Exact docking unsatisfiable; worst error at least 1/65 m; 34,590 positive labels per grid reverse | Certificates are bound to the declared hypothesis support |
| Pusher | `pusher/` | Specialized against composed solver on ten fixtures; six corrupted certificates | 20 of 20 intervals match in each arm; six of six bad certificates rejected; composed over specialized median time 1.345 warm and 1.088 cold | No new kind of answer on this plant; the speed gate failed |
| Pusher audit | `pusher/AUDIT_PILOT.md`, `pusher/audit_pilot/` | Timing ceiling; quantifier elimination from the raw plant | A residual of 575.7 µs that the solver does not touch (parsing, assembly, checking, serialization and harness, not separately timed), so a zero-cost solver would reach about 1.46 warm (842.8 ÷ 575.7); an off-the-shelf engine produced the family answer directly for 8 of 12 queries | The speed test had no power; compute the ceiling before running one |

| Decision reuse | `information/reuse_check.*` | Semantic receipt against a hermetic dependency graph over four edit states | Both: 3 pair evaluations and 2 reductions; all verdicts match fresh replay; omitting one dependency inherits a stale promotion | No reuse advantage over a correctly keyed graph |
| Shared bus | `information/contract_bus_check.py` | Two fingers on one unit-current bus | Zero one-tick schedules; two two-tick schedules; an additive peak rule falsely prunes | Negative control for contract compilers |

| Static against dynamic sill | `sill/` | Sampled statics against a planar dynamic scorer, 156 cases | 94 agree; 62 static rejections succeed dynamically; an audit found scorer defects | A static rejection is a candidate for a dynamic test |

What the pilots did not do is as important as what they did.

- **None used FrankenSim dynamics, FrankenSim contact or a real sensor pipeline.** The analytic pilots used
  small CPU programs and conventional solvers. The native runs executed one scalar decision kernel.
- **The integrated interface remains a hypothesis.** The independent audit of the planning study classed "a
  scoped interface for checked inclusions, exclusions and unresolved cells, returning a distinguishing
  intervention or an ambiguity witness" as HYPOTHESIS: the pilots establish that individual witness types can be
  computed; none runs a combined agent interface, certifies an acquired physical capability, or measures
  authoring cost.
- **Every pilot's strong baseline tied or won.** A lifted linear program tied the projection. A programmed
  expert tied the probe generator and direct measurement beat both on the withheld law. Exact Bayes tied the
  sensor calculation. A scenario-tree program tied the docking family. A dependency graph tied the receipt.
  Quantifier elimination produced the pusher answers. What survives is the interface: one typed question, a
  checked answer in a common form, and the discipline of counterexamples. That is what this chapter specifies,
  and why ADR-AUGUR-03 and ADR-AUGUR-09 exist.
- **No physical claim follows.** The material laws are artificial, the loads stipulated, the plants scalar.

### 25.23 Delivery order and stop decisions

The aim is to find the first class of amended engineering decisions where the whole workflow can be an order of
magnitude faster, starting where correctness is independently decidable and extending to high-dimensional
contact, vision and learning only after a cost has been located that survives strong baselines.

| Order | Milestone | Working slice | Evidence that buys the next investment | Decision if the test fails |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | M1 | A fresh agent is given the docking mission. Through the CLI or MCP it changes the allowed motor authority, the read error and the delivery tick, and asks for the feasible sensor–actuator region | `frob-verify` reproduces the boundary ε < (U + 1/2)/4, finds the exact shared reading at equality, and accepts an ordinary scenario-tree program as a competing answer. The agent explains which hardware restriction to relax | Repair the mapping from sensors and actuators to the game before adding physics. Ship the reference algorithm if it gives the better answer per engineering hour |
| 2 | M1–M3 | Amend the stance, material and load-sharing assumptions of §25.13–§25.14 through one schema | One edit preserves a valid witness; a second forces withdrawal; a third changes the required instrument. All three match independent full recomputation | If uncertainty in the physical contract dominates, spend the next increment on measurement, or settle for a narrower envelope |
| 3 | M3 | Seek a decision in hybrid contact that the cheap model gets wrong, starting from a dry and split-grip stance, one periodic gait and a rear-wheel pull-over | A paired world or an edited body reverses a design decision for a reproducible physical reason and breaks an overbroad proof. A refined controller or body recovers under the named conditions | If scene reduction changes the mechanism, or collocation wins, keep the counterexample and advance the conventional control path |
| 4 | M4 | Time source-to-verdict amendments on heterogeneous bodies with sensing, controller updates, contact and independent checking | The matched rival spends enough time on repeatable work for ten-fold to remain possible. A breakdown by stage locates the saving. Both native backends agree on accepted outcomes for the tested profile | Stop specialized GPU work in cells where transfers, authoring, training, checker work or baseline reuse rule out the target |
| 5 | M8 | Return an engineer's Pareto set for the two-carrier brownfield handoff, then commission the multi-room shift | A modified site, a modified body and a relay policy are compared under one mission. Withheld evidence overturns or supports a named prediction. Speed and physical claims are reported separately | Reduce to the failed subtask; until it is revalidated its uncertainty propagates through the handoff contract |

**The first slice an implementer can finish.** Two gains, two packet timings, one actuator bound, one
observation-noise family. Translate the query to a conventional scenario-tree linear program; export the exact
success region and the equality counterexample; check both outside the process; mutate the packet timestamp and
rerun. The compulsory interfaces are a causal history, a feasible controller, two indistinguishable worlds, an
exact physical parameter chart, and an independent checker. The verb returns what additional measurement or
actuator authority would restore feasibility. This ships as a CPU worked example before the first complex GPU
kernel exists, and it is the M1 exit demonstration for this chapter.

**The second slice, which could reveal a ten-fold opportunity.** Change one measured surface law in a warehouse
with multiple routes, body variants and sensor mounts. Compile the exact dependency support of each accepted
result (§25.8). Prove that an edit disjoint from a result's support preserves it, or recheck the precise
obligation where the changed interval still lies within slack. A conventional dependency graph, an incremental
optimizer and a hot-started simulator are eligible comparators, and their fastest correct implementation sets
the bar.

**A release cell names its capability and its limit**, for example "exact static family with independent active
vertical reactions", "time-bounded sensor game certificate", or "empirical mobile-manipulator ranking in the
sealed kitchen setup". No cell is described more broadly than the fixture that qualified it.

### 25.24 Refusals

Mission and certificate refusals are in the `8xx` family (evidence and protocol). The block 840–859 is used
here. Each carries a message, the offending field and ranked repairs.

| Code | Refused because | First repair offered |
|---|---|---|
| `FROB-REF-868` | The `.fmission` file is not valid: unknown field, missing unit, misspelt parameter, number not an exact string | The schema diff |
| `FROB-REF-874` | The world family is empty, or its scope changed after candidates were tested | The emptying constraint |
| `FROB-REF-877` | The predicates conflict with the world family for every design | A minimal conflicting subset, with its Farkas certificate where linear |
| `FROB-REF-881` | Evidence or a certificate establishes a different quantifier prefix than the query's, including clairvoyant evidence offered for a robust claim | The prefix it does establish |
| `FROB-REF-884` | No quantifier prefix, or a hidden parameter with no persistence declaration | The two candidate declarations and the fixture that separates them |
| `FROB-REF-887` | A policy is indexed by a parameter the controller cannot observe | Move the parameter into the world, or add the calibration observation |
| `FROB-REF-846` | A chance constraint lacks its population, event or confidence, or marginal stage rates are multiplied without a dependence assumption | The joint-outcome request |
| `FROB-REF-847` | An observation has no arrival instant, or a policy uses information before it arrives | The instant at which it becomes usable |
| `FROB-REF-848` | A proof kind is unknown, at an unknown version, disabled, or used outside its scope | The kinds admitted for this claim |
| `FROB-REF-849` | Certificate arithmetic is malformed: a non-reduced rational, a size limit exceeded, an interval without a declared rounding | Re-encode; or split the cell |
| `FROB-REF-850` | A frame, unit, sign or port order in a certificate does not match its definitions (a first moment passed as a torque; reordered feet) | The typed field that disagrees |
| `FROB-REF-851` | A certificate assumes an authority the design does not declare, or omits a force floor or other active bound | Re-solve under the declared authority |
| `FROB-REF-852` | A monotone or symmetry transport lacks a side condition | The missing sub-certificate |
| `FROB-REF-853` | A minimum is claimed without a matching lower bound, or an unattained infimum is reported as attained | `feasible-candidate` with its gap |
| `FROB-REF-854` | A classifier, screen or certificate is reused outside its eligibility: support, deadline, error units or tolerance changed | `mission.revalidate` |
| `FROB-REF-855` | Evidence profiles are mixed inside one cell, or a probability mass is requested without a supplied weighting | Split the cell; supply the weighting |
| `FROB-REF-856` | A region certificate is requested over more parameters than the admitted limit, or a joint paving is requested | The per-constraint decomposition |
| `FROB-REF-857` | A synthesis system is outside the symbolic caps or is not zero-dimensional | A smaller template, or the continuation lane with its label |
| `FROB-REF-858` | Stage composition fails: an exit set not inside the next entry set, a clock mismatch, or a resource spent twice | The violating state or interval |
| `FROB-REF-859` | An experiment or world edit cannot be realized through the declared interfaces, or does not declare the causal path it changes | The nearest realizable intervention |

Standing rules, in addition to those of §35: a failed training run is never an exclusion; a solver failure is
never an exclusion; an unresolved cell is never reported as either verdict; and a query whose estimate exceeds
its budget is refused under the budget family with the estimate attached.

### 25.25 Invariants and proof obligations

| ID | Invariant |
|---|---|
| INV-AUGUR-01 | I ⊆ F ⊆ O under the declared model: every inner cell has an inclusion proof for the query's exact prefix, and every cell outside O has an exclusion proof for it |
| INV-AUGUR-02 | The inner, excluded and unresolved cells of an answer partition the declared domain, with disjoint interiors and stated boundary ownership |
| INV-AUGUR-03 | `MissionId` changes whenever a quantifier, comparator, world support, persistence declaration, observation timing, policy class or horizon changes |
| INV-AUGUR-04 | Answers are monotone in work: a later answer to the same `MissionId` moves cells only out of the unresolved set. A cell leaves I or re-enters O only through a logged withdrawal that names its counterexample |
| INV-AUGUR-05 | The class of an answer is the weakest class among its cells, and no operation raises a class |
| INV-AUGUR-06 | No numerical failure, timeout or failed search is recorded as an exclusion |
| INV-AUGUR-07 | A policy is never indexed by a quantity absent from the observation contract at the decision instant |
| INV-AUGUR-08 | A `.frobcert` family payload is self-contained: checking needs no network, no GPU, no simulator and no producer |
| INV-AUGUR-09 | Every exported answer, witness and bundle carries the `authorization` object with its three flags, all `false` |
| INV-AUGUR-10 | Scheduling heuristics (opportunity loss, learned proposers, agent guesses) can change the order and cost of work and cannot change any verdict |
| INV-AUGUR-11 | A candidate from `frob-synth` has no verdict until `frob-mission` assigns one through a proof rule |

| ID | Obligation | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| PO-AUGUR-01 | Each lowering from a design family and a mission to primitive equations is correct | A second, independently written lowering for every supported template, compared exactly; one deliberately invalid fixture per lowering that the checker must reject |
| PO-AUGUR-02 | The checker's big-integer and rational arithmetic is exact | Differential test against an independent implementation on 10⁶ random operations and all fixture certificates |
| PO-AUGUR-03 | The checker's interval arithmetic is outward-rounded using `std` only | Every operation widened by one unit in the last place in each direction; property test that the enclosure contains the exact rational result |
| PO-AUGUR-04 | `partition` checking is exact, including open and closed ends | Exhaustive test on boxes with shared faces, edges and corners in up to six dimensions |
| PO-AUGUR-05 | Bundle bytes are a deterministic function of the answer (class D0) | Encode on two hosts and two worker counts; compare digests |
| PO-AUGUR-06 | Each proof rule of §25.4.5 is sound on its finite and polyhedral fragments | Stated as candidate theorem cards for §12; until proved, tested against the mutation corpus and classed by the weakest step |
| PO-AUGUR-07 | The checker's dependency closure is `std` and shares no source file with any proposer | A closure check in the build, and a file-set comparison |

### 25.26 Known answers

Each row is exact under its stated model and hand-checkable. The numbered known-answer suite is compiled in §38.

### 25.28 Open questions

- **OPEN-AUGUR-1.** Whether `.fmission` predicates are written in the requirement language of `.ftask` (§24) or
  only reference its terms by identifier. Default: reference by identifier, so there is one grammar. Owner: the
  Arena lead. Blocks GATE-AUGUR-01.
- **OPEN-AUGUR-2.** Whether the linear programs are solved exactly over ℚ or in floating point with rational
  reconstruction. Default: the cone solver of `frob-algebra` in floating point, basis reconstruction over ℚ,
  exact check; a failed reconstruction leaves the cell unresolved. Decide at GATE-AUGUR-02 from the
  reconstruction failure rate.
- **OPEN-AUGUR-3.** The measured sparsity of the constraint-to-parameter graph for the plan's robot classes, and
  the coupled dimension that linkage closure adds. Default: region certificates are refused above six
  parameters. Owner: the Augur lead. Blocks GATE-AUGUR-09.
- **OPEN-AUGUR-4.** Whether a quantifier-elimination or SMT engine is admitted as a production dependency or
  only as a comparator outside the product. Default: comparator only; the product uses in-tree elimination for
  small linear systems. Owner: the project owner. Decide before the M3 partial gate, because KILL-AUGUR-TIE
  depends on it.
- **OPEN-AUGUR-5.** Sound reachable tubes for contact-rich full-order cells. No owner in the suite provides
  them. Default: constructive inclusion is limited to static, quasi-static, finite-game and low-dimensional
  smooth cells; contact-rich cells stay unresolved with `Tested` trajectories. Revisit at M4.
- **OPEN-AUGUR-6 (settled by §34, ADR-WS-02).** Where the `std`-only checking code lives, and who writes
  bundles. `frob-cert` has an empty dependency table and holds the schema, the reader and the checking rule for
  each proof kind; `frob-verify` is its binary. `frob-mission` never links it. A mission answer leaves
  `frob-mission` as plain proof objects (witnesses, cells, dual vectors, enclosures) in types defined in
  `frob-core`; `frob-lemma` serializes those objects into a `.frobcert` bundle, written against the schema and
  sharing no code with the reader; `frob-verbs` then runs the checker on the bundle before the answer is
  returned. Where this chapter says that `frob-cert` "reads and writes" the family payload, read: `frob-cert`
  defines and reads it, `frob-lemma` writes it. A defect shared by proposer and checker would need the same
  mistake in two code bases that have no common source.
- **OPEN-AUGUR-7.** The exit code of a mission query that stops on budget with certified cells (§25.3.4).
  Default: exit 2 with `resolution-unmet`. Owner: the Tether lead.
- **OPEN-AUGUR-8.** Who reviews the primitive equations in a bundle, and whether that review is recorded in the
  bundle. Default: unreviewed bundles say so in their flags and cannot be cited under the Proof claim outside
  the fixtures of §25.26.
- **OPEN-AUGUR-9.** Whether `.fmission` version 1 expresses several decision makers with separate histories.
  Default: the field is present and accepts one decision maker; more than one is refused until slice 5.
- **OPEN-AUGUR-10.** The compute and calendar envelope for the [M] slices of §25.17 to §25.20. Default: none is
  funded before its pilot passes. Owner: the project owner.
- **OPEN-AUGUR-11.** Whether a measure on unresolved sets should be standardized (volume in a named chart).
  Default: no measure; the caller supplies one in `resolution`, and probability mass is reported only under a
  supplied weighting.

### 25.29 Chance claims transport only through a coupling

**What it is.** [F] A restriction on `mission.transport` (§25.11), and the proof object that lifts it. The
refinement relation of §25.11 matches every possible successor of the target to an allowed successor of the source.
That preserves universal claims. It preserves only the support of a probability law, so it carries no chance claim
and no expected value.

**Counterexample.** Source and target each have one action and two outcomes, success and failure. The source
succeeds with probability 0.99 and the target with probability 0.01. Every target successor has a matching source
successor, so the relation holds, and the claim "succeeds with probability at least 0.95" is true of the source and
false of the target. Every coupling of the two laws disagrees on at least 0.98 of its mass, which is their
total-variation distance.

**Mechanism.** DESIGN:
- A transport certificate declares the kind of each transported claim: `universal`, `chance` or `expectation`.
- For `chance` and `expectation` it carries a coupling budget: for each step t of the horizon, a bound εₜ on the
  total-variation distance between the source and target transition-and-observation kernels at related states,
  under the command that the interface selects. The transported bounds are
  P_target(accept) ≥ P_source(accept) − Σₜ εₜ and, for a quantity in [0, B], |E_target − E_source| ≤ B·Σₜ εₜ. The
  coupling is causal: it uses no disturbance that the interface cannot have observed.
- Sources of εₜ, in order of strength. Exact computation for finite kernels (class Certified). A common-noise
  construction in which both systems are driven by one disturbance stream compiled at physical coordinates (C-40)
  and the relation is shown to persist, with its failure rate bounded from sealed paired runs (class Tested: a
  one-sided upper confidence bound). Otherwise none, and the claim is measured on the target by `eval.qualify`.
- A certificate that marks a chance claim `universal`, or omits the budget, is rejected by `frob-verify`
  (refusal: chance claim transported without a coupling budget).

Owner: `frob-mission` (proposer); `frob-lemma` and `frob-cert` (bundle and check).

**Known answers.** The two-outcome case: Σ ε = 0.98, the transported bound is 0.01, and the claim is refused. A
finite chain of 10 steps with ε = 0.003 per step: a source probability of 0.99 transports to at least 0.96, and the
exact target value computed by enumeration lies above it.

**Pilot, ceiling, kill.** Pilot: 200 random finite Markov fixtures with known kernels, then the tray carried by a
wheeled base and by a quadruped. Falsifier: one transported bound that the exact or sealed target value violates.
Ceiling: the budget helps only when Σ ε is small against the slack of the claim; it saves one qualification study
per transported skill and no simulation time.

| | |
|---|---|
| GATE-AUGUR-25 | Known answer. Zero violated bounds over the 200 finite fixtures; the two-outcome reversal is refused; on the tray fixture the 95% upper bound of the measured budget is below the claim's slack for at least one skill, or the kill gate fires. Finite part M4; tray M8. |
| ✖ KILL-COUPLING | Trigger: one violated transported bound that survives a repair cycle, or no skill on the tray fixture with a budget below its slack. Fallback: `mission.transport` carries universal claims only, and every chance or expected-value claim is re-measured on the target in the qualification lane of §24.13. |

### 25.30 No monotone fill without a proof of monotonicity

**What it is.** [S] A restriction on proof rule 3 (§25.4) and on every sweep that feeds a mission answer. A verdict
at an unevaluated parameter value is never inferred from its neighbours unless a checked monotonicity argument for
that parameter, model and verdict is attached. An observed pattern is not such an argument.

**Counterexample.** FACT (planning archive, the 300-trajectory planar friction sweep of the sill fixture; Appendix H;
to be re-run before a gate cites it): for the 75 mm wheel, a sharp lip and the payload shifted 40 mm backward, the
planar scorer returns success, timeout, success at μ = 0.500, 0.525 and 0.550. Filling every friction level above
the first success adds one success that did not occur. With the scoring period held at 1 ms, halving the physics
step from 50 µs to 25 µs changes the triplet to timeout, timeout, success; at 25 µs with a stiffer contact and
adjusted damping all three succeed. The physical reading of the middle timeout is unresolved, and the fill is
refuted without resolving it.

**Mechanism.** DESIGN:
- `mission.synthesize`, `nemesis.search` and `phylum.sweep` return `unresolved` for every parameter value that was
  neither evaluated nor covered by a proof. No verb interpolates verdicts.
- A fill is a proof step of the monotone-inheritance kind. It cites the theorem that makes the verdict monotone in
  the parameter under the declared model. The creep-limit rows of §24.10 qualify, because the friction demand
  μ ≥ tan θ is monotone in μ by construction. A dynamic rollout verdict has no such theorem by default.
- A detector runs on every swept scalar: along the sorted grid it counts the sign changes of the verdict. More than
  one change is recorded as a non-monotone outcome, with the grid, the step and the contact parameters, and is
  routed to the fidelity ledger (§16.8) for step-halving and stiffness variants. Results that depend on the affected
  interval are typed `model-conditional` until the variants agree.
- When the physics step is refined the requirement clock stays fixed (§24.5), so two refinements are compared on
  one definition of the verdict.

Owner: `frob-mission` (answers); `frob-nemesis` and `frob-phylum` (sweeps); `frob-analyze` (detector).

**Known answer.** A planted fixture with a provable band: a cart on a compliant sill mount passes below and above a
resonance band of mount stiffness and fails inside it, so the grid shows pass, fail, pass. The licensed fill on the
creep rig reproduces its exhaustive grid exactly. The unlicensed fill on the banded fixture is refused.

| | |
|---|---|
| GATE-AUGUR-26 | Known answer. On the banded fixture the detector flags the non-monotone outcome in 100 of 100 seeds, no verdict is filled, and the mission answer leaves the band `unresolved`; on the creep rig the licensed fill equals the exhaustive grid at every point; a mutant that fills above the first success is caught on both. M3. |

### 25.31 Monomial screens in exponent coordinates

This subsection extends §25.6 ("Monotone bounds first") and the static-exclusion step of the worklist in §25.7. It
excludes a whole design family when a conjunction of sizing relations is contradictory, with a certificate that is
checked in integer arithmetic. Tier [S]. Owners: `frob-mission` for the screen, `frob-cert` for the proof kind and its
checking rule. Verb: `mission.refute` for a family, and the worklist of `mission.synthesize`.

**The object.** Design parameters θ₁, …, θₙ are positive: lengths, masses, ratios, ratings. A monomial constraint is
c · θ₁^a₁ ⋯ θₙ^aₙ ≤ 1 with c a positive rational and integer exponents (rational exponents are cleared by raising the
inequality to a common power). Parameter bounds are monomial constraints: lo/θᵢ ≤ 1 and θᵢ/hi ≤ 1. Many static sizing
relations have this form: holding torque m·g·ℓ ≤ N·τ, no-load speed v·N ≤ ω·ℓ, bus current, pressure against sinkage.

**The certificate.** For constraints k = 1, …, K with coefficients c_k and exponent rows a_k, nonnegative integers
λ_k, not all zero, with

  Σ_k λ_k · a_k = 0   and   Π_k c_k^λ_k > 1

prove that no positive θ satisfies all K constraints: multiplying the constraints raised to the powers λ_k cancels
every parameter and leaves Π_k c_k^λ_k ≤ 1, a contradiction. In the coordinates y = ln θ the constraints are the
linear system a_k · y ≤ −ln c_k, and by the theorem of the alternative such λ exists whenever the system is
infeasible; because the exponent matrix is rational, λ can be taken integer. The search is a linear program in
floating point. Only the certificate is trusted: the checker verifies n integer sums, one per parameter, and
compares one product of integer powers of rationals with 1. It never evaluates a logarithm. Multipliers and bit
sizes have declared caps, and a certificate beyond them is refused, not approximated.

DESIGN: the proof kind `monomial-product` is added to the closed registry of §25.5.2 with class `Certified`, the
checking rule above and an invalid fixture per field. A cell's box bounds enter as constraints, so the same rule
excludes one cell or the whole positive orthant.

**Sums of monomials.** A constraint P(θ) = Σ_j m_j(θ) ≤ 1 with several monomial terms is not linear in y: its
logarithm is a convex log-sum-exp. Two necessary conditions are monomial and may join the system:

- each term alone: m_j ≤ 1;
- a weighted mean inequality: for positive rational weights w_j with Σ w_j = 1 and common denominator D,
  Σ_j m_j ≥ Π_j (m_j/w_j)^w_j, so P ≤ 1 implies Π_j (m_j/w_j)^(D·w_j) ≤ 1.

Any positive weights are sound. Default weights are equal, plus the term shares m_j/P at the centre of the cell,
rounded to denominators of at most 16. The screen only excludes. Inclusion, and cells the screen does not decide, go
to the per-constraint lane of §25.6.

**Known answer: no gear ratio and no leg length helps.** A leg must hold m·g = 12 kg · 9.81 m/s² = 117.72 N at lever
arm ℓ and move the foot at v = 1.5 m/s, through a reduction N, with a motor of torque τ = 2 N·m and speed
ω = 80 rad/s. The two constraints are (117.72/2) · ℓ · N⁻¹ ≤ 1 and (1.5/80) · ℓ⁻¹ · N ≤ 1, with coefficients 2943/50
and 3/160 and exponent rows (1, −1) and (−1, 1). The multipliers λ = (1, 1) cancel both parameters and give
8829/8000 = 1.103625 > 1. No (ℓ, N) exists. The certificate reads as physics: the mission needs
m·g·v = 176.58 W and the motor's corner power τ·ω is 160 W. Control: with τ = 2.5 N·m the product is
17,658/20,000 = 0.8829, no certificate exists, and ℓ = 0.2 m with N = 10 satisfies both constraints (0.94176 and
0.9375).

A per-constraint paving does not see this cheaply. Over ℓ ∈ [0.1, 0.4] m and N ∈ [5, 50] each constraint alone is
satisfiable (0.118 at ℓ = 0.1, N = 50 for the first; 0.234 at ℓ = 0.4, N = 5 for the second). The two feasible sets,
ℓ/N ≤ 0.01699 and ℓ/N ≥ 0.01875, are separated by a diagonal band that boxes approximate only by refinement.

**Counterexample: the term-wise screen is not a decision.** With two terms m₁ = m₂ = 0.6 each term passes and the sum
is 1.2. Equal weights give 4·m₁·m₂ = 1.44 > 1 and exclude it. With m₁ = 0.9 and m₂ = 0.15 the sum is 1.05, equal
weights give 4 · 0.135 = 0.54 and do not exclude, and the weights (6/7, 1/7) give 1.05⁷ ≈ 1.407 > 1 and do. Over a
cell with fixed weights the relaxation is an outer approximation, so an undecided cell says nothing.

**Scope and ceiling.** An exclusion covers the static rigid model named in the bundle and says nothing about dynamic
performance. No speed claim is made: for a single proposed design a pointwise check gives the same answer. The value
is a family exclusion with a one-line certificate and a named binding pair of constraints, which `mission.refute`
reports with the smallest change of a constant that removes the contradiction (here, motor corner power above
176.58 W).

**Gate.** GATE-AUGUR-27 (Known answer, M3). On 1,000 generated monomial systems of at most 12 parameters and 24
constraints with planted status: no feasible system is excluded; every infeasible system whose contradiction has a
product of at least 1.01 and fits the size caps is excluded; every certificate is accepted by `frob-verify`, and each
of 200 mutated certificates (one multiplier or one coefficient changed) is rejected. The leg fixture returns
λ = (1, 1) and 8829/8000; its control returns the witness; the two-term case (0.9, 0.15) is excluded at weights
(6/7, 1/7) and not at equal weights.

### 25.32 Utility brackets and the dominance stop

**Utility brackets [F].** This extends Rules 1 and 2 of §25.4.5 from feasibility to a bounded task utility, and gives
the ladder of §28.9 a sound reason to stop spending controller effort on a design. For a mission whose task declares a
utility u ∈ [0, 1] (a success probability, a normalized payload, a normalized energy margin), a design d and a world
law, a **bracket** is a pair L_d ≤ U*_d ≤ Ū_d, where U*_d is the best value any admitted causal controller achieves.

- *The upper end Ū_d* uses the relaxations of Rule 1: every contact force inside an outer wrench cone, every torque
  under the card envelope, the energy budget of A-20 with every admitted energy source, reach and deadline limits, and
  any observation a controller could wish for. Per scenario the relaxation is optimized for u instead of tested for
  feasibility, and Ū_d(w) is the outward-rounded optimum with its dual as certificate. Over a world law, the mean of
  Ū_d(w) on the sampled scenarios carries an upper confidence bound.
- *The lower end L_d* is achieved performance: rollouts of one frozen controller on confirmation addresses that its
  development never read, with a lower confidence bound. A stronger controller raises L_d and leaves Ū_d valid.

With m the comparison's margin and u_req the requirement threshold, four labels follow.

| Condition | Label | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Ū_d < u_req | `body-limited` | An exclusion under Rule 1, with its certificate |
| Ū_d − L_d ≤ m | `saturated` | More controller effort cannot change a decision at this margin |
| Ū_d − L_d > m, and Ū_d at or above the k-th best lower end | `controller-limited` | Effort belongs on the controller; the design escalates (the budget curves of §28) |
| Ū_d < L_c for a competitor c | `dominated` | **The dominance stop**: d receives no further training, fine-tuning or planner budget in this comparison |

Only the dominance stop removes work, and it is sound only when both bounds hold at once. With M designs compared at a
study level α, each one-sided bound is taken at level α/(2M) (DESIGN: a union bound; a design's bounds across
scenarios share one world sample). The stop ends effort inside one comparison. It is not an exclusion from O: a
dominated design may still satisfy the mission.

*Worked case.* A carrier of body mass 10 kg lifts a payload p through h = 2 m on a ramp with 300 J of usable stored
energy at the foot, and the mission admits arrival at the foot at up to 1.5 m/s. Utility is p divided by 10 kg. Every
controller obeys (10 + p)·(g·h − v²/2) ≤ 300 J, so 10 + p ≤ 300/(19.62 − 1.125) = 16.22 kg and Ū = 0.622. A
relaxation that leaves out the approach energy gives 10 + p ≤ 300/19.62 = 15.29 kg and Ū = 0.529. Against a
competitor with L_c = 0.60 the incomplete relaxation issues a dominance stop, and it is false: p = 6 kg is feasible
with a run-up, because 16 × 9.81 × 2 = 313.92 J ≤ 300 + ½·16·1.5² = 318 J. The sound bound 0.622 does not stop the
design. This is the utility form of the sill case of Rule 1, and the incomplete relaxation is the seeded defect the
gate must catch.

*Honest limits.* A bound over all controllers is only as tight as its relaxation. For contact-rich full-order tasks
it is often vacuous (Ū = 1); the bracket then says nothing and has cost one small program. Whole-body certifying
relaxations are not built here. The value concentrates in briefs limited by energy, torque, reach or a deadline.

*Ceiling.* The stop removes controller-stage work only. If a fraction x of candidates is dominated before training
and computing the bounds costs a fraction y of baseline controller work, the stage shrinks by 1/((1 − x) + y): 10 at
x = 0.93 and y = 0.03, and 1.4 at x = 0.3 (illustrative). The end-to-end gain is capped by the controller stage's
share of the phase ledger (§2.2).

*Owners and verbs.* `frob-mission` produces both ends as Rule 1 certificates over the relaxations of `frob-analyze`;
`frob-opt` applies the labels and the stop in the ladder. `mission.refute` returns Ū_d with its binding constraint.
`eval.compare --bracket` returns both ends, the label and, for a dominated design, the competitor and both
certificates. A request to stop on a bound whose relaxation does not enclose a declared state or energy source is
refused, under the existing rule for exclusions (§28.4).

| Gate | Claim | Threshold (TARGET) | First milestone |
|---|---|---|---|
| GATE-AUGUR-28 | Known answer; Design comparison | On an exhaustively solvable planar ramp-and-carrier family (states and controls discretized so the optimum of each of at least 500 design and scenario pairs is known by dynamic programming): every Ū at or above the optimum, every L at or below it, zero false dominance stops; the run-up candidate is not stopped and the relaxation without approach energy is rejected. On a held-out brief limited by energy or torque: controller effort per accepted decision at least 3 times lower than static filters followed by the ladder, at matched decisions | M4 |

| Kill gate | Trigger | Fallback |
|---|---|---|
| ✖ KILL-AUGUR-BRACKET | One false stop on the solvable family or in an audited campaign (the audit of §28.12 samples dominated designs and trains them); or less than 3 times at matched decisions; or the label changes the agent's next action in under a tenth of comparisons | Brackets are printed as advisory labels, no stop is automatic, and designs leave the ladder only by the ladder's own rules |

### 25.33 Placement and sizing along a prescribed motion

**A fifth constructive lane [F].** For a fixed topology with fixed joint axes and link lengths, the inverse dynamics
of a prescribed motion is linear in the inertial parameters (C-03, C-04). At knot k of a motion (q_k, q̇_k, q̈_k) with
active contacts C_k,

    Y(q_k, q̇_k, q̈_k)·π = Sᵀ·τ_k + Σ_{c ∈ C_k} J_c(q_k)ᵀ·λ_{c,k},

where π stacks the ten inertial parameters of every body, S selects the actuated coordinates, and Y is the regressor
that `frob-kir` emits from the derived inverse-dynamics kernel. The lane (`mission.synthesize --strategy placement`,
owned by `frob-synth`) takes a small library of nominal motions for the archetype (from the gait atlas, the skill
artifacts and centroidal planning) and solves one cone program per motion and per catalog choice, over:

- **inertia**: π = π_fixed + Σ_s m_s·φ_s with m_s ≥ 0, where φ_s is the parameter vector of a unit mass at an
  admissible site s (battery cells, compute, ballast), and, for bodies whose distribution is free, the pseudo-inertia
  cone and the mass-support bound of C-03;
- **contact forces** λ_{c,k} inside the friction cone of the scene's interface card at that contact;
- **joint torques** τ_k, tied to the others by the equation above, under the cards of §15 at fixed gear ratios N:
  peak |τ_{j,k}| ≤ η·N·τ_peak; thermal ‖τ_j‖₂ ≤ √K·η·N·τ_cont over the K knots; voltage
  R·|τ_{j,k}|/(η·N·k_t) + k_e·N·|q̇_{j,k}| ≤ V_bus, linear because q̇ is data;
- **objective**: electrical energy Σ_j Σ_k [R·(τ_{j,k}/(η·N·k_t))² + τ_{j,k}·q̇_{j,k}]·Δt, a convex quadratic.

The solver is the one cone solver of §22.5, on the CPU; the certificate kinds are `lp-primal`, `lp-farkas` and
`conic-farkas` of §25.5. Three results come back: a placement and sizing that realizes the motion at least energy; a
lower bound on electrical energy *for that motion*; or a dual certificate that no placement and no admissible contact
forces realize it.

*What the certificate says, and what it does not.* The statement excluded is the pair (design cell, motion). A design
that completes the mission by a different motion is untouched. The lane therefore proposes candidates and prunes
motions; it removes a cell from O only when the mission itself prescribes the motion (a declared lift profile, a
commanded acceleration). A count of library motions a design can realize is a screening signal under rule 4 of §28.4.

*Three limits, each with its smallest case.*

1. *A continuous site enters quadratically.* A mass m at position x contributes m·x to the first moments and m·x² to
   the second. The program is linear in masses at fixed sites, not in a position. A splittable mass (cells along a
   rail) is exact; for one unsplittable module the program is a relaxation whose infeasibility still excludes every
   single-site placement, and a fractional optimum is rounded and re-solved.
2. *Energy is not jointly convex in torque and gear ratio.* With N a variable the peak, thermal and voltage limits
   stay convex (the voltage limit times N reads c₁·|τ| + k_e·|q̇|·N² ≤ V_bus·N), so feasibility over a continuous
   ratio is one cone program. The copper-loss term g(τ, N) = τ²/N² is not convex: g(0, 1) = 0, g(2, 3) = 4/9 and at
   the midpoint g(1, 2) = 1/4 > 2/9. Minimum energy therefore enumerates catalog ratios, one program each.
3. *Link lengths are not variables.* Y depends on them nonlinearly. They are enumerated on the cells of the query.

*Known answer.* A rear-drive cart with wheelbase 1 m and centre of mass at floor height: 15 kg fixed at 0.5 m from
the rear axle and a 5 kg battery at x_b on a rail. The rear normal force is g·[7.5 + 5·(1 − x_b)] and traction needs
μ·N_r ≥ 20·a. With μ = 1/2 and g = 981/100 m/s²: at a = 3 m/s² the motion is feasible exactly when x_b ≤ 35/654 m
(53.5 mm); the largest acceleration over all placements is 0.5 × 9.81 × 12.5/20 = 3.066 m/s²; at a = 4 m/s² the
program is infeasible for every placement, with the traction inequality as its dual. The same 4 m/s² motion is
feasible with all wheels driven (μ·g = 4.905 m/s²), and the original cart reaches the same goal by a slower motion:
the certificate excludes a motion, not the cart.

*Pilot, ceiling and gate.* Ceiling: the lane decides only the share of a design decision that is placement and
sizing for known motions, and it starts a search; it does not replace one. A conventional optimizer over a dynamics
library can pose the same program, so this is a convenience of the typed core and not a differentiator. Pilot before
funding: the cart and one quadruped trot with a movable battery, two engineer-days on the CPU.

| Gate | Claim | Threshold (TARGET) | First milestone |
|---|---|---|---|
| GATE-AUGUR-29 | Known answer; Design comparison | The cart: boundary 35/654 m in exact rationals, the dual at 4 m/s² accepted by `frob-verify`. The regressor identity Y·π equals the derived inverse dynamics within 10⁻¹² relative on 10⁴ random states per reference robot. A request for jointly optimal energy and ratio is routed to enumeration. On 30 designs and two missions, candidates initialized by the lane beat their class templates by at least 15% in electrical cost of transport in closed-loop evaluation at a 95% paired lower bound, or start within 10% of the optimum that forward co-design reaches; the share of designs infeasible on every library motion that still pass the mission is reported | M4 |

| Kill gate | Trigger | Fallback |

| ✖ KILL-SYNTH-REGRESSOR | The design-comparison part of GATE-AUGUR-29 fails; or more than 15% of designs infeasible on every library motion pass the mission in closed loop, in which case the motion-count screening signal is withdrawn first | The mass-placement program of §25.21 and A-24 as they stand; candidates start from class templates |

### 25.34 Weak-variable enclosure and the split set

**Boxes of any dimension with a bounded split set [F].** This extends §25.6 and corrects the reading of
ADR-AUGUR-06 under which a certificate's box has at most about six parameters. What is bounded is the number of
parameters that are bisected, not the number the constraint reads. A constraint may depend on every parameter of
a family and still be decided over most of the box, when most of that dependence is weak.

*Definitions.* For a lowered constraint g(x) ≤ 0 on a box B ⊂ ℝⁿ, an affine-form enclosure gives
g(x) ∈ g₀ + Σᵢ aᵢ·εᵢ + r·[−1, 1] with εᵢ ∈ [−1, 1]. Parameter i contributes width 2·|aᵢ| and the nonlinear
remainder contributes 2·r. Order the parameters by |aᵢ|. The **split set** S is the leading part of that order,
capped at six (DESIGN: the cap of ADR-AUGUR-06). The other parameters are **weak**, and the **weak width** is
ω = 2·(Σ_{i ∉ S} |aᵢ| + r) with every weak parameter at its full range.

*Algorithm.* A queue holds sub-boxes that differ from B only in the coordinates of S.

1. Enclose g over the sub-box with every weak parameter at full range. Upper end at most 0: inner. Lower end above
   0: excluded. Either result is an `interval-box` or `taylor-box` certificate whose box is the full n-dimensional
   sub-box. The checker's work is linear in n per box.
2. Otherwise bisect along the parameter of S with the largest current contribution. The enclosure is linearized
   again on each sub-box, so the aᵢ are local and the order may change.
3. Stop splitting a sub-box when the width contributed by S falls below ω. No further split inside S can decide
   it, because the weak parameters alone straddle the threshold. The cell is `unresolved` with the reason
   `weak-variable width`, and the report names the weak parameter with the largest |aᵢ| as the next candidate.
4. The budget is the box count of §25.6, per constraint.

Combination across constraints is unchanged: a design is inner when it lies in every constraint's inner set. Each
set is now stored over the whole box with its split set recorded.

*Known answer.* On [0, 1]²⁰ let m = (1/19)·Σ_{i=2..20} (2·xᵢ − 1) and δ = 0.01·m², so 0 ≤ δ ≤ 0.01. Require
g₁ = x₁ + δ − 0.8 ≤ 0 and g₂ = 0.2 + δ − x₁ ≤ 0. Both constraints read all 20 parameters and neither is monotone
in x₂ to x₂₀. With S = {x₁} the weak width is 0.01. The slab x₁ < 0.2 is excluded by g₂; 0.21 ≤ x₁ ≤ 0.79 is
inner for both; x₁ > 0.8 is excluded by g₁; the slabs [0.2, 0.21) and (0.79, 0.8] are unresolved. Five slabs
decide 0.98 of the volume: 0.58 inner and 0.40 excluded. An isotropic paving of the same box with the budget of
§25.6 (10⁴ boxes, 13 bisections, less than one cut per axis) decides almost none of it.

*Negative control.* g = Σ_{i=1..20} xᵢ − 10 ≤ 0 on the same box. Every parameter contributes the same width, 1.
With any six parameters in S the weak width is 14 and the sum over S ranges over [0, 6]. An inner cell would need
that sum to be at most −4 and an excluded cell would need it above 10; neither can occur. Stopping rule 3 fires at
once, since 6 < 14. The mechanism must return `unresolved` for the whole box after one enclosure and no
bisection, although half the volume is feasible by symmetry. A run that bisects here burns budget, and a run that
returns an inner or excluded cell is unsound. The exact answer to this constraint belongs to the monotone rule of
§25.6. That is the point of the control: the split-set rule is for dependence that is weak, not for strong
dependence spread evenly.

*Scope and ceiling.* The mechanism decides volume only where the weak width is small against the constraint's
margin. HYPOTHESIS: for the static constraints of legged and wheeled classes, the parameters of other limbs and
of distal bodies enter one leg's torque, reach and clearance constraints weakly, through posture and load share.
OPEN-AUGUR-3 measures the constraint-to-parameter graph and now records |aᵢ| per parameter, not only incidence.
Ceiling: no speed claim. Decided volume is evidence quality and tolerance robustness (§25.6); the number that
matters is candidate evaluations avoided.

*Owner and verbs.* `frob-mission` owns the driver and the choice of S; enclosures come from the interval and
Taylor-model arithmetic behind the airlock; certificates are of the existing kinds. `mission.refute` and
`mission.synthesize` take `--split-cap k` (default 6) and report, per constraint, S, ω and the three volume shares.

The negative control returns `unresolved` for the whole box with one enclosure evaluation and no bisection. On the 12-parameter static quadruped family of §25.6, against per-constraint decomposition restricted to constraints that read at most six parameters and at the same box budget: at least 10 percentage points more decided volume, or at least 10% more candidate evaluations avoided, with no certificate rejected | M4 |

### 25.35 The controller class is part of a family answer

**What it is.** [S] A typing rule for inclusion over a set of loads or disturbances. A cell is certified for a
declared class of control laws, and the certificate carries the law. One feasible command per vertex of a load set
shows that a feasible command exists for every load in the hull, because the constraints are convex. It does not show
that a controller of the declared class can produce those commands. The class is the set of functions from the
observed quantities to the command, and it is a field of `policy_class` beside the authority model of §25.13. Owner:
`frob-mission` for the lowering, `frob-cert` for the checking rule. Verbs: `mission.synthesize`, `mission.refute`.

**The stance family under three classes.** The mission of §25.13: 400 N on feet at (±a, ±b) with a = 1/3 m, ratings of
160 N, and load moments P = (P_x, P_y) with abs(P_x) ≤ 60 N·m and abs(P_y) ≤ 30 N·m. The feet are ordered [++, +−, −+,
−−], and foot i has signs (s_x, s_y).

| Class | Smallest half-width b | A law that attains it |
|---|---|---|
| `adjustable`: any function of the observed P | 3/14 m | f(P) = Σ_σ w_σ(P)·f_σ over the four vertex allocations f_σ of §25.13, with w_σ(P) = ¼·(1 + σ_x·P_x/60)·(1 + σ_y·P_y/30) |
| `affine`: f(P) = f₀ + A·P | 1/2 m | fᵢ(P) = 100 + s_x·P_x/(4a) + s_y·P_y/(4b) newtons |
| `constant`: P is not observed before the command | none | No fixed f satisfies Σ xᵢ·fᵢ = P_x for two values of P_x |

- *Adjustable.* The weights w_σ are nonnegative, sum to one and satisfy Σ w_σ·P_σ = P. The interpolant therefore meets
  the three balance equations at every P and stays inside the ratings by convexity. It is not affine: at b = 3/14 m
  its coefficient of P_x·P_y is (−20, 20, 20, −20)/1800 N per (N·m)². At P = 0 it gives 100 N on every foot.
- *The four witnesses are not values of one affine law.* An affine function on a rectangle satisfies f(60, 30) +
  f(−60, −30) = f(60, −30) + f(−60, 30). The vertex allocations give (160, 240, 240, 160) N on the left and (240, 160,
  160, 240) N on the right.
- *Affine.* If an affine law is feasible, so is its image under each reflection of the load rectangle with the
  matching exchange of feet, and so is the average of the four images, because the constraints are convex and the
  mission is symmetric. The average is invariant under the reflections, which forces the form in the table, and the
  balance equations fix its coefficients. Its largest value is 100 + 60/(4a) + 30/(4b) = 145 + 15/(2b) N, which is at
  most 160 N exactly when b ≥ 1/2 m; its smallest value, 55 − 15/(2b) N, is positive there. The affine class needs 7/3
  times the half-width of the adjustable class.
- *The passive suspension is an affine controller.* The symmetric affine law is the load sharing of four equal
  springs. At b = 1/4 m it gives (175, 115, 85, 25) N at the vertex (60, 30), which is the passive allocation of
  §25.13. The authority counterexample and the class counterexample are one fact seen twice.

**Mechanism.** DESIGN.

- `policy_class` gains the field `law`, one of `adjustable`, `affine`, `piecewise-affine` and `constant`. The
  arguments of the law are the fields listed as observed before the decision. A query that asks for inclusion over a
  load or disturbance set and omits `law` is refused (refusal: inclusion over a disturbance set without a declared law
  class).
- Lowering. For `adjustable`: one command per vertex of the load polytope, which is the lifted program of §25.13; the
  returned law is the multilinear interpolant on a box, and the barycentric interpolant on a declared triangulation
  otherwise. For `affine`: the unknowns are (f₀, A); equalities are imposed as identities in P by matching
  coefficients; inequalities are imposed at the vertices, where an affine function on a polytope takes its extremes.
  For `constant`: one command for every vertex.
- Certificate. The `lp-primal` kind carries a `law` object with its kind (`multilinear-vertex`, `barycentric`,
  `affine` or `constant`) and its data. The checker recomputes the balance equations and the ratings at every vertex.
  For `affine` it checks that the listed vertex commands equal f₀ + A·P exactly. For `multilinear-vertex` it checks
  that the load set is a box whose vertices are the listed ones. In every case it checks that each argument of the law
  arrives before the decision instant (§20.4).
- `mission.refute` under `affine`, for b in [3/14, 1/2) m, returns the dual of the affine program and names the class
  as a repair beside the geometric one: widen to 1/2 m, or admit a law that is not affine.

**Known answers** (exact rationals; every value is derived on file from the stated inputs).

| `affine`, b = 1/2 m | Inner; (160, 130, 70, 40) N at the vertex (60, 30) | — |
| `affine`, b = 1/4 m | Excluded; the symmetric law needs 175 N | A hull certificate with no law object |
| `constant`, any b | Excluded | A constant command accepted because each vertex has some feasible command |

|---|---|
| GATE-AUGUR-31 | Known answer. Through the public verb the stance family returns 3/14 m under `adjustable` with the bilinear law, 1/2 m under `affine` with the symmetric law and a matching dual, and an exclusion for every b under `constant`. The bilinear law evaluated on a 121 × 61 grid of loads meets every balance equation and rating in exact rationals. The four vertex witnesses relabelled `affine` are rejected by `frob-verify`, and so is a certificate with no law object. M1. |

### 25.36 Docking to a finite tolerance over a continuous gain interval

**What it is.** [S] The amended docking game that §25.15 leaves open, solved in closed form. It is a second known
answer of the docking family: a least guaranteed tolerance over a continuum of hidden gains, with an irrational
algebraic optimum, a rational witness above it and a rational exclusion below it. Owner: `frob-mission`, with
`frob-conformance` for the fixture. Verbs: `mission.synthesize` with the objective "least guaranteed tolerance", and
`mission.refute`.

**The game.** The plant, the three ticks and the packet timing are those of §25.15. The gain g is any constant in [1,
2]. The command bound is U = 3/4. The first velocity reading r = g·p + e arrives before the second command, with e in
[−ε, +ε] and ε = 1/64. The robot must be exactly at rest after the third tick, and the guarantee sought is abs(x₃ − 1)
≤ δ for every admitted g and e.

**The answer.** The least guaranteed tolerance is δ* = (√1745 − 41)/32 m, about 24.1624 mm, the positive root of 16·δ²
+ 41·δ − 1 = 0. It is attained with the first command p* = (39 + √1745)/128, about 0.631041. A 20 mm requirement is
infeasible. A 25 mm requirement is met with the rational probe p = 5/8.

**Derivation.** Write p = u₀ and c = 2p + u₁. Rest forces u₂ = −p − u₁, and then x₃ = g·c. For p > 0 the limits on u₁
and u₂ confine c to [2p − U, p + U]. A reading r admits the gains [a, b] with a = max(1, (r − ε)/p) and b = min(2, (r
+ ε)/p), and the tolerance requires (1 − δ)/a ≤ c ≤ (1 + δ)/b. A common c exists at every reading exactly when three
conditions hold.

1. *Ambiguity.* The ratio b/a is largest at the reading p + ε, where a = 1 and b = 1 + 2ε/p. The interval for c is
   nonempty there exactly when ε/(p + ε) ≤ δ, that is p ≥ ε·(1 − δ)/δ.
2. *Reach at the high gain.* Where the reading admits g = 2, c is at most (1 + δ)/2, so 2p − U ≤ (1 + δ)/2, that is p
   ≤ (2U + 1 + δ)/4.
3. *Reach at the low gain.* Where the reading admits g = 1, c is at least 1 − δ, so p + U ≥ 1 − δ.

A larger probe eases the first condition and tightens the second. Equating them gives 4ε·(1 − δ) = δ·(2U + 1 + δ),
which is 16·δ² + 41·δ − 1 = 0 at U = 3/4 and ε = 1/64, with p* = (2U + 1 + δ*)/4. The third condition is slack. A
probe p ≤ 0 gives c ≤ U = 3/4, which is short of 1 − δ in the world g = 1 for every δ < 1/4. The error interval and
the tolerance are closed, so the optimum is attained and the answer carries `attained: true`, unlike the strict family
of §25.3.6. DESIGN arithmetic: for other values with U ≥ (1 + δ)/2 the same argument gives the positive root of δ² +
(2U + 1 + 4ε)·δ − 4ε = 0.

**The witness policy.** After the reading, compute [a, b], choose any c in [max((1 − δ)/a, 2p − U), min((1 + δ)/b, p +
U)], and command u₁ = c − 2p and u₂ = −p − u₁.

**Certificates.** The optimum is irrational. It is returned as the root of its polynomial with a rational enclosure,
bracketed by two rational certificates.

- *Inclusion at δ = 1/40 with p = 5/8.* 1/41 ≤ 1/40; 2p − U = 1/2 ≤ 41/80; p + U = 11/8 ≥ 39/40. The reading interval
  [p − ε, 2p + ε] is partitioned at p + ε and 2p − ε, and the interval for c is checked at the ends of each piece,
  where its bounds are monotone in r. Kind: `partition` over `interval-box` pieces.
- *Exclusion at δ = 1/50.* The polynomial is negative there: 16/2500 + 41/50 − 1 = −0.1736. Every p in (0, 49/64)
  fails condition 1 through an alias pair: the worlds g = 1 with e = +ε and g = min(2, 1 + 2ε/p) with the error that
  gives the same reading share p + ε and need disjoint values of c. Every p above 63/100 fails condition 2. Since
  63/100 < 49/64, the two cases cover (0, 3/4], and p ≤ 0 fails as above. Kind: `alias-pair`, with a `partition` of
  the probe axis.

**What the fixture is for.** It checks that Augur returns a minimum that is not rational, that a closed tolerance is
reported as attained, and that a continuum of hidden parameters is settled by endpoint reasoning with a certificate
and not by sampling gains.

FACT (a recorded pilot, Appendix K; to be re-run before a gate cites it): a solver on the raw three-tick dynamics
excluded 20 mm, and independent interval checks confirmed inclusion at the threshold. Recomputed for this section in
exact rationals: the witness policy at δ = 1/40 and p = 5/8, run on the raw dynamics for 2,049 gains and 65 errors,
ends at rest inside the tolerance in all 133,185 cases; at δ = 1/50 no probe on a grid of 95 values succeeds on all
cases.

| | |
|---|---|
| GATE-AUGUR-32 | Known answer. Through the public verbs: δ = 1/50 is excluded with the alias pair and the partition of the probe axis; δ = 1/40 is included with p = 5/8; the minimum is returned as the root of 16·δ² + 41·δ − 1 with an enclosure no wider than 10⁻⁹ m and `attained: true`. The witness policy passes the 133,185 exact cases on the raw dynamics. A screen compiled for the gain set {1, 2} is refused on the interval [1, 2]. M1. |

### 25.37 Channel laws: the joint error law of repeated reads, and the code that carries a label

**What it is.** [S] Two declarations that a guarantee about information must carry, each with the smallest case in
which omitting it gives a wrong answer. A sensor budget states the joint law of its read errors, not their pairwise
tables. A label count states the channel that carries the label and the length of the message. Owner: `frob-sense` for
the error law, `frob-mission` for the label query, `frob-analyze` for analysis A-17. Verbs: `sense.alias`,
`mission.synthesize`.

**Pairwise independence is not joint independence.** A hidden binary class is read seven times, and each read is right
with probability 3/4.

| Declared law of the errors | Best success, equal priors |
|---|---|
| Jointly independent | 3807/4096, about 0.9294 |
| One fault bit shared by all reads | 3/4 |
| The pairwise-independent law below | 55/64, about 0.8594 |

In each class draw the number K of wrong reads as 1, 2, 3 or 4 with probabilities (43, 3, 9, 9)/64, and place them
uniformly among the seven slots. Each read is wrong with probability E[K]/7 = (112/64)/7 = 1/4. Each pair is wrong
together with probability E[K·(K − 1)]/42 = (168/64)/42 = 1/16, so every pair has the table of two independent reads.
A history with one or two errors relative to one class has six or five relative to the other, which has probability
zero there, and is decoded with certainty. A history with three errors relative to one class has four relative to the
other, and its likelihood is (9/64)/35 under both. The best decoder succeeds with probability 46/64 + ½·(18/64) =
55/64. A requirement of 0.9 is met by the independent law and missed by this one, with the same accuracy and the same
pair tables.

DESIGN. A sensor card states `error_dependence`: `joint-independent`, `shared-fault`, `declared-law` (a finite joint
law by reference), `pairwise` or `unknown`. Analysis A-17 and `sense.alias` credit redundancy, meaning a success
probability above the single-read accuracy, only under `joint-independent`, under a `declared-law` whose best decoder
is found by enumeration (128 histories here), or under a proved lower bound on the histories that decide. Under
`pairwise` or `unknown` the guaranteed value is the single-read accuracy, and a request for more is refused (refusal:
redundancy credited without a joint error law).

**A label is a message.** The label query of §25.18 counts labels. The factory must also deliver the label by the
commitment deadline over a real channel. DESIGN: the query gains `channel`, one of `clean`, `erasures(e)` (up to e
known positions lost) and `flips(t)` (up to t unknown bit errors), for a one-shot binary message of fixed length with
no feedback, and a bit time. For L labels the least length n is the least n that admits a binary code of L words with
minimum distance 1, e + 1 or 2t + 1. The answer returns the label count, the length, a code, and the check n × bit
time ≤ time to commitment. For L ≤ 16 and n ≤ 12 (DESIGN caps) the least length is found by exhaustive search: the
code is the upper-bound witness, and the exhausted search, or a counting argument where one exists, is the lower
bound.

Known answers for the three labels of the one-label-map fixture of §25.18.

| Channel | Least length | Code | Why no shorter |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clean` | 2 bits | 00, 01, 10 | One bit has two words |
| `erasures(1)` | 3 bits | 000, 011, 101 (pairwise distance 2) | Any three words of length 2 include a pair at distance 1 |
| `flips(1)` | 5 bits | 00000, 00111, 11001 (distances 3, 3, 4) | Distance at least 3 for each pair needs the three distances to sum to 9; each bit position adds at most 2 to that sum, since three binary symbols cannot differ pairwise; four bits give at most 8 |

A transmission deadline of four bit times therefore admits guaranteed operation under one erasure and excludes it
under one flip. The checker enumerates the received-word sets under the declared channel and verifies that they are
disjoint.

| | |
|---|---|
| GATE-AUGUR-33 | Known answer. Enumeration of the 128 histories returns 55/64 for the pairwise law, 3807/4096 for the independent law and 3/4 for the shared fault, exactly; a redundancy claim on a card marked `pairwise` is refused. The three label rows return 2, 3 and 5 bits with codes whose received-word sets are disjoint; the four-bit request under `flips(1)` returns an exclusion with the counting argument. On 20 generated instances with L ≤ 8 and e, t ≤ 2 the least length equals brute force. The error-law rows at M3, the label rows at M4. |

### 25.38 Shared nuisance parameters, and the probe for four admitted laws

**What it is.** [F] Two additions to §25.14. The first is a rule: nuisance parameters that two quantities share in the
world stay shared in every bound that compares them. The second is a known answer: once the delayed law D is admitted
to the mechanism set, a probe exists that separates all four laws, at a longer dwell than the three-law probe. Owner:
`frob-mission`. Verbs: `mission.distinguish`, `experiment.suggest`.

**Shared parameters.** In the fixture both pads of one trial have the same residual fraction q and the same time
constant τ. The margin of the compact pad over the broad pad at the handover is m(q, τ) = 60·R(1, T; q, τ) − 50·R(2,
T; q, τ) newtons. Minimizing the two terms separately lets the compact pad take (q, τ) = (0.18, 0.9 s) while the broad
pad takes (0.22, 1.1 s). No such trial exists.

| Law | Least m with q and τ shared | Least m with independent extremes |
|---|---|---|
| V and C | 4.50 N, at (0.18, 0.9 s) | 0.28 N |
| D | 4.72 N, at (0.18, 1.1 s) | −0.078 N |
| P | −13.06 N; the broad pad wins everywhere, by at least 10.02 N | −15.08 N |

The values are derived on file on a 201 × 201 grid of the box. FACT (a recorded pilot, Appendix K; to be re-run): an
enclosure of the D row reported at least 4.07 N shared and −0.0776 N independent. Under D the independent bound
changes sign. It reports that the broad pad might win where the compact pad wins by more than 4.7 N over the whole
box.

DESIGN. Every nuisance parameter of a mission or a measurement contract has a `scope`: the set of quantities that read
one realization (a trial, a pad pair, a batch of material, a unit). Interval and affine evaluation treats a scoped
parameter as one variable across every expression in its scope, by a shared noise symbol or by subdividing the shared
box, never as an independent interval per expression. A parameter with no declared scope is evaluated independently
and the result is marked `scope: undeclared`. That direction is safe for inclusion, since it only widens the
unresolved set. It is not safe for refutation: an extreme point of an independent box is not a world, and it cannot
serve as a counterexample witness (refusal: witness assembled from unshared values of a shared parameter).

**The four-law probe.** With D admitted the decisions are compact for V, C and D and broad for P. On the candidate
grid of §25.14 no probe at a dwell of 1/4 s or less separates P from D, because D follows P until t/τ = 1/4. At 1/2 s
three radii separate them after both read errors of ±0.02 are included.

| Probe | Least reading under P | Greatest reading under V, C, D | Gap after both errors | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| r = 3/2, t = 1/2 s | 0.8206 | 0.7677 | 0.0129 | 0.75 s |
| r = 2, t = 1/2 s | 0.8937 | 0.7874 | 0.0662 | 0.75 s |
| r = 3, t = 1/2 s | 0.9509 | 0.8019 | 0.1090 | 0.75 s |

Each of the three decides all 900 enumerated cases correctly (four laws, 225 cases each). Against the direct
measurement at mission dwell, 1.25 s with the archived compact reading, the modeled time ratio is 1.25/0.75 = 5/3.
DESIGN: among probes of equal cost `mission.distinguish` chooses the largest gap, here r = 3. A tie-break by smallest
radius returns a gap eight times smaller at the same cost.

**What this does not change.** The 225 reversals of the three-law probe on the withheld law stand, and so does the
normative lesson of §25.14. This is a result on a known mechanism set. A fifth law outside it can reverse it again,
and the direct measurement at mission conditions stays in the candidate set.

**Ceiling, stated before any speed test.** 5/3 in modeled exposure time on this fixture, and 1 against a programmed
expert who is given the same four laws.

| | |
|---|---|
| GATE-AUGUR-34 | Known answer. The margin table reproduces to 10⁻³ N, and a refutation built from the independent extremes under law D is refused. With four laws admitted `mission.distinguish` returns a probe at t = 1/2 s with r = 3 and a gap of at least 0.10, decides 900 of 900 cases, and returns no probe at any dwell of 1/4 s or less. M4. |
