# PART VI. SUBSTRATE AND ENGINEERING

## 33. Suite consumption

This chapter fixes what FrankenRobotics takes from its sibling projects, in which form, behind which boundary,
what happens when a sibling does not hold still, and how this program changes a sibling where the sibling is what
has to change (§33.8). Every statement about sibling code below was read on 2026-11-21
at the heads listed in §33.13 and is a FACT with its path. Every statement about how this project behaves is a
DESIGN. A sibling fact goes stale when the sibling moves, so a fact that a gate depends on is re-read by that
gate's admission test and is never copied from this page into a record.

### 33.1 Postures

Five postures, the vocabulary FrankenMining established (FACT: Mining §27):

| Posture | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Consume** | A Cargo dependency at an exact pin, default features off |
| **Subprocess** | A binary or CLI we invoke; no crate in our build graph |
| **Lift** | Copied source with a provenance header, a row in `registries/lifts.toml` and a golden test; re-owned here |
| **Oracle** | Development and test only; never in a production graph |
| **Pattern** | We copy the design, not the code |

Each foundation has an `FD-` row with its posture, its pin, the crates allowed to touch it, an admission gate and
a fallback, because no milestone may be blocked by a sibling that has not converged. A posture belongs to a use,
not to a repository: one sibling may be consumed for one purpose and be an oracle for another, and the ledger
(§33.4) says which. Two refinements follow from the facts in this chapter. A consumed FrankenSim crate may sit
behind a Cargo feature that is off by default, so that its closure is compiled only by the milestone that needs
it (§33.9). And the Subprocess posture is the first fallback for FrankenSim itself (§33.14).

### 33.2 The FrankenSim decision

**ADR-SUITE-01: consume FrankenSim by path dependency, confined behind the airlock crate `frob-fsim`, pinned by
commit in `franken-stack.lock`.**

The owner's brief is to use FrankenSim for the physics to the greatest extent possible. The referee tier needs
`fs-mbd` and `fs-contact` whole, together with geometry, integrators, optimizers and the ledger. Those two crates
are about 438 thousand lines between them with their tests (FACT: 291,848 and 146,603 lines of Rust under
`frankensim/crates/fs-mbd` and `frankensim/crates/fs-contact`). Copying that would be a fork.

What is consumed and what is owned must be stated plainly. FrankenSim is the referee and the source of geometry
kernels, structure-preserving integrators, optimizers, statistics and the design ledger. The batched engine is
FrankenRobotics code: the kernel library, the fixed-step convex compliant solve, the model-variant tables, the GPU
backends and the gym (§16, §17, §21, §23). FrankenSim's `fs-control` crate covers sampled motor current loops
only (FACT: `frankensim/crates/fs-control/Cargo.toml`, description). Four further limits are reported and are
re-read at INT-FSIM-03 before any gate cites them: FrankenSim has no batched environments, `fs-mbd` is plain
`f64` and not generic over a differentiation scalar, it emits no articulated adjoints, and it steps over contact
sets the caller supplies.

The two sibling products chose otherwise, and their reasons are facts this plan must answer. FrankenMining
rejected a Cargo dependency on FrankenSim because it would link two asupersync versions, needs a different
nightly for one crate's const-generic feature, failed `cargo check` on fifteen targets at the time, and uses
out-of-repo relative paths. Its stack lock records the result as `posture = "lift"` (FACT:
`franken_mining/franken-stack.lock`, row `FD-FSIM-00`). FrankenTextiles lifts files one by one. Why the decision
differs here:

1. **The need is different in kind.** Those products took numerics files. This one needs the multibody and
   contact engines.
2. **The mechanism has precedents, and their limit is known.** Five crates sit outside FrankenSim's workspace with
   their own `[workspace]` table and consume `fs-*` crates by path: `apps/instrument-lab/render-gpu`,
   `apps/instrument-lab/render-gpu-piano`, `apps/pocket-watch/engine-watch`, `crates/fs-cmaes-viz-wasm` and
   `crates/fs-flyer-wasm` (FACT: their `Cargo.toml` files). All five live inside FrankenSim's directory tree, so
   they inherit its `.cargo/config.toml`. `crates/fs-g1-train` is also excluded from the workspace, but it
   depends on no `fs-*` crate (FACT: its only dependency is `libm`), so it is not a precedent. One project
   outside the tree consumes four crates by path (FACT:
   `jazz_chord_progression_editor_html/tools/piano-v2-soundboard-pack/Cargo.toml`), and it carries no patch
   entry, no toolchain file and no build-identity setting, so it is not evidence that an out-of-tree build passes
   today. The precedents establish the mechanism. INT-FSIM-01 is the first measurement of the out-of-tree case.
3. **Each objection has a mitigation that is a gate.** The whole build graph, FrankenSim's crates included,
   builds on one toolchain T (INT-TOOLCHAIN-01, §33.13). The workspace root repeats three things that Cargo does
   not propagate from a path dependency: FrankenSim's `[patch.crates-io] asupersync` entry, its FrankenSQLite
   profile overrides, and the build-identity environment its linear-algebra crate requires (hazard 5 below).
   FrankenSim's own manifest states the rule for profiles (FACT: `frankensim/Cargo.toml`, comment above
   `[profile.dev.package.fsqlite]`); that the same holds for patches and for `[env]` in our graph is a
   HYPOTHESIS settled by INT-FSIM-01. A build may contain exactly one asupersync package (INT-ASUP-01), and the
   siblings are aligned on one published version in their own repositories (FD-ASUP-01). Volatile FrankenSim
   types are named in one crate only.
4. **The fallbacks are written down, in order.** First a pinned FrankenSim worker process, then a lift
   (§33.8, §33.14).

Known hazards on the day of writing (FACT, each with its path):

1. **Churn.** 409 commits touched `crates/fs-mbd` in the thirty days to 2026-11-21, on 17 distinct days
   (`git log --since=2026-10-22 -- crates/fs-mbd` in `frankensim`).
2. **An unfrozen composition contract.** `COMPONENT_CONTRACT_VERSION` is 0
   (`frankensim/crates/fs-ports/src/component.rs:52`).
3. **A stale constellation lock.** `frankensim/constellation.lock` pins asupersync 0.5.0 at `7a0f2f55047c`,
   while `frankensim/Cargo.lock` resolves asupersync 0.6.2 by path and the local checkout is 0.6.2 at
   `b32c5ba66315` with 267 modified paths. The lock's pins for franken_numpy, frankenscipy, frankensqlite,
   frankentorch and franken_networkx also differ from the local heads. FrankenSim's verify-only preflight
   treats an off-pin or dirty sibling as a refusal (`frankensim/AGENTS.md`, "Cargo-Independent Constellation
   Preflight"), so by its own rule it would refuse today; the preflight was not run for this chapter. Whether
   each difference is a fast-forward or a divergence is classified at INT-FSIM-01, not assumed.
4. **A nightly feature in the units crate.** `fs-qty` enables `generic_const_exprs`
   (`frankensim/crates/fs-qty/src/lib.rs:20`). §33.12 treats this as a named risk.
5. **A build script that fails closed outside the tree.** `frankensim/crates/fs-la/build.rs` panics unless
   `FRANKENSIM_DEPGRAPH_RECEIPT` or `FRANKENSIM_DEPGRAPH_SALT` is set; inside FrankenSim the salt comes from
   `.cargo/config.toml`, which a workspace outside the tree does not read. `fs-la` is in the closure of `fs-ad`,
   `fs-mbd` and `fs-contact`. The core workspace therefore sets its own salt, naming its own development
   equivalence class, in its root `.cargo/config.toml`, and evidence-bearing performance builds export a
   receipt (§33.5).
6. **A large closure.** A path dependency on `fs-mbd` compiles 42 other FrankenSim crates and about 1.57 million
   lines of library source, because `fs-contact` depends on `fs-material` (633 thousand lines), `fs-thermal`,
   `fs-thermochem` and `fs-feec` (computed from the `Cargo.toml` files under `frankensim/crates`). The crate set
   M1 needs compiles 65 crates and about 2.06 million lines. FrankenSim's lockfile holds 479 packages, of which
   262 come from the registry (`frankensim/Cargo.lock`). INT-FSIM-01 records cold and warm build times and peak
   memory, and the lift fallback is priced against these numbers, not against the size of two crates.
7. **A contact capacity.** The sustained contact solver admits at most 21 contacts
   (`frankensim/crates/fs-contact/src/sustained/solve.rs:26`), and its articulated step keeps fixed material
   witnesses (§33.11, row 4).
8. **Dirty trees.** FrankenSim's own checkout has 32 modified paths at head `483d09c682f2`. A pin names a
   commit; the resolution receipt (§33.5) hashes bytes when a tree is dirty.

A pinned commit, the airlock and the receipt are what make those survivable. Hazards 2, 3, 4, 5 and 7 are also
upstream work items that this program does in FrankenSim's repository, under its rules (FD-FSIM-08; FD-FSIM-16
with FD-ASUP-01; FD-FSIM-15 and FD-FSIM-31; FD-FSIM-14; FD-FSIM-13; §33.8, Appendix F). Each keeps the interim
posture stated in this chapter until its change lands. Hazard 1 is why the airlock stays whatever lands.

### 33.3 The airlock

`frob-fsim` is the only crate that may name types from FrankenSim's volatile crates. It exposes
FrankenRobotics-native traits and adapts them. A FrankenSim API change then costs one crate.

DESIGN (trait names fix intent, not signatures). The traits are grouped, and each group is a Cargo feature of
`frob-fsim`, so that a crate above the airlock compiles only the closure it uses:

| Feature group | Traits exposed | FrankenSim crates behind it | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `referee` | `RefereeDynamics`, `RefereeContact`, `Integrator`, `PortSystem` | `fs-mbd`, `fs-mbd-material`, `fs-contact`, `fs-tribo`, `fs-time`, `fs-motion`, `fs-ports`, `fs-system` | on |
| `geometry` | `GeometryKernel`, `SceneQuery`, `MeshExchange` | `fs-query`, `fs-geom`, `fs-rep-sdf`, `fs-rep-mesh`, `fs-rep-frep`, `fs-scene`, `fs-topo`, `fs-io` | on |
| `ledger` | `Ledger`, `Session`, `Recompute` | `fs-ledger`, `fs-session`, `fs-package`, `fs-recompute` | on |
| `optimize` | `Optimizer`, `Archive`, `Racing` | `fs-dfo`, `fs-bo`, `fs-ascent`, `fs-archive`, `fs-opt`, `fs-sos`, `fs-race`, `fs-eproc`, `fs-tropical`, `fs-symmetry` | off |
| `stats` | `Uncertainty`, `ValueOfInformation`, `Surrogate`, `Assimilation` | `fs-uq`, `fs-voi`, `fs-surrogate`, `fs-assimilate`, `fs-robust`, `fs-regime` | off |
| `spectral` | `Spectral` | `fs-spectral` | off |
| `actuation` | `Magnetics`, `ThermalNetwork`, `CurrentLoop`, `PortHamiltonian` | `fs-em`, `fs-thermal`, `fs-control`, `fs-phs`, `fs-matdb` | off |
| `structure` | `StructuralOpt`, `ToleranceAllocation`, `AsBuilt`, `FabricationRules` | `fs-solid`, `fs-topopt`, `fs-topols`, `fs-toleralloc`, `fs-asbuilt`, `fs-geocon`, `fs-fab`, `fs-adjoint` | off |
| `multiphysics` | `FluidIsland`, `CoupledIsland` | `fs-lbm`, `fs-couple` | off; gated bridge (§33.9) |
| `harness` | none (test support) | `fs-roofline`, `fs-detaudit`, `fs-propcheck`, `fs-render` | dev only |

What a group costs to compile beyond the M1 set (`referee`, `geometry`, `ledger`, 65 crates and about 2.06
million lines of library source) is FACT, computed from the manifests on 2026-11-21: `spectral` adds nothing,
because `fs-spectral` is already in that closure; `optimize` adds 12 crates and about 84 thousand lines; `stats`
10 crates and about 113 thousand; `actuation` 2 crates and about 151 thousand; `structure` 13 crates and about
412 thousand; `multiphysics` 19 crates and about 2.31 million. The groups therefore serve two purposes of unequal
weight. They bound what a crate above the airlock may name, always. They save compile time only for the last
two.

A short **bedrock-direct** list may be used anywhere, because the types of those crates are the vocabulary of the
mathematics. Sizes are FACT, counted on 2026-11-21 as lines of Rust under each crate's `src` and under the whole
crate directory:

| Crate | Library lines | With tests | Depends on `fs-qty` | Leaves FrankenSim | What it provides |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fs-ga` | 4,078 | 4,883 | no | no | Motors, screws and meets in PGA; Lie façades in `src/lie.rs` |
| `fs-math` | 5,063 | 7,633 | no | no | Deterministic elementary functions with error budgets in units in the last place |
| `fs-qty` | 8,950 | 9,947 | it is `fs-qty` | no | Compile-time dimensional analysis; runtime-checked quantities; SI parsing |
| `fs-rand` | 7,356 | 12,053 | no | no | Counter-based Philox streams keyed by logical identity; Sobol and Owen sequences |
| `fs-blake3` | 7,304 | 13,757 | no | no | BLAKE3 in safe Rust; the 32-byte content hash |
| `fs-ivl` | 5,956 | 11,295 | yes, through `fs-evidence` | no | Outward-rounded intervals, affine forms, Taylor models, exact predicates |
| `fs-simd` | 3,331 | 4,242 | no | no | SIMD tiers behind safe façades |
| `fs-exec` | 33,870 | 38,543 | no | asupersync, by path | Two-lane executor and the `Cx` contract |
| `fs-evidence` | 37,120 | 57,107 | yes, directly | no | `Evidence<T>` and `Certified<T>` with conservative composition |
| `fs-ad` | 2,917 | 4,062 | no | asupersync through `fs-la`; FrankenTorch crates if a feature is on | Forward-mode duals and the `Real` scalar contract |

Eight of the ten are under nine thousand lines. `fs-exec` and `fs-evidence` are larger and are admitted direct
because `Cx` and `Evidence<T>` appear in signatures throughout. The closure of the list is 16 crates and about
161 thousand lines of library source (FACT, same count). Everything else goes through the airlock.

Three rules bind the adapter. It converts, and never reinterprets: a FrankenSim refusal becomes a typed referee
refusal carrying the upstream reason, and is never retried with weakened inputs. It does not cache across pins:
every memoized referee result carries the stack-lock digest in its key. And it exposes capacities as data: the
21-contact limit of hazard 7 is a field of `RefereeContact`, checked when a model is compiled and again at run
time, so that an over-capacity contact set is a refusal by name and is never silently truncated (the contact set
of a tracked robot overflows where a point-foot robot's does not, and dropping contacts would bias exactly the
comparison the studio exists to make).

### 33.4 Foundation ledger

| FD | Foundation | Posture | Used for | Confined to | Admission | Fallback |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FD-FSIM | frankensim | Consume by path | Bedrock-direct crates (§33.3). Through the airlock: the feature groups of §33.3, extended in §33.9 | `frob-fsim`, plus the bedrock-direct list | INT-FSIM-01 to INT-FSIM-18 | KILL-FSIM: a worker process, then a lift |
| FD-ASUP | asupersync | Consume | Structured concurrency, cancellation, `Cx`; the lab runtime for deterministic simulation testing (§33.15) | All async code; one package identity per build, on the one published version FD-ASUP-01 aligns the siblings on | INT-ASUP-01, INT-ASUP-02 | A surface that still brings a second package moves to its own workspace (for `frob-mcp`, KILL-MCP fallback 1) |

Honest notes on four of these:

- **franken_numpy** is an `f64` array library on heap vectors with no single-precision storage and no fixed-size
  matrix types, and it lists GPU arrays and automatic differentiation as out of scope (FACT). It is the right
  tool at the interchange boundary and as an oracle. It is not put in a hot path where it does not fit. Its
  stride convention differs from FrankenTorch's (§33.11, row 3).
- **frankensympy**'s workspace refers to two sibling pin directories, `../franken_numpy-pin` and
  `../frankenscipy-pin`, that do not exist on this machine, and it pins a different nightly from the rest of the
  suite (FACT: `frankensympy/Cargo.toml:95–96`, `frankensympy/rust-toolchain.toml`). `derive/` therefore depends
  on individual `fsym-*` crates by path. The different nightly is the starting state: `derive/` builds on T and
  has no toolchain file of its own, and frankensympy is moved to T by the toolchain train (§33.13).
- **frankentorch** tensors live on the host. `Device::Metal` and `Device::Cuda` are tags, and `ft-nn` and
  `ft-autograd` run on the CPU (FACT as reported from a source reading; re-read at INT-FT-02). A device tag earns
  no GPU operator coverage. On-device learning kernels are written here, in the shared dialect (§21, §23).
- **franken_threed** does not yet package a single self-contained page (FACT: `franken_threed/README.md`, "Honest
  status"). The viewer's self-contained HTML export is this project's own build step.

### 33.5 The stack lock

`franken-stack.lock` is TOML in FrankenMining's format (FACT: `franken_mining/franken-stack.lock`). One row per
foundation, checked by `xtask check-stack`:

```toml
toolchain = "<T, chosen at INT-TOOLCHAIN-01; moved only by a toolchain train (§33.13)>"

[[foundation]]
id = "FD-FSIM"
name = "frankensim"
posture = "consume-path"
path = "../frankensim"
git_rev = "<40-hex commit recorded at INT-FSIM-01>"
toolchain = "<the channel in the sibling's own toolchain file at git_rev; equal to T after the train>"
features = ["referee", "geometry", "ledger"]            # airlock groups compiled by default
build_env = { FRANKENSIM_DEPGRAPH_SALT = "franken-robotics-dev-v1" }
confined_to = ["frob-fsim", "bedrock-direct"]
admission_gate = "INT-FSIM-01"
receipt = "<BLAKE3 of the resolution receipt this row was admitted under>"
fallback = "KILL-FSIM: (a) pinned worker process exchanging whole jobs; (b) lift the minimal referee set."

[[foundation]]
id = "FD-ASUP"
name = "asupersync"
posture = "consume"
version = "<the single version every workspace resolves>"
admission_gate = "INT-ASUP-01"
fallback = "FD-ASUP-01 aligns the siblings; a surface that still brings a second package: KILL-MCP fallback 1."
```

**The resolution receipt.** A pin is a statement of intent. What was built is a different fact, and the two have
already diverged inside the suite (hazards 3 and 8 of §33.2). `xtask check-stack` therefore writes one receipt
per admission and per pin move. DESIGN, schema `frob.stack-receipt/1`, canonical JSON:

```json
{
  "schema": "frob.stack-receipt/1",
  "repo_rev": "<this repository's commit>",
  "toolchain": "<T>",
  "siblings": [
    {"fd": "FD-FSIM", "rev": "<40 hex>", "dirty": false, "tree_hash": null,
     "features": ["referee", "geometry", "ledger"],
     "own_lock": {"file": "constellation.lock", "hash": "<BLAKE3>", "agrees": false,
                  "class": "stale-lock | drift | on-pin"}},
    {"fd": "FD-ASUP", "rev": "<40 hex>", "dirty": true, "tree_hash": "<BLAKE3 of tracked bytes>"}
  ],
  "lockfiles": [{"workspace": "core", "hash": "<BLAKE3 of Cargo.lock>", "packages": 0, "registry": 0}],
  "patches": ["asupersync -> ../asupersync"],
  "profile_overrides": ["fsqlite*: opt-level 1"],
  "build_env": {"FRANKENSIM_DEPGRAPH_SALT": "franken-robotics-dev-v1"},
  "duplicates": [],
  "commands": [{"argv": ["cargo", "tree", "-d"], "exit": 0, "output_hash": "<BLAKE3>"}]
}
```

Rules for the receipt:

- It captures source trees, requested features, compiler channels, lockfiles and the constraints of direct and
  transitive siblings in one file. A sibling's own lock (`constellation.lock`, `SUITE.lock`) is hashed and
  compared, and a disagreement is classified the way FrankenSim classifies it: on-pin, stale-lock (the checkout
  is a fast-forward of the lock), or drift (dirty, retreated or diverged).
- When a tree is dirty the receipt hashes the tracked bytes. A dirty sibling admits development builds only; no
  gate records a PASS on a dirty tree.
- Identities are independent of machine paths. The receipt stores repository-relative paths and revisions, never
  `/Users/...`.
- Every admission record (§33.6) cites a receipt hash. A result in the Chronicle ledger carries the receipt hash
  of the binary that produced it, which is what lets a later reader decide whether two results may be compared
  as results of the same stack.
- `xtask check-stack` fails if the tracked lockfiles, the toolchain files or the sibling heads disagree with the
  newest receipt. It never moves a sibling checkout. Receipts are kept under `receipts/`, named by their hash.

Known answer: a receipt computed twice on an unchanged tree is byte-identical. Negative control: touching one
tracked file in a sibling flips `dirty` and changes `tree_hash`, and `check-stack` fails.

An admission record is valid only if it cites a commit of this repo whose tracked `Cargo.lock` contains the
foundation, with the command, its output and the receipt hash (the rule FrankenMining adopted after finding
admission records for crates that were not in the build, FACT). Records live in `DEPENDENCY_ADMISSION.md`, a
convention taken from FrankenThreeD (FACT: `franken_threed/DEPENDENCY_ADMISSION.md`). Thresholds below are
TARGETs until the gate records measured values.

| INT-TOOLCHAIN-01 | The one toolchain T is chosen and recorded in `franken-stack.lock` and `rust-toolchain.toml`, in the order of preference of §33.13: (a) the suite's common nightly, (b) FrankenSim's present pin. The whole build graph (the core, the GPU annexes, `derive/frob-derive` and `surface/frob-mcp`) builds and tests on T. ### 33.8 Upstream work and drift

Every sibling this plan consumes is the owner's project (FACT, stated by the owner on 2026-11-22). DESIGN: a
limitation, defect or mismatch in a sibling is therefore work this program does, in the sibling's repository,
under that repository's own `AGENTS.md`, gates and conventions. Each such change is an **upstream work item**
(Appendix F): a bead in this program's graph with the label `upstream`, mirrored as a bead in the sibling's
tracker, with a priority, an interim posture here, and a switch-over rule. The interim posture and the
switch-over rule exist so that no milestone waits on a sibling change landing. Upstream changes are additive: a
new mode, type or feature, never a change to existing behaviour, with any lossiness self-described (the rule the
Wright Flyer plan sets for its upstream extensions, FACT). Each upstream work item carries one reproducible
failing fixture and a description of the needed argument or result.

The sibling's rules bind the work. For FrankenSim they include its layer checks, its contracts, its
unsafe-capsule discipline, its ban on in-process foreign kernels in production paths, which is why the GPU
annexes stay in this repository, and its ban on branches and worktrees (FACT: `frankensim/AGENTS.md`,
`frankensim/docs/ACCELERATOR_DOCTRINE.md`; §21.2, §34.4, §34.7). Other agents work in the same sibling
repositories. Before an upstream change edits a file it reserves that file through Agent Mail and follows the
sibling's own coordination rules, and it lands on the sibling's `main` through the sibling's own gates.

Pins advance through a compatibility train: move the pin, write a new receipt, rerun the admission and parity
gates, relock. A sibling's newer clean head is never rolled back locally. The airlock crate `frob-fsim` stays,
because FrankenSim's API still moves daily (hazard 1 of §33.2). The fallbacks stay written down (KILL-FSIM,
KILL-MCP and the others); they are fallbacks, and no default wiring rests on one.

The order matters because of hazard 6. The lift set is small only on paper: the two modules it names sit on a
closure of about 1.5 million lines, and cutting them free of `fs-material` is engineering that fallback (a)
avoids entirely. A worker keeps FrankenSim's real code as the referee at an old pin for as long as needed.

Group gates. Each is the form of INT-FSIM-01 applied to one group at the milestone that first uses it: the group
compiles from this repo behind its feature, one known answer passes through the airlock trait, and one negative
control fails. Thresholds are TARGETs.

| Gate | Group | Known answer through the airlock | Negative control |
|---|---|---|---|

| INT-FSIM-15 | `structure` | A tolerance allocation on a two-term stack reproduces the hand-computed variance split; a mesh written through `fs-io` reads back with the same hash | A STEP file above the stated bound is quarantined with a receipt, not parsed |
| INT-FSIM-16 | `ledger` (`fs-recompute`) | Incremental recomputation equals full recomputation on 10⁴ random edit sequences | An input missing from a key is caught by the shadow recompute within 64 hits |
| INT-FSIM-17 | `multiphysics` | Poiseuille flow between plates matches the parabola to the crate's own stated tolerance; total film mass is conserved to 10⁻¹² relative over 10⁴ steps | The bridge refuses when the feature is off, and refuses a throughput-tier request |

**The gated bridge.** `fs-lbm` and `fs-couple` are two of the largest crates in FrankenSim, and their closure is
66 crates and about 4.1 million lines of library source, of which 19 crates and about 2.3 million lines lie
outside what M1 compiles (FACT). They are reached only through the `multiphysics` feature of `frob-fsim`, which
is off in every default build, is compiled only by the M6 lanes, and exposes two traits that exchange whole
fields at declared instants. No kernel of the batched step calls across the bridge. A result that crossed it is
labelled as evaluation tier and cannot enter a throughput claim. If INT-FSIM-17 fails, the fluid film stays the
Solid film-friction law of §18 and coupled islands are dropped (the kill gate and its fallback are stated in §19
and §16 with the mechanisms themselves).

### 33.11 Reported foundation defects

Five defects or limits were reported in components this plan stands on: the three errors in the suite's PPO update
(row 1), the joint law of its action sampler (row 6, in §33.17), the planar-drive integration defect (row 2), the
stride-convention trap (row 3) and the fixed-witness assumption of the sustained contact step (row 4). The
mixed-frame `fs-mbd::Wrench` (row 5, in §33.17) is a convention hazard beside them, not a defect. Each is recorded as
a fact to recheck: what was reported, what a reading of the source on 2026-11-21 does and does not confirm, the
admission
test that settles it, the upstream work item, and what this project does meanwhile. None was re-executed for this
chapter. A reported number stays a report until its admission test records it.

| # | Component | Reported | Read in source on 2026-11-21 | Admission test | Upstream work item | Interim posture |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `fs_g1_train::ppo_update` (`frankensim/crates/fs-g1-train/src/ppo.rs:253–345`) | Three errors: the clip branch is reversed for negative advantage; the critic gradient ignores the current output; two reset episodes concatenated are forwarded as one sequence | First two confirmed by reading (lines 322–326 and 340); the third is consistent with line 309 and its number was not re-run | INT-FSIM-06 | FD-FSIM-10 | Not linked, not an oracle, not a baseline |
| 2 | `fs-mbd::planar_drive` (`frankensim/crates/fs-mbd/src/planar_drive.rs:117–133`) | Near-straight motion at a large heading returns zero translation | Mechanism confirmed by reading and by the rounding arithmetic below; the run was not repeated | INT-FSIM-05 | FD-FSIM-11 | Independent formula in `frob-conformance` |
| 3 | Strides in `fnp-ndarray` and `ft-core` | Signed byte strides on one side, unsigned element strides on the other; a verbatim copy reads the wrong element in bounds | Both conventions confirmed (`fnp-ndarray/src/lib.rs:258, :390`; `ft-core/src/lib.rs:397, :2460`); the wrong read was not executed | INT-FNP-02 | FD-FNP-01 | A typed converter; no bare stride tuple crosses the boundary |
| 4 | Sustained contact step (`frankensim/crates/fs-mbd/src/articulated_contacts/step/sustained.rs`) | Fixed material witnesses and a fixed contact frame; a wheel rolling over a sharp lip changes both | Confirmed as a documented scope limit with typed refusals (module header, lines 1–10 and 333–339); capacity 21 at `fs-contact/src/sustained/solve.rs:26` | INT-FSIM-07 | FD-FSIM-12, FD-FSIM-13 | Witness migration in the referee's transactional step (§16); over-capacity refuses |

**Row 1, the hand cases.** The clipped surrogate is min(ρ·Â, clip(ρ, 1 − ε, 1 + ε)·Â), and the unclipped branch
carries the gradient exactly when ρ·Â ≤ clip(ρ)·Â, for either sign of Â. The source tests the opposite
inequality when Â < 0. Take Â = −1 and ε = 0.2. At ρ = 0.5 the two terms are −0.5 and −0.8, the minimum is the
clipped term and the gradient is zero, but the code lets it flow. At ρ = 2 the terms are −2 and −1.2, the
minimum is the unclipped term, but the code clips. The reported finite differences of the loss in the log
standard deviation at ratios 0.5, 1 and 2 are 0, −0.5 and −1 against the code's −0.25, −0.5 and 0. For the
critic, the gradient is formed from the value stored during the rollout, and the value returned by the training
forward pass is discarded; the reported case is a critic output of 2 with stored value and return 0, where the
code's gradient into the critic bias is 0 and the squared-error objective gives 2. For sequences, the reported
case is two independently reset one-step episodes whose concatenation gives a frozen policy a second likelihood
ratio of 1.582459 where 1 is correct. INT-FSIM-06 has three probes: the four combinations of advantage sign and
clip side, each against a finite difference of the scalar loss to 10⁻³ relative in single precision; the critic
gradient against the current forward output; and a packed sequence against separate episode replays, ratio 1 to
10⁻⁶. The same three probes are the first tests of this project's own PPO (§23), because a defect this easy to
write is easy to write twice.

**Row 2, the arithmetic.** The step takes its straight branch only when |ω| ≤ 10⁻¹² rad/s. Otherwise it forms
θ′ = θ + ω·Δt and returns R·(sin θ′ − sin θ) and −R·(cos θ′ − cos θ). Take θ = 32 rad, wheel speeds 1 and
1 + 6·10⁻¹³ m/s, track 0.5 m and Δt = 1/400 s. Then ω = 1.2·10⁻¹² rad/s, just above the threshold, and
ω·Δt = 3·10⁻¹⁵ rad. Half the spacing of doubles at 32 is 2⁻⁴⁸ ≈ 3.55·10⁻¹⁵, so θ′ rounds to θ and both
differences are exactly zero. Both wheels advance and the chassis does not move. Over 400 steps the true
displacement is one metre along the heading, about (0.83422336, 0.55142668) m. The independent formula is
Δp = v·Δt·sinc(δ/2)·(cos(θ + δ/2), sin(θ + δ/2)) with δ = ω·Δt, sinc(x) = sin(x)/x and sinc(0) = 1. Its
hand-checkable case: unit speed through a half turn from θ = 0 gives the chord (0, 2/π) m. INT-FSIM-05 tests
exact straight travel, the near-zero-curvature case above, wrapped against unwrapped headings, and incremental
against one-shot integration to 10⁻¹².

**Row 3, the hand case.** A contiguous 2×2 single-precision view has strides (8, 4) in bytes and (2, 1) in
elements. Copying (8, 4) into an element-stride view over a 16-element buffer addresses element 8 + 4 = 12 at
index [1, 1], where element 3 belongs. Both reads are in bounds, so nothing faults. A view with byte origin 4
and strides (8, −4) addresses elements (1, 0, 3, 2), which unsigned strides cannot express. The converter at the
export boundary carries the logical origin, the allocation extent, the stride unit and the signedness. A view
that the target cannot represent is materialized and the copy is charged to the caller, or refused under a
zero-copy contract. A writable view is also checked for independence, separately from bounds: a 2×2 view with element strides (1, 1) maps index [0, 1] and index [1, 0] to one element, so stores of 7 and 11 leave a result that depends on their order. Shared elements are admitted for reads; a write needs an injective index map, a declared reduction or separate storage, and is refused otherwise. Neither library is wrong by itself; the trap is at our boundary.

**Row 4, the consequence.** The limit is declared upstream and enforced by refusal, which is the behaviour this
plan wants from a referee. It still decides what M1 can claim: referee rollouts over planes and primitive
obstacles are admitted, and a wheel climbing a riser is admitted only through the event-located transactional
step, which localizes new witness pairs at a consistent world contact point and transports or resets tangential
memory. INT-FSIM-07 passes when the flat-to-edge-to-top transition returns the typed refusal through the airlock
at the pin, and the same transition completes under witness migration with the energy ledger closed to its
stated residual.

### 33.12 The `fs-qty` coupling and the `frob-units` escape hatch

**The risk, named.** Rule L-6 (§34.3) puts `fs-qty` types in every public signature above layer 1. `fs-qty` is
the one crate in FrankenSim that enables a nightly feature, `generic_const_exprs`, which the compiler marks
incomplete (FACT: `frankensim/crates/fs-qty/src/lib.rs:20–21`; a search of `crates`, `apps` and `xtask` finds no
other crate-level feature attribute). `fs-evidence` depends on `fs-qty` directly, and through `fs-evidence` so
do `fs-ivl` and nearly every physics crate (§33.3, §33.9). The whole build graph is therefore tied to nightlies
on which an incomplete feature still compiles one crate. The structure of the coupling matters for the upstream
change (FACT to recheck, a reported reading of the dependency graph that this chapter did not repeat;
INT-TOOLCHAIN-01 records it): of 22 crates coupled to `fs-qty`, 12 depend on it directly and 10 only through
another crate, and removing `fs-qty` from `fs-evidence` alone would free 8 of the 22. That is a smaller change
than FD-FSIM-15 and is listed beside it (Appendix F, FD-FSIM-31). The coupling can bite in three ways:

1. A toolchain train moves T to a nightly where the feature has regressed. Candidate (a) of §33.13 is such a
   move for FrankenSim, from `nightly-2026-07-06` to `nightly-2026-08-31`.
2. A crate in the graph needs a newer compiler than a nightly on which `fs-qty` compiles. The starting state has
   this shape: fastmcp_rust declares a minimum of 1.100, and FrankenSim's pin is a 1.99.0 nightly (§33.13). The
   choice of T and FD-FMCP-01 remove it.
3. A stable-only target appears. Firmware export [M] would be one; franken_firmware is on stable 1.99.0.

**The test.** INT-TOOLCHAIN-01 records a matrix, not one result. The first and last columns are the two
candidates for T (§33.13); the middle columns are the present pins of frankensympy and fastmcp_rust, recorded as
the starting state:

| Build set | `nightly-2026-07-06`, candidate (b) | `nightly-2026-08-20` | `nightly-2026-08-25` | `nightly-2026-08-31`, candidate (a) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fs-qty` alone | recorded | recorded | recorded | recorded |
| Bedrock-direct list | recorded | recorded | recorded | recorded |
| M1 closure (`referee`, `geometry`, `ledger`) | recorded | — | recorded | recorded |
| Core with the Metal annex (`ft-kernel-metal`) | recorded | — | — | recorded |
| `surface/frob-mcp` with fastmcp_rust | recorded | — | recorded | recorded |
| `derive/frob-derive` with the `fsym-*` crates | recorded | recorded | — | recorded |

Every row must pass on the column chosen as T.

**The decision rule.** T is the first candidate, in the order (a) then (b), on which every row passes, with the
upstream changes that candidate needs (§33.13). If `fs-qty` compiles on it, nothing else changes. If `fs-qty` is
what fails on candidate (a), the preferred fix is an upstream change in FrankenSim (FD-FSIM-15 or FD-FSIM-31),
and T is candidate (b) until that change lands and the train to (a) runs. If `fs-qty` fails on T after a later
toolchain train and the upstream change cannot land within that train, `frob-units` is created.

**The escape hatch, kept cheap from the first commit.** DESIGN: the core never imports `fs_qty` by name outside
`frob-core` and `frob-fsim`. Quantity types reach every other crate through one re-export module,
`frob_core::qty`. While the hatch is closed that module re-exports `fs-qty`. If it opens, the module re-exports
`frob-units` instead, and the change is one module plus the conversions in the airlock.

`frob-units` [S], if it exists: layer 0, standard library only, compiles on stable. A dimension is a vector of
six signed 8-bit exponents in the order metre, kilogram, second, kelvin, ampere, mole, which is `fs-qty`'s order
(FACT: `fs-qty/src/lib.rs`, `DIMENSION_COUNT = 6`). Typed quantities are a closed set of aliases; products and
quotients among them are generated by a declarative macro, the fallback `fs-qty` documents for itself. Data
loaded at run time uses a checked quantity that carries its dimension as a value. Conversions to and from
`fs-qty` live in `frob-fsim` only, so rule L-2 still holds. Cap: 3 thousand lines.

- Known answers: every alias product agrees with `fs-qty` in a differential test while both exist; a pressure
  cannot be added to a time (a compile-fail test); a round trip through the airlock conversion preserves the
  value bits.
- Counterexample to the shortcut "a dimension vector is all the typing a quantity needs": a torque and an
  energy have the same vector (1 in kilogram, 2 in metre, −2 in second), so dimension checking alone cannot
  separate them. Both crates therefore keep them as distinct aliases over the same dimension, and the test adds
  a torque to an energy and expects a compile error.
- Gate: the alias set stays at or below 64 (TARGET); above that the macro's product table is no longer
  reviewable and the question returns to the owner as OPEN-SUITE-4.
- Cost, stated: `frob-units` loses `fs-qty`'s open-ended dimension arithmetic. A quantity outside the alias set
  must be added to it or carried as a checked runtime value.

Four nightlies and one stable release are in play. That table is the starting state, which the toolchain train,
FD-FMCP-01 and FD-ASUP-01 change. Three consequences are DESIGN:

1. **One toolchain, T, for the whole build graph.** T is recorded in `franken-stack.lock` and in
   `rust-toolchain.toml`. Every crate that any `frob` binary links builds on T: the core, the GPU annexes, the
   derivation tool and the MCP server. No annex carries a toolchain file of its own; `lean/` is not Rust and
   keeps its own toolchain, and `frob-cert` builds on T in the graph and also alone on a stable release
   (§34.11). T is chosen at INT-TOOLCHAIN-01 and after that is moved only by a **toolchain train**: one
   coordinated change that moves T in this repository and in every consumed sibling that needs it, followed by
   the admission and parity gates. The candidates, in order of preference:
   - (a) The suite's common nightly, the one most siblings already pin: `nightly-2026-08-31` on the day of
     writing (asupersync, frankentorch, franken_numpy, franken_lean, franken_threed and others in the table
     above). It requires advancing FrankenSim's pin from `nightly-2026-07-06` in FrankenSim's repository, and
     moving frankensympy from `nightly-2026-08-20` and fastmcp_rust from `nightly-2026-08-25`.
   - (b) FrankenSim's present pin, if FrankenSim cannot yet build on (a). fastmcp_rust's declared `rust-version`
     and toolchain file are then changed so that it builds on that pin, and the train to (a) is scheduled.
2. **fastmcp_rust is upgraded to match T, and `frob-mcp` is in the core graph.** As found, fastmcp_rust
   declares a minimum of 1.100 and FrankenSim's pin is a 1.99.0 nightly; Cargo refuses such a build unless told
   to ignore the declared minimum, and this plan does not build on an ignored constraint. The mismatch is fixed
   in fastmcp_rust. Under either candidate, upstream work item FD-FMCP-01 (P0, at M0) is done by this program in
   fastmcp_rust's repository, and it is complete when fastmcp_rust's own test suite and its MCP conformance
   checks pass on T. `frob-mcp` is then an ordinary member of the core workspace: it links `frob-verbs`, runs
   verb implementations in process, and shares the one toolchain and the one asupersync package with the rest of
   the graph (§32.12.2). INT-FMCP-01 is the gate. KILL-MCP names the fallbacks, and fires only if INT-FMCP-01
   cannot pass within the M0 budget after FD-FMCP-01 and FD-ASUP-01 have been attempted.
3. **One asupersync version, and 0.5.0 never enters a graph.** FrankenSim's constellation, FrankenTorch and
   fastmcp_rust are aligned on one published asupersync version by changes in those repositories (FD-ASUP-01,
   P0, at M0); INT-ASUP-01 is the gate that proves it. frankentui's executor feature is forbidden, and
   frankenjax and franken_threed are never Cargo dependencies. `xtask check-deps` enforces all three.

### 33.14 The worker-process fallback

**ADR-SUITE-02: before any FrankenSim source is lifted, the referee moves behind a process boundary.** [S]

What it is. `frob-fsim` has two build modes behind the same traits. In mode `inproc` (the default) the adapters
call FrankenSim through path dependencies. In mode `remote` every volatile `fs-*` dependency is compiled out and
the adapters speak a job protocol to a worker. The worker is the binary target `frob-fsim-worker` of the same
crate, built in mode `inproc` from the small workspace `worker/` on FrankenSim's toolchain at the pinned commit.
No new crate is created, and `frob-fsim` remains the only code that names volatile types. One worker runs per
device or per process slot; the daemon starts, supervises and stops it.

The protocol exchanges whole jobs and bounded chunks. It never carries a per-link, per-ray or per-tick call: the
solver and its working set stay together on one side.

```
job    = { job_hash, stack_receipt, model (compiled referee model, canonical bytes), scene, initial_states,
           control (a schedule, or a controller program the worker evaluates), horizon, cadence, seeds,
           outputs (state columns, events, digests, energy-ledger rows) }
chunk  = { job_hash, index, first_step, last_step, columns, events, digest, final: bool }
refuse = { job_hash, code, upstream_reason }
```

- A job is identified by the BLAKE3 hash of its canonical bytes, and submission is idempotent on that hash.
- Chunks follow a fixed logical partition of the horizon, so a restarted worker regenerates the same chunk
  boundaries and the client resumes from the last contiguous chunk whose digest it holds.
- The worker reports the stack receipt it was built under. A mismatch with the job's receipt is a refusal
  (`FROB-REF-791`), not a warning.
- Transport is a local socket or a pipe, framed by length, with integers above 2⁵³ as strings where JSON is used
  and binary columns elsewhere.

What the fallback preserves: the referee is FrankenSim's own code; teleport from a device tier to the referee
(a job whose initial state is a snapshot); shadow sampling; promotion. What it costs: a fixed overhead per job,
so the referee is called in rollouts and never inside a loop; and a second build to keep, though only at pin
moves. What it does not solve: an API change still costs the adapter, but the worker can stay on an old pin while
the core moves.

INT-FSIM-18 runs at M0 even though the fallback is not active, because a fallback that has never run is a hope.
Pass criteria (TARGET): a 2,000-step G1 referee rollout submitted through the worker returns chunk digests equal,
bit for bit, to the same job run in process; killing the worker mid-job and resubmitting returns the same
digests; fixed overhead is at most 50 ms per job and at most 5% of wall time on jobs of one second or more.
Negative control: a worker built at a different commit refuses the job.

The trigger for fallback (b) is numeric too (DESIGN). If shadowing through the worker falls below 0.1% of device
world-seconds at the M2 batch size, which is the bottom of the range §36 gives for a CPU referee, the worker
cannot do the referee's job and the lift is considered.

### 33.15 What the other siblings contribute

Each entry was checked in code, and each has a posture, an admission gate and a fallback. Gate thresholds are
TARGETs.

**asupersync's lab runtime: deterministic simulation testing of the daemon** [S]. FACT: `asupersync/src/lab/` is
about 127 thousand lines; its module header lists virtual time, deterministic scheduling by seed, trace capture
and replay, schedule exploration, test oracles, cancellation injection at await points and chaos injection
(`src/lab/mod.rs`). It is compiled under the `full-runtime` feature and re-exports `LabConfig` and `LabRuntime`
(`src/lib.rs:237, :502`). `chaos.rs` (918 lines), `ldfi.rs` (567), `replay_minimization.rs` (991),
`dual_run.rs` and `snapshot_restore.rs` exist. Use: every test of `frobd`'s job protocol and of the Chronicle
writer runs under `LabRuntime` with a recorded seed. Faults are injected by schedule: a kill inside a chunk
write, a cancel at each await point, completions out of order, a storage error. A failing schedule is minimized
and stored as a replay fixture. Device work is represented by a stub whose timing the lab clock controls, and a
dual-run scenario compares the stub against a real device on a small job. Posture: Consume, as a
dev-dependency of `frob-chronicle`, `frob-verbs` and `frob-conformance`; it is the same single asupersync
package. Gate: INT-ASUP-02. Fallback: the chaos tests at kernel-batch boundaries of §38 with a hand-written
virtual clock, which keep fault injection and lose schedule exploration. One caution: `lab/conformal.rs` (906
lines) calibrates the lab's own oracle metrics and is not a general interval library, so the interval on a
runtime estimate (§32) takes its design from that file and none of its code.

**FrankenSQLite's pager policies: eviction for the memo store** [S]. FACT:
`frankensqlite/crates/fsqlite-pager/src/s3_fifo.rs` (3,058 lines) implements a three-queue policy: a small
admission queue, a main queue with bounded reinsertion, and a ghost queue of metadata, with an adaptive small
share between 5% and 30% and a rollout gate. Sibling files `arc_cache.rs` and `evalue_eviction.rs` hold two
further policies. The state machine is keyed on `fsqlite_types::PageNumber`, so it cannot be instantiated over
content hashes. Use: the memo graph of §28 stores results by content identity and must evict by something
better than recency, since a scan over many designs touches each key once. Posture: Pattern for the policy,
written with the memo graph in `frob-verbs`; Oracle for the sibling module in `frob-conformance`. Gate
INT-FSQL-02: under a bijection from keys to page numbers, our eviction sequence equals the sibling's on 10
recorded traces of at least 10⁵ accesses, and on the edit-loop trace the hit ratio is not below LRU's.
Fallback: LRU with admission weighted by recompute cost; never an unbounded store. Entries differ in recompute
cost by orders of magnitude, so the size accounting is in bytes and the admission rule may refuse a cheap
entry; that departure from the sibling's policy is tested separately, not hidden inside the differential test.

**frankenjax's e-graph: a pattern, and only if a profile asks** [F]. FACT: `frankenjax/crates/fj-egraph` exists
(9,408 lines in `src/lib.rs`), built on the third-party `egg` crate over frankenjax's own intermediate
representation; frankenjax pins asupersync 0.5.0. Use: none at run time. Extraction over an e-graph could shrink
derived kernel arithmetic beyond common-subexpression elimination. Ceiling, stated before any test: the gain is
at most the arithmetic share of step time multiplied by the reduction in operations, so if the M2 profile puts
arithmetic below 20% of step time, a 10% reduction is worth at most 2% and the item is dropped without a run.
Posture: Pattern. It is never a dependency, because it would add `egg` and a second asupersync. Pilot and gate
INT-FJAX-01, in the `derive/` annex only: with rewrite rules restricted to identities exact over the reals that
also preserve floating-point results under the kernel's determinism class, the extracted kernel matches the
baseline bit for bit on the conformance vectors, and the operation count falls by at least 10% on at least three
kernels. Kill: either condition fails. Fallback: common-subexpression elimination only (`fsym-simplify`, 3,105
lines, already in the annex).

**frankentui: the dashboard** [F]. FACT: version 0.10.0, twenty crates under `frankentui/crates`, about 1.15
million lines; `ftui-runtime` carries an optional exact pin on asupersync 0.5.0 behind `asupersync-executor`
(`crates/ftui-runtime/Cargo.toml:56, :81`); `ftui-harness` supports headless tests. Use: `frob-tui` shows jobs,
races, budgets and gate status. Posture: Consume with default features off and `runtime` and `native-backend`
on; the executor feature is forbidden. `frob-tui` reads the daemon's event stream over the local socket and
links no physics crate. If frankentui does not build on T, the remedy is an upstream change in frankentui or the
toolchain train of §33.13, and until it lands the fallback below applies; the crate gets no toolchain of its
own. Gate INT-FTUI-01: one asupersync package or none in its graph; the job pane
rendered from a recorded event stream equals its stored snapshot in the headless harness; idle processor use at
most 2% of one core. The gate is also the pilot, run on a recorded stream before the crate is funded. Ceiling: a
convenience for a person watching a campaign; no claim and no agent workflow depends on it. Kill: the gate
fails, or frankentui cannot be built without its executor. Fallback: no dashboard; the same events as
line-delimited JSON.

**franken_threed: a discipline, and an optional renderer route** [F]. FACT: four crates (`f3d-core` 10,688
lines, `f3d-math` 19,100, `f3d-graph` 7,507, `f3d-runtime` 31,564). Its status table says: Three.js r186 is
pinned; an ingest command routes an ordinary application's WebGPU renderer to a new backend for an admitted
feature subset; pixel parity holds for ten scenes on a software rasterizer; no hardware run and no speedup have
been measured; single-file packaging is not built (`franken_threed/README.md`). It pins asupersync 0.5.0. Use:
its `DEPENDENCY_ADMISSION.md` discipline is already adopted (§33.6). The viewer is an ordinary Three.js r186

page built through the route match the plain bundle within 1/255 per channel on at least 99.9% of pixels, and
an unadmitted feature fails explicitly. Fallback: the plain bundle. Ceiling: this route changes rendering cost
only, and rendering is outside every claim of §39.

**franken_drone_geometry_reconstruction: a scan-import lane** [F]. FACT: its status file (snapshot 2026-09-04)
describes an evidence path from recorded-media custody to an audited relative bundle problem, and says it does
not yet optimize cameras, emit metres or publish geometry (`IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md`); its crates hold about 27
thousand lines. The schemas for what it will publish exist: `schemas/geometry_generation.schema.json` requires
`coordinate_frame`, `scale_status`, `representations`, `uncertainty_root`, `coverage_root` and
`publication_stage`, and `schemas/scale_model.schema.json` records a scale authority with residuals in parts per
million. Use: a place scanned by a drone or a phone enters Habitat with its coverage and uncertainty attached.
Posture: Pattern today, as a schema adapter in `frob-scene` with no crate dependency; Subprocess once its
command-line tool publishes geometry. Gate INT-FDGR-01: the schema fixtures validate; a geometry generation
whose scale status is not metric is refused, because a relative scale cannot enter a physics scene; coverage
masks become the scene's unknown-space label, so a clearance certificate treats an unscanned region as unknown
and never as free; and the privacy inheritance of §37 applies to the result. Fallback: mesh and point-cloud
import through `fs-io` with scale declared by the operator and `reality: no-claim`. Counterexample to the
shortcut "import the mesh and trust it": a corridor whose far half was never observed appears as empty space in
a naive import, and a traversal certificate over it would be false; with the coverage mask the same query
returns unknown. Pilot: the schema fixtures and the refusal cases, which need no geometry. Ceiling: one import
lane among several; no milestone waits for the sibling to publish geometry. Kill: no published geometry by the
M5 entry review, after which the lane stays a schema adapter.

**fastmcp_rust: the MCP server** [S]. FACT: workspace version 0.13.0; the facade package is `fastmcp-rust`, with
`fastmcp-core`, `-protocol`, `-transport`, `-server`, `-client`, `-macros`, `-console` and `-cli`, about 1.23

fastmcp_rust onto T (§33.13). Gate: INT-FMCP-01. Fallback: KILL-MCP.

  (`check-deps`).

- **INV-SUITE-03** Every recorded gate result cites a resolution receipt, and no PASS is recorded on a dirty
  sibling tree (`check-stack`).
- **INV-SUITE-04** No sibling checkout is ever modified or moved by this project's tooling (`check-stack` writes
  nothing outside this repository, and its test runs it against a copy it cannot write to). An upstream change
  is made by an agent working in the sibling's repository under that repository's rules (§33.8), never by a tool
  of this one.
- **INV-SUITE-05** A result that crossed the multiphysics bridge or came from a worker at a different receipt is
  never merged into a throughput-tier or same-stack claim (enforced by the evidence types of §12, tested in

**Row 5, the hand case and the type.** Let the body frame be rotated by 90° about z, so that body x is world y. A
caller holding a body-frame wrench with force (1, 0, 0) N means a push along world y. Copied unconverted into
`force_world` it pushes along world x: the same magnitude, the same energy, a direction wrong by 90°, and nothing
faults. DESIGN: `frob-fsim` defines `MixedWrench { force_world, torque_body }` beside the three maps of §11.3. Its
only constructors are from a body wrench at the centre of mass (f_world = R·f_body, torque unchanged) and from a
world wrench at the centre of mass (τ_body = Rᵀ·τ_world, force unchanged). A wrench at any other reference point is
first moved by the pushforward of §11.3. No other crate names the type.

**Row 7, the consequence.** A Cargo graph holds one version of `serde_json` 1.x. The cloth oracle of §33.15 cannot
be a dependency of a crate that also links FrankenSim, whose graph resolves 1.0.154. INT-FTX-01 therefore runs
`ftx-drape` as a worker process that exchanges whole jobs, the posture §33.14 already defines for FrankenSim, until
the pin is relaxed in franken_textiles. That change is upstream work item FD-FTX-01 (Appendix F).

**Row 8, a reported fact to recheck.** A compile probe on this M5 Ultra is reported to show that Metal Shading
Language 3.2 and 4.0 provide no 64-bit integer atomic add and no 64-bit compare-and-swap (FACT to recheck; the
fingerprint of §21.16 re-runs it). The consequence for kernels is in §21.

**Row 10, the closed form and the hand case.** For a pure translation the twist has zero angular part, ad² = 0, and
the left and right differentials of the exponential are exactly I + ad/2 and I − ad/2, both with determinant one. For
a translation of 33 m along +x and a unit rotation rate about +z, the linear y component is −16.5 m in one and +16.5 m
in the other. A warehouse aisle is longer than 32 m, so a refusal there would exclude ordinary poses. The anchored
coordinates of §11 keep translations inside a cell small, but a relative pose between two bodies in one aisle is not
anchored.

**Row 13, why it matters although no certificate depends on it.** §25.4.9 and C-32 name `fs-sos` as an owner worth
probing, and §22.12.4 cites its region-of-attraction routine. A value from it is a proposal to check. Two rules follow
for any bound this project accepts from a floating-point routine: the bound is evaluated on the authored coefficients,
or the error of translating them is bounded on the actual domain; and the last operation is rounded outward.

**Upstream work items**, added to Appendix F by description: fold or declare the omitted masses of the G1 catalog; a
closed-form differential for small rotation and large translation; a documented or removed legacy transformer; an
arc-aware swept bound; an authored-coefficient check and an outward-rounded result in `fs-sos`; a ray transform that
returns the scale of its parameter. Each is done in the sibling's repository under its rules (§33.8), and the interim
postures above hold until it lands.

|---|---|
| GATE-WS-09 | Known answer. Each of the six admission tests is recorded at the pin with its result: the roll-up of 31.96314202 kg; the refusal at 33 m and the agreement at 1 m to 10⁻¹², with the closed form returning ∓16.5 m; the signed motion witness for both transformer entry points; the arc fixture; the two `fs-sos` probes compared with exact evaluation; the two-plane ray fixture. A probe that now passes upstream is recorded as fixed and its interim posture is reviewed. M0, with rows 12 and 14 at M2. |

## 34. Workspace, crates, formats

This chapter fixes where code lives, what each crate is for and how large it may grow before someone asks why,
which crate may depend on which, which artifact formats exist and who owns each, and the working rules. Its
purpose is to keep a large program reviewable: a reader should be able to find the crate for any sentence of
Parts III to V, and a tool should be able to refuse a dependency this chapter forbids.

### 34.1 Repository layout

```
franken_robotics/
  Cargo.toml  rust-toolchain.toml  franken-stack.lock        # core workspace; the one toolchain T (§33.13)
  .cargo/config.toml                                         # build-identity setting for path consumption (§33.2)
  AGENTS.md  README.md  DEPENDENCY_ADMISSION.md  COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_FRANKEN_ROBOTICS.md
  crates/frob-*/            # the core: 38 crates, unsafe denied, Franken-only runtime dependencies
  crates/frob-cert/         # also builds alone, on a stable compiler, with no dependency (§34.11)
  surface/frob-mcp/         # MCP server on fastmcp_rust; core workspace member; links frob-verbs (§32.12.2)
  spark/frob-spark-cuda/    # annex workspace on T: cudarc, registered unsafe capsules
  spark/frob-spark-metal/   # annex workspace on T: ft-kernel-metal gateway
  apps/                     # workspace that links core + annexes into frob, frobd
  worker/                   # workspace manifest for frob-fsim-worker (INT-FSIM-18; KILL-FSIM fallback (a))
  derive/frob-derive/       # annex workspace on T: build-time derivation with FrankenSymPy
  bindings/frob-gymnasium/  # optional Gymnasium-compatible adapter: a Rust shim and a Python package
  lean/                     # Lake project; outputs not committed
  viewer/                   # Three.js viewer and HTML export
  kernels/                  # shared-dialect sources and generated arithmetic, with digests
  registries/               # verbs.toml, refusals.toml, kernels.toml, gates.toml, formats.toml, upstream.toml,
                            #   lifts.toml, capsules.toml, cards/
  schemas/                  # generated from formats.toml and verbs.toml; never edited
  demos/                    # one demo.yaml per release path (§34.12)
  receipts/                 # resolution receipts (§33.5)
  assets/                   # templates, generic actuator and interface cards, license manifests
  tests/fixtures/oracle/    # pinned oracle captures, never regenerated from the candidate
  tools/oracle/             # capture scripts for development-time oracles
  docs/delivery/            # the delivery log (never in this plan)
```

Six workspaces exist: the core, which includes `surface/frob-mcp`, the two GPU annexes, `apps/`, `derive/` and
`bindings/`, with `worker/` as a seventh that only re-targets an existing crate. All of them build on T, and no
annex carries a toolchain file of its own (§33.13); `lean/` is not Rust. One exception is a fallback by design:
when KILL-FSIM's fallback (a) keeps the worker at an older pin, `worker/` builds on that pin's toolchain
(§33.14). The reason for an annex boundary is never the compiler. It is the unsafe and foreign-interface policy:
a dependency the core's lockfile may not contain (a third-party driver binding, an FFI capsule, a Python
interpreter, FrankenSymPy at build time).

The two GPU annexes keep their own lockfiles for that reason, and it rests on FACTs of §21.2 and §33.13: the
suite keeps its working GPU code outside FrankenSim's workspace, `cudarc` is a third-party driver binding, and
`ft-kernel-metal` needs FrankenTorch's `[patch.crates-io] block` entry at the root of whichever workspace
resolves it. A separate lockfile keeps the driver bindings, the registered capsules and that patch out of the
core's resolution (rules L-3 and L-4, §34.4). `surface/frob-mcp` has no such reason: fastmcp_rust is a Franken
foundation that forbids unsafe code (FACT, §32.12.1), so the server is an ordinary member of the core workspace
and its directory name says only that it is a surface.
