### 39.22 Three arms, the recovery ratio and the phase ablations

**Three arms [S].** One ratio cannot answer the two questions the test is asked: how far this system is ahead of
the incumbent pipeline as it is commonly run, and how much of that lead an incumbent engine recovers once every
portable method is layered over it. Every stratum is therefore run with three arms on the same sealed missions,
acceptance protocol, hardware and resource caps.

| Arm | What it is | Frozen by |
|---|---|---|
| B, the declared incumbent | A leading incumbent simulator with per-design reinforcement learning and a standard outer-loop optimizer | Its own advocates, on development fixtures |
| W, the composed incumbent | The same engine or engines with every portable method layered on: native state restore and forks, per-topology buckets or the engine's own heterogeneous solver, a sampling controller or a multi-embodiment prior with checkpoint resume, racing and stopping, importance-weighted failure search, a second engine as referee | A competent baseline engineer (§2.1), on development fixtures |
| F, this system | The release under test | The release |

With T_X the restricted mean time of arm X on a stratum and C_X its GPU-hours, the **recovery ratio** of the
composed incumbent is

    r_T = (T_B − T_W) / (T_B − T_F)        r_C = (C_B − C_W) / (C_B − C_F)

defined when F beats B on that measure. A value of 1 means the layer recovers the whole saving and the engine adds
nothing on that stratum; 0 means the layer recovers nothing. If T_F = 0.10·T_B, then r_T ≥ 0.8 exactly when
T_W ≤ 0.28·T_B. Three cases are fixed before any measurement. If T_F ≥ T_B the stratum is reported as "no saving to
recover" and r is undefined. If T_W < T_F then r exceeds 1 and the stratum is a loss to the composed incumbent.
A mission unresolved at the deadline H costs H in every arm.

Decision rules (TARGET thresholds, registered before the sealed suite opens):

- r_T ≥ 0.8 and r_C ≥ 0.8 on a stratum: a thin layer over an incumbent is enough there. The report says so and the
  fallback of BET-14 applies to that stratum.
- Both below 0.5: the engine is a source of the gain on that stratum.
- Otherwise the stratum is reported as mixed, with the phase the layer could not recover named from the ledger.
- The word "ten-fold" is governed by F against the stronger of B and W (§2.1), never by F against B alone.

*One receipt first.* FACT (Appendix H): in the incumbent documents read, run-to-run determinism, heterogeneous
worlds and the fastest solver sit on different solver paths, so each is available and their conjunction is not
shown. Arm W is therefore built as one pipeline, on one fixed-topology brief and one mixed-topology contact-rich
brief, before F exists, and the property that binds when all are demanded at once is recorded. One expensive
incompatibility can sink the layer; several rarely exercised gaps may leave it competitive. Feature counts decide
neither.

**Phase ablations [S].** The phase ledger separates three accounts of where a gain comes from. On two briefs (one
narrow wheeled, one contact-rich legged), on arm B's engine, three single-change replays run against the traced
baseline.

1. *Information only.* Batch proposals and a sound cheap diagnostic filter; the same controller acquisition and
   the same solver.
2. *Controller acquisition only.* The same candidates, with per-design training replaced by a qualified cheaper
   controller: a prior with fine-tuning, inheritance, or a delivered sampling controller (§22).
3. *Stepping only.* The same candidates and controllers on a faster solver at matched fidelity.

Each returns its own ratio and the share of the baseline's critical path that it touched. The ablations must
respect two bounds computed from the baseline trace. If training that an intervention does not remove is a share
s of elapsed time, that intervention's ratio is at most 1/s (1.43 at s = 0.7). If an intervention removes that
share entirely its ratio is at most 1/(1 − s) (3.33). Illustration: 50 trained designs at 35 minutes each with 1.5
minutes of agent time per design make training 1,750 of 1,825 minutes, 95.9%, and cap information alone at 1.04.
With controller acquisition at 45 s per design, agent time is 75 of 112.5 minutes, two thirds, and information
becomes the larger lever. Which regime a stratum is in is a measurement, not a premise.

*Owner and verbs.* The protocol is this chapter's; the phase ledger is `frob-chronicle`'s. `report.campaign --arms
B,W,F` prints T, C, r_T and r_C with intervals, and `report.campaign --ablate {information, controller, stepping}`
prints an ablation with its bound.

| Gate | Claim | Threshold (TARGET) | First milestone |
|---|---|---|---|
| GATE-TENFOLD-13 | Design comparison; Performance | r_T and r_C are published with 95% intervals for every stratum that has a ratio, whatever their values. The three ablations are run on both briefs, and a ratio above its 1/s or 1/(1 − s) bound voids the stratum as an accounting error. The one-receipt pipeline for arm W is built and its binding property recorded before any engine-internal work package beyond M2 is funded | M3; M7 for the sealed suite |

## 40. The gate register

This chapter is the single list of every gate in the plan. The subsystem chapters define their gates where the
mechanisms are described; the register collects them, gives each one claim and one earliest milestone, lists every
kill gate with its trigger and fallback, and says what each milestone exit must have on record. It contains 32
admission gates and five sibling admission gates, 278 convergence gates with the Gauntlet's own gate and the
thirteen gates of the ten-fold test beside them, 112 kill gates with the seven kill gates of the ten-fold test
beside them, and the program gates. The gates of subsections added after these tables were compiled are indexed in
§40.8. All thresholds are TARGETs until a gate records a measured value.

### 40.1 Semantics

1. **A gate passes only with a recorded measurement against its threshold.** The record is a row of
   `registries/gates.toml` that cites a commit of this repository, the command, its output and a receipt hash, and
   that resolves in the artifact graph of §29. A gate with no record has the status `not run`, which is not a pass.
   Statuses are `not run`, `pass`, `fail`, `killed: fallback adopted` and `blocked: ⟨open question⟩`.
2. **A kill gate (✖) names its trigger and its fallback in advance and is never quietly re-scoped.** Its decision is
   recorded as an ADR at the milestone named here. A trigger, a threshold or a fallback changes only by a dated
   amendment to this register, with its reason, made before the measurement it governs. A kill gate that fires is
   not a failure of the program: the fallback is the plan.
3. **Each gate names exactly one of the seven claims of §8**: Proof, Known answer, Parity, Fidelity, Design
   comparison, Reality or Performance. A row that a chapter labelled "method" or "Performance of the method" is a
   Design comparison, as §8.1 rules. A row that named two claims is given the claim of its governing part, and the
   note under §40.3 says which part that is.
4. **Where a chapter and the register differ, the register governs**: on a gate's identity, its claim, its earliest
   milestone, a kill gate's trigger, fallback and decision point, and on every number the register states. The
   threshold column is a brief. The full pass criterion, with its fixtures and negative controls, is the row in the
   defining subsection, and a clause that the brief leaves out is not waived.
5. **Every convergence gate has a registered negative control that it catches** (GATE-GAUNT-01, §38). A gate whose
   control has not been shown to fail has not passed.
6. **Earliest milestone.** The first milestone at whose exit the gate must have a record. Where two milestones are
   given, a part is due at each, as stated. A milestone exits when every gate with a part due there has a record
   that is a pass or a kill decision with its fallback adopted. A failed convergence gate that has no kill gate
   blocks the exit.
7. **Admission is never inherited** (§33). A foundation first used at a later milestone is admitted then, by its own
   record, at the pin of that day.
8. **Recurring gates.** GATE-GROUND-01, GATE-SAFE-01, GATE-GAUNT-01 and GATE-TENFOLD-09 are re-run at every exit
   after their first.
9. **Owner.** The chapter of the defining subsection owns the gate and its fixtures. Six kill gates are stated in
   two chapters; the register lists each once under its owner and names the other chapter as a consumer (§40.7).

rest, as version 0.2 did. Twenty-three rows that a chapter labels, or first labelled, "Performance of the method" or
"method" are Design comparison (the chapters of §24 to §32 now print that claim; the rows quoted below are quoted as
first drafted):
GATE-ARENA-09; GATE-ATEL-01, -03, -07, -08, -15; GATE-AUTOPSY-08; GATE-CORTEX-03, -11, -13, -14, -17;
GATE-FOUNDRY-05; GATE-NEMESIS-02, -05; GATE-PHYLUM-06, -08; GATE-REFLEX-02, -06, -09; GATE-SHIELD-03;
GATE-TETHER-01, -13; and, by the readings below, GATE-AUGUR-07. Rows that named two claims, or a claim outside the
seven, are read as follows.

- GATE-ATEL-12. Row: Known answer, Performance. The latency figures govern; PO-ATEL-07 and the shadow-mismatch stop
  are known-answer preconditions.
- GATE-AUGUR-07. Row: Performance. Read as Design comparison: two agent arms on scripted tasks; no speed figure on
  named hardware is claimed.

  rows govern; referee episodes per verdict are recorded figures.

  figure is evaluated by GATE-SPARK-20 and KILL-SHARD (§40.7).

  the shuffled-label control is its negative control.

  reference within a stated error.

  ballistic row and the binary-metric refusal are known-answer preconditions.

**Milestones the register assigned.** Where a chapter's gate table has no milestone column, the earliest milestone
above comes from the milestone skeleton of §43 (Marrow, Skeleton, Sinew, Tether, safety, workspace, GATE-QUAL-01 and
GATE-REFLEX-04) or from the milestone note printed under the chapter's own table (Atelier and Chronicle). Every other
milestone is the one in the gate's own row, except where that row disagrees with the milestone skeleton: there the
register follows the skeleton, and §40.7 lists each case.

**Shared fixtures.** Several gates record one experiment from the side of the chapter that consumes it. The batch
independence of a world's digests is recorded by GATE-KIN-05, GATE-PHYLUM-02, GATE-SPARK-15, GATE-CHRON-01,
GATE-AUTOPSY-01 and the digest part of GATE-TETHER-09. The model-form check is recorded by GATE-FID-05,
GATE-CORTEX-15 and GATE-ATEL-10. The frozen 30-amendment campaign serves GATE-ATEL-11 and GATE-AUGUR-12, over one
revalidation engine. The tier correction is recorded by GATE-FID-08 and GATE-CHRON-09. In each case the fixture is
one, it is run once per milestone, and each gate is compared with the threshold in its own row.

### 40.4 Kill gates

Every kill gate of the plan, once. "Decided" is the milestone at whose exit the decision is recorded as an ADR; for
a gate whose trigger is a pilot, it is the earliest milestone at which the work package can be funded. "Owner" is
the subsection that governs the trigger and the fallback; a second subsection in parentheses is a consumer that
states the same gate from its side.

### 40.5 Program gates

Program gates decide whether the program continues as planned. They do not belong to a subsystem.

| Gate | When | Measurement and threshold | If it is not met |
|---|---|---|---|
| The schedule gate (BET-12) | End of M1 | The elapsed time of M0 plus M1 against the planning estimate of §43, with the cause of any slip attributed in the M1 exit review. Not met if the two milestones took more than 1.5 times their estimate because a sibling lacked a primitive, its upstream work item had not landed and no interim posture of Appendix F applied | The program pauses for a written re-plan before M2 starts |
| GATE-TENFOLD-01 (the parity-baseline gate) | M0 | The rival audit and the incumbent phases that need no agent, measured on `trj`: the M0 rows of GATE-SPARK-21 (§39.11) | M0 does not exit. The arithmetic of §2 stays a HYPOTHESIS and no work package is funded as a speed lever |
| GATE-TENFOLD-02 | M1 | The incumbent design loop with the common agent, with closed phase ledgers (§39.11) | The same. The table of §2.2 may not be cited as a denominator |
| GATE-TENFOLD-09 | M1, then every exit | Ceiling before speed, program-wide (§39.8) | The speed comparison is refused; the work package loses its speed justification (KILL-TENFOLD-LEVER) |
| GATE-TENFOLD-03, -04, -05 | M3 and M7, before a sealed suite is opened | The harness known answers; the freeze and seal order with the pre-analysis; adjudicator acceptance (§39.18) | The suite is not opened |
| GATE-TENFOLD-06 (the partial ten-fold gate) | M3 | On `legged-quad` and `wheeled`, and on `envelope` and `sensing` where ready: the pooled ratio with its interval, verdict, completion, coverage, tie test and phase ledgers for arms A, B and C; the outcome rules of §39.10 applied. Met when the record exists, whatever the ratio | M3 does not exit |
| GATE-TENFOLD-07 (the tournament) | M7 | The same record for every stratum run, on fresh sealed families with every pin frozen, published with its ledgers and its kit. Met when the report is published, whatever it says | M7 does not exit, and no comparative claim is made |
| GATE-TENFOLD-08 | M7 | The replication kit recomputes every published number and re-runs a sampled pair per stratum (§39.14) | The result is labelled `unreplicated` and the word "ten-fold" is not used |
| GATE-TENFOLD-10 | M3, before the partial gate | The pre-analysis known answers of §39.20 (10.081, 9.677, 1.8215, 0.78568; the counts 32, 46, 49 and 182); the contrast test certifies ten-fold in none of 2,000 rare-tail campaigns, and the percentile bootstrap, run as the negative control, certifies it in 78.6% ± 3 points | The suite is not opened; no population wording is used |
| GATE-TENFOLD-11 | M3 for the partial gate; M7 | The rival audit of §39.21 is complete before sealing: each arm's frozen configuration reproduces its development-fixture figure within 10%; the sign-off and the pack digest are recorded | The suite is not sealed; a changed digest voids the arm |
| GATE-TENFOLD-12 | M7 | Suite hygiene (§39.21): an easy win and an unresolved answer in every stratum; every planted mutation rejected; zero missed withdrawals for a scoped claim | The affected stratum is `descriptive` |
| GATE-TENFOLD-13 | M3; M7 for the sealed suite | The recovery ratios r_T and r_C with 95% intervals for every stratum that has a ratio; the three phase ablations on both briefs, each inside its bound; the one-receipt pipeline for arm W built first (§39.22) | No engine-internal work package beyond M2 is funded |

| Kill gate of the ten-fold test | In brief | Decided |
|---|---|---|
| ✖ KILL-TENFOLD-SPEED | A measured ratio below 3 on a confirmatory cell, or a futility stop, withdraws the speed claim for that class; the product is described by what does not depend on speed | M3 for the classes run; M7 |
| ✖ KILL-TENFOLD-TIE | The ablation arm reaches the same accepted scope within a factor of 1.5, or the composed incumbent's recovery ratio is at least 0.8 on elapsed time and on compute (§39.22): say so and ship the layer over that engine for that stratum | M3; M7 |
| ✖ KILL-TENFOLD-CERT | One false certificate disqualifies the arm from the scoped claim | Standing, from M3 |
| ✖ KILL-TENFOLD-LEAK | Any leak from sealed confirmation worlds voids the affected cells, retires their families and, if unbounded, voids the gate | Standing, from M3 |
| ✖ KILL-TENFOLD-LEVER | A mechanism whose removable cost is under 10% of the measured loop is not funded as a speed lever | M1; M2 |
| ✖ KILL-TENFOLD-ADJ | No neutral simulator passes acceptance for a stratum: cross-home adjudication, labelled; failing that, the stratum is descriptive | M3; M7 |
| ✖ KILL-TENFOLD-REACH | A cell whose pre-analysis cannot reach its verdicts is opened as descriptive | M3; M7 |

### 40.7 Discrepancies resolved by this register

**Kill gates stated in two chapters.** The owner chapter governs the trigger and the fallback, and the other
chapter is a consumer.

| Kill gate | Owner's row | Consumer's row | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| KILL-DR | §29.20: ρ_ep below 0.7 on 200 paired addresses in every stratum tested, or GATE-CHRON-09 coverage fails after one repair cycle. Fallback: promotion reports the label only, from referee episodes alone | §16.17: ρ below 0.7 for the promoted quantities on 200 battery addresses, or effective sample size below 30% of the audited count in more than a tenth of promotions. Fallback: the plain paired promotion of C-15, with segment mode where whole-episode ρ is low | §29 governs. §16's effective-sample-size clause is not a trigger; it stays a recorded diagnostic of the correction. The two fallbacks describe one state from two sides: the tier correction is off and promotion returns to the paired label of C-15. Segment mode remains an option inside that fallback |
| KILL-RANK | §28.23: GATE-ATEL-07 fails for every morphology class tested. Fallback: R1 is `uninformative` everywhere, every candidate that survives static analysis is scored on the higher rung, and the ladder's claim shrinks to stopping and elimination among trained candidates | §16.17: top-weighted τ below 0.5 in more than half the strata for the reference classes. Fallback: tier pairs promote individual results only | §28 governs: the kill gate concerns agreement between evaluation rungs. §16's row concerns agreement between physics tiers, which GATE-FID-04 measures; its consequence, that no population is ordered across a tier pair whose τ is below 0.5, is the per-stratum rule of GATE-FID-04 and holds without a kill gate |
| KILL-FDGRAD | §17.13: the pilot's falsifier fires (variance ratio below 2 at every horizon of 50 steps or more, or sign agreement below 70%), or no end point is confirmed by a specialist. Fallback: rank-based search, with the stencil kept as a sensitivity report | §28.8 and §28.23 cite §17.13 and repeat its trigger and fallback | One gate; §17's statement is the register's |
| KILL-FILM | §18.8: on the wet-floor battery the film law changes fewer than 10% of episode outcomes against a constant-coefficient patch, or adds more than 5% to step time. Fallback: static condition cards on lockstep tiers | §19.10: the advected film fails its mass gate after one repair cycle, or costs more than 15% of the step, or design rankings on the spill battery agree with static patches at a rank correlation of 0.95 or above. Fallback: static film-friction patches | Two mechanisms shared one name, and they are two gates. The register's KILL-FILM is §18's and governs the film-friction law [S]. §19's gate is KILL-ADVECT, the stop rule of the advected film [F], with its own row in §40.4 and its decision recorded with GATE-HAB-07: when it fires, advection is not built and Habitat uses the law of §18 on static film patches. If KILL-FILM itself fires, both fall to static condition cards |
| KILL-SLOT | §32.21: any digest difference under co-tenancy, or the throughput or step-time limits of GATE-TETHER-09 fail after one optimization pass | §21.11: any slot-invariance failure at GATE-SPARK-15, or 99th-percentile step time more than 10% above the same job run alone | §32 governs. Its limits contain §21's and add the 5% throughput limit and the optimization pass. The fallback is the same |
| KILL-SPECIALIZE | §21.18: the specialized kernel below 1.2 on the whole step in the pilot, or a compile above 60 s, or a specializable share under one third in the M2 profile | §17.9: measured whole-step gain below 1.2, or compile above 60 s per design | §21 governs and adds the profile clause, which can fire at M2 before any pilot is funded. The fallbacks agree |

**Admission gates stated twice.** INT-FLN-02, INT-FNP-02, INT-FSYM-02 and INT-FT-02 appear in §33.6 and again, with
their source anchors, in §33.10. The thresholds do not differ. The register uses the fuller statement of §33.10.

**KILL-MCP, stated once.** The design of record is `frob-mcp` as a member of the core graph on T, running verbs in
process (§33.13). The row in §32.21 and the register agree: the trigger is that INT-FMCP-01 cannot pass within the M0
budget after FD-FMCP-01 and FD-ASUP-01 have been attempted, and the fallbacks are, in order, `frob-mcp` as its own
workspace reaching `frobd` over a local socket in newline-delimited JSON, and then the CLI.

## 41. Risks and the pre-mortem

This chapter asks how the program fails, names the earliest measurement that would show each failure coming, and
points at the mechanism that answers it. It has three parts: a pre-mortem written from a failed future, a second
pre-mortem for the case where every gate passed and the claim still failed, and the risk register. Labels: every
threshold in a signal or mitigation column is a TARGET repeated from the gate named beside it, and §40 governs where
the two differ; incumbent figures are FACTs registered in Appendix H; counts of crates, milestones and gates are
FACTs about this document (§34.2, §40, §43). Nothing in this chapter is a result.

### 41.1 It is late 2029 and FrankenRobotics failed. Why?

DESIGN: each row is a story told from the failure backwards. The earliest signal is a quantity the program already
records, chosen so that it moves while the failure is still cheap. The countermeasure names the section that owns
it. The residual is what remains after the countermeasure works as designed. Stories 1 to 15 are carried from
version 0.2 with their countermeasures corrected to this version's mechanisms. Stories 16 to 27 are new: five about
the thesis, three about the evidence, four about the program.

| # | Failure story | Earliest signal | Countermeasure in this plan | Residual |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The mathematics became the product. Elegant algebra crates grew and no robot walked. | Layer-1 crates grow while the M1 exit slips; a construction with no verb or no failing test | D-2 and D-6 (§9); milestone exits are robots moving and answers accepted (§43); a construction missing any of its four obligations moves to Appendix C | The temptation is constant |
| 2 | FrankenSim moved weekly and adapter churn consumed the effort. | BET-04's metric: upstream breakage above 20% of working days in a four-week window. Context (FACT, §33.2): 409 commits touched `fs-mbd` in thirty days | Pinned commit, the airlock, the compatibility train; KILL-FSIM with the worker process first and the lift second (§33.8, §33.14) | The lift is priced against a closure of about 1.5 million lines, not against two crates |
| 3 | GPU kernels passed tests and diverged in the field, so nobody trusted fast results. | Divergence-ledger entries without explanations; a world whose digest depends on the batch it ran in | `spark.check` on every driver or compiler change; the fingerprint gate; teleport; batch-composition invariance (GATE-SPARK-15); decision-level equivalence (GATE-SPARK-16); the promotion rule (§16, §21, §35) | Class D3 comparisons are statistical |
| 4 | Throughput landed far under the parity band and agents stopped waiting. | The M2 profile; a paired lower bound under 0.67 of the incumbent measured on `trj` | Profile first (§36); KILL-PARITY; KILL-KIR; the ladder reduces how many steps a decision needs (§28) | Every figure is a TARGET until M2 |
| 5 | Policies exploited contact compliance and promotions kept failing. | Promotion failure rate; `energy-created` flags; the share of finalists typed `model-conditional` | The trust ladder, the energy audit and the model-form rank check (§16); the detectors of §23.16; KILL-CONTACT with CL-2 (§18) | Convex compliant models have real artifacts |
| 6 | Baseline controllers failed on new morphologies, so every design needed training after all. | GATE-REFLEX-02's trend on the corpus; the share of designs reported `not-synthesizable` | Three-outcome reporting (§22.6); KILL-BASELINE; the sampling controller as fallback (BET-27); behaviour-cloning warm starts (§23.10) | Novel bodies are hard |
| 7 | The agent surface was too large and agents got lost. | GATE-TETHER-01 and GATE-TETHER-13 failures; serial turns per accepted answer | Clusters of at most seven tools; `session.focus`; `next_actions`; `robot-docs`; the surface A/B of BET-10 (§32, §28) | The registry is large even in clusters |
| 8 | The swarm closed beads that proved plumbing. | Shared close reasons; a gate without a caught negative control; a PASS recorded by the session that implemented the capability | The rules against false progress in §38; GATE-GAUNT-01 at every exit; typed close reasons (§0.7, §45) | Needs discipline at every exit review |
| 9 | Interiors were toy boxes and results did not transfer to real places. | Reviewer inspection of generated scenes; the share of dimensions labelled `assumed` | OPEN-HAB-1 norms; hazard registries; scene acceptance; real-place ingestion (§19) | Realism is unbounded work |
| 10 | Sim-to-real was never tested and claims overreached. | Any report without a `reality:` line | The seven claims (§8); GATE-GROUND-01 at every exit; `reality: no-claim`; card provenance; the no-authorization flags (§12) | No hardware is in scope |
| 11 | "Certified" became a marketing word while the proof tools stayed immature. | Certificates without replay hashes; the word "verified" in any output | The wording rule of §12; `frob-verify`; KILL-LEMMA; the record of whether a certificate changed a decision | Depends on the proof siblings maturing, which is upstream work of this program (Appendix F) |
| 12 | Single precision failed in large scenes and long runs. | GATE-SPARK-05; the share of worlds marked `Degraded: ill-conditioned`; the guarded-predicate fallback rate | Anchored positions, diagonal scaling, guarded predicates with an exact fallback (§35); half precision is not built | Near-rigid cards stay outside `f32` |
| 13 | The GPU mandate and the suite's no-FFI doctrine were never reconciled, and work stalled on policy. | OPEN-SPARK-1 still open at M2 | The annex design (§21.2); the question is put to the owner at M0; M2 has a variant with no GPU (§43.5) | Owner decision |
| 14 | The Metal gateway's limits throttled the Mac tier. | Step-plan launch counts and blocked host time on Metal; GATE-SPARK-04 | Packed slabs and one batch per chunk; upstream work item FD-FT-01; KILL-METAL, after which the Mac keeps the world bank, proof, replay and `batch-cpu` roles (§21) | A Metal binding of our own needs an owner decision (OPEN-SPARK-5) |
| 15 | The plan itself became the delivery log and stopped being readable. | This file growing after conversion to beads | §0.7; `docs/delivery/` | See story 27 |
| 16 | The ten-fold claim failed on quadruped missions because incumbents already train in minutes. | The M0 phase ledger: time to threshold near the published 410 s on one RTX 4090 (FACT, Appendix H); a ceiling under ten for the class | §2.3 states the ceilings before anything is built; §2.6 gives the class a range of 3 to 10; GATE-SPARK-21 measures the denominator first; BET-13 fixes the wording for a ratio under 3 and for a ratio between 3 and 10; the partial gate at M3 | The quadruped ceiling cannot be engineered away, and the class may leave the claim |
| 17 | A composed incumbent layer tied. | Ties already on record from the plan-time pilots (a lifted linear program, a dependency graph); the composed arm within a factor of 1.5 at the M3 partial gate | BET-14; D-17; KILL-AUGUR-TIE; KILL-FAMILYCERT; the layer ships over that engine for the stratum, and engine work continues only for gaps internal to an engine (§2.6, §39) | The engine's share of the product shrinks |
| 18 | Rank agreement between rungs was low, so most designs were trained anyway. | Verdict flips after finalist training; top-weighted τ under 0.5 in the pilot on incumbent tools | The rank-agreement experiment runs first (§2.7); GATE-REFLEX-04, GATE-CORTEX-12, GATE-ATEL-07; `discard-only` mode; the audit lane and the planted winner; KILL-RANK; training at parity (GATE-CORTEX-05) | With most designs trained, the compute ratio is near 1 |
| 19 | Family policies did not transfer. | The pre-funding pilot; return with no adaptation under 70% of specialists; OPEN-CORTEX-1 at its default when M4 opens | KILL-FAMILY; inheritance for parameter edits; the baseline and sampling rungs; the variant of M4 with no family policy (§43.7) | The class is decided by specialists, and the humanoid range narrows |
| 20 | Mixed batches lost to per-family templates. | The M1 pilot of padding overhead and bucket count; arm B expressing at least 95% of the mutation corpus | The head-to-head with outcomes declared in advance (§17.14); KILL-PHYLUM and KILL-BUCKET; parameter variants within a topology are [S] and unaffected | Two performance differentiators are withdrawn |
| 21 | The plan's breadth starved the spine. Forty-three crates, nine milestones and more than four hundred gates spread a swarm thin. | Crates that hold only [F] or [M] content gain lines while an M1 or M2 exit slips; more than four [M] items active; a work package funded without its pilot | A tier on every mechanism; features that select a tier are off by default (L-12); D-6 and the cap of four; pilots before funding (§0.7); M1 needs three foundations; the program gate; exits defined by demonstrations and not by gate counts (§43) | Breadth is the brief, and the cap is enforced by people |
| 22 | Qualification was gamed. | A campaign with many requests and no close; a receipt field outside the listed set; a denominator that shrank | The blinded lane (§24): sealed clusters, pre-committed requests, α_i = α / [i·(i + 1)]; GATE-QUAL-01 under 500 adaptive retries; the firewall gates GATE-QUAL-02 and GATE-SAFE-03; scorecard accounting (GATE-ARENA-07) | Whoever holds `qual:admin` is trusted |
| 23 | Certificates were issued for the wrong statement. | A bundle whose embedded statement differs from the query; a changed quantifier accepted with consistent hashes | D-12; the bundle embeds the canonical bytes of the statement (§34.9); `MissionId` changes with any quantifier (INV-AUGUR-03); the mutation suites of GATE-LEMMA-03 and GATE-AUGUR-01, -06; KILL-AUGUR-FALSECERT; one false certificate disqualifies an arm (§39) | A true certificate of an uninteresting statement still reads as evidence (OPEN-AUGUR-8) |
| 24 | A foundation defect surfaced late. | A known answer or a baseline that cites a module before its admission test has passed | §33.11 records four reported defects as facts to recheck; INT-FSIM-05, -06, -07 and INT-FNP-02; an admission is never inherited; the file-by-file tests run at M0 | Unreported defects exist |
| 25 | The toolchain train stalled: the siblings could not be brought onto one toolchain, and a merge was blocked. | A failing cell in the matrix of INT-TOOLCHAIN-01; two asupersync packages in `cargo tree -d` | One toolchain T chosen at INT-TOOLCHAIN-01, with candidate (b) in reserve; FD-FMCP-01 and FD-ASUP-01 done at M0; KILL-MCP's fallbacks (§33.13); the `frob-units` escape hatch (§33.12); `check-deps` | Four nightlies and one stable release are the starting state (FACT, §33.13) |
| 26 | Calibration data never arrived. | No dataset admitted when M5 opens; OPEN-GROUND-1 and OPEN-GROUND-2 at their defaults | Reality is an import lane (§30): a synthetic rehearsal, frozen predictions, a published-anchor comparison at M3, bench packages that may be sourced from M0; the resting state is `no-claim` and blocks nothing | The Reality claim stays empty |
| 27 | The document itself became unreadable. | A threshold stated two ways; an identifier defined twice; a reader who cannot tell the spine from the frontier | The reading paths of §0.4; tier tags; §40 as the only authority for a threshold; registries generated from the plan's tables; the plan stops growing at conversion to beads | The plan is long by design |

Three clusters deserve a sentence each. Stories 16 to 20 are the thesis failing lever by lever, and §2 already says
that no single lever delivers the result; what the plan adds is that each lever has its own early experiment and a
fallback that ships under its own name. Stories 22 to 24 are the evidence failing, and they share a remedy: the
party that proposes a result never checks it. Stories 21 and 25 to 27 are the program failing under its own weight,
and their remedy is structural: M1 is small, the upper tiers are off by default, and the document delegates
progress to beads and registries.

### 41.2 Every gate passed and the claim still failed

A gate measures a mechanism. The ten-fold claim is about an outcome. The reasons below could hold with every
convergence gate green, so each is tied to a measurement that is not a mechanism gate. They are ranked by how early
the signal is available.

| Rank | Reason | Earliest signal | Where the plan answers it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Nothing confirmable existed: no metric, no incumbent arm, no neutral check. | No incumbent phase measurement on record at M0 exit | §2.1 defines the metric; §39 the arms and the adjudicator; GATE-SPARK-21 is an M0 exit condition (§43.3) |
| 2 | Amdahl. Incumbent training takes minutes, and the agent's latency is common to both arms. | Training under about 90% of a measured incumbent cycle in the M0 ledger | The ceilings of §2.3; many designs per turn (§17); the phase ledger of §39 |
| 3 | The cheap rung reorders designs, so most are trained after all, on a training rung that is only at parity. Worst on stairs, rubble and bipeds, where the multiplier would be largest. | Verdict flips after finalist training; the trained fraction f above about 1% | BET-17; the rank-agreement gates; `discard-only`; classes expected to be hard are sampled on purpose (§23, §28) |
| 4 | The referee could not run interior or tracked scenarios, so results stayed `provisional`. | The share of standard-battery scenarios the referee completes at M2 (GATE-FID-03) | The transactional step with witness migration (§16.5); the `strict` profile as adjudicator; BET-34 |
| 5 | Common-mode error. Every tier shared `generic` and `assumed` cards, so tiers agreed with each other and accepted decisions failed neutral adjudication. | The share of card fields that are `assumed` or `generic` in benchmark designs | Card provenance on every report (§15); the published-anchor comparison at M3 (§30); an evaluator neither arm trained in (§39) |
| 6 | Structure helped agents only slightly. | The ratio of restricted mean times in the surface A/B (GATE-ATEL-03), which needs an effect size and not merely a win | BET-10's threshold of 1.5 on at least ten briefs; the verbs that showed no effect lose their speed claim |

a capability or a claim; Low when it costs convenience. RISK-01 to RISK-20 keep their version 0.2 meaning, except
RISK-02 and RISK-20, which are restated because sibling work is this program's work (§33.8). Their mitigations are
corrected where this version changed the mechanism, and each now has an earliest signal. RISK-21 onward are new.
The owner column names a role, not a person.

### 41.4 How the register is used

- **Review.** The register is read at every milestone exit by the fresh-context session that records the exit
  (§43.2). For each row the session records whether the earliest signal has fired.
- **Escalation.** A fired signal ends in one of three recorded outcomes: a kill gate decided, an ADR that changes a
  mechanism or a scope, or a written reason why neither applies. A fired signal with no record is a defect of the
  exit review.
- **Growth.** A new risk continues the series. A risk that can no longer occur is tombstoned with the gate that
  retired it and is not renumbered.
- **No risk is mitigated by a hope.** A mitigation column names a mechanism with a gate, a fallback named in advance,
  or an owner decision with a fail-closed default. An upstream work item is never a mitigation by itself; its interim
  posture is (RISK-20).

### 41.5 Four risks that follow from late foundation facts

**What it is.** [S] Four rows for the register of §41.3, in its columns. Each arises from a fact recorded in §23,
§33, §34 or §39, each has an earliest signal that an existing check already produces, and none is covered by a row
that is already in the register. Identifiers are assigned with the rest of the series.

| Risk | Severity | Earliest signal | Mitigation | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A dependency feature changes canonical bytes: a sibling that enters the build graph switches the JSON library to insertion-ordered maps or to another number representation, and digests of unchanged artifacts move | High | `xtask check-deps` reports a unified feature set of the JSON library that differs from the stack lock; a golden digest changes with no change to its artifact | Canonical bytes come only from this project's writer; the four-way feature build of §34; the stack lock records the feature set | Workspace lead |
| An exact version pin in a sibling blocks an oracle: two siblings require different exact versions of one package, so they cannot share a build graph | Medium | Dependency resolution reports two exact requirements on one package; the admission gate of the oracle cannot build | The oracle runs as a worker process in its own workspace (§33.14); the pin move is an upstream work item (FD-FTX-01, FD-F3D-01) | Suite lead |
| A sampler has correct marginals and a wrong joint law, so the likelihood ratio is computed for a variable that was not sampled and exploration is correlated across channels | High | A pairwise sign-agreement frequency outside ½ ± 0.005 in the sampler battery; a learning curve that changes when channels are reordered | Rule P-12 and its gate (§23); counter-based draws keyed per channel; no sibling sampler is linked | Cortex lead |
| A rare slow mission is absent from the sealed sample, and a resampling interval certifies a ratio the population does not have | High | The pre-analysis of §39 reports a family count below the count its registered bound needs; every sealed mission of an arm finishes near its fastest time | The bounded paired contrast; the two result types of §39; a stratum below the necessary count reports a finite-suite result | Gauntlet lead |

DESIGN: the detector of each row is exercised by a planted instance in the negative-control registry (§38), so the
signal is known to fire: a dummy dependency that enables the two library features; a second exact pin on one
package; the planted linear-phase sampler; the rare-tail arm of the ten-fold pre-analysis.

Counterexample to the shortcut "a passing build means the pins are compatible": a build that never enables the
oracle's feature flag resolves, and the conflict appears only when the flag is first turned on at the oracle's
milestone. The resolution check therefore runs with every optional feature group enabled.

## 42. Open questions

An open question is a decision the plan has not taken, written so that not taking it is safe. This chapter states
the rule every question obeys, lists the questions only the owner can answer, and then registers every open
question of the plan by subsystem. Labels: every row is OPEN; a number in a default column is a DESIGN default or a
TARGET, never a measurement.

### 42.1 The decision rule

Every OPEN has an owner, a deadline expressed as the gate or milestone it blocks, a fail-closed default, and the
evidence that would decide it. Nothing is decided by silence: at its deadline an undecided question takes its
default, and the default is recorded as an ADR. Five clauses make the rule operational.

1. **A default removes a claim or a capability. It never adds one.** "GPU results are labelled exploratory", "no
   pretraining", "`reality: no-claim`" and "refuse" are defaults. "Assume the catalogue price" is not.
2. **A question is asked one milestone before the gate it blocks.** The owner-input line of each milestone in §43
   lists the questions due. A question that reaches its deadline at its default is reported in the exit review
   with the capability it removed.
3. **Evidence decides where evidence exists.** A question whose row names a gate, a profile or a pilot is decided
   by that measurement and not by preference. Only the questions of §42.2 are decided by the owner's judgement.
4. **A closed question is tombstoned, not reused.** Its identifier stays in the register with the ADR that closed it.
5. **This register adopts the identifiers the chapters defined.** A chapter's text governs the mechanism behind a
   question, and §40 governs any threshold a question touches. Where a chapter named no owner, the lead of its
   subsystem owns the question.

The register holds 147 questions: 141 raised in §12 to §37, of which four are closed, and six at program level.
OPEN-PROG-1 and OPEN-GAUNT-1 are carried from version 0.2. OPEN-PROG-2 to OPEN-PROG-5 are new. The questions that
§38 and §39 raise are adopted under the same rule with the owners and defaults those chapters state:
OPEN-GAUNT-2 to -8 and OPEN-TENFOLD-3 to -9. OPEN-TENFOLD-1 and -2 are OPEN-PROG-2. With these fourteen the
register holds 161.

### 42.4 What the defaults add up to

If every question stayed at its default, the program would still exit M0 to M5 and M7. DESIGN: that is the test a
default must pass before it is written. The resulting product would be a CPU-first studio with exploratory GPU
results, no family policy, cheap rungs that only discard, generic cards and assumed norms, no Reality claim, a
ten-fold ratio labelled `self-adjudicated`, and a private repository. Every one of those limits would be printed on
the results it touches. The owner's answers in §42.2 are therefore the difference between that product and the one
this plan describes, and the six that matter most, in the order they fall due, are OPEN-SPARK-1 and OPEN-SPARK-2
at M0, OPEN-PROG-4 at M1, OPEN-PROG-2 at M2, OPEN-CORTEX-1 at M3 and OPEN-PROG-1 before the pins are frozen for M7.

Four questions are closed. OPEN-SKEL-1 was closed by ADR-SKEL-02 and OPEN-AUGUR-6 by ADR-WS-02; both identifiers
are retired. OPEN-SUITE-2 and OPEN-TETHER-1 were decided by the owner on 2026-11-22: one toolchain T for the whole
build graph, fastmcp_rust brought onto T by FD-FMCP-01, and `frob-mcp` a member of the core graph that runs verbs in
process (§33.13, §32.12.2). Both identifiers stay in the register with the decision. Four defaults are confirmed by
the gate register and are open only to new evidence: the anchored cell of OPEN-NUM-3, the parity tolerance of
OPEN-PERF-1, the stricter threshold pair of OPEN-REFLEX-2, and the single revalidation engine of OPEN-ATEL-4.

# PART VIII. DELIVERY

## 43. Milestones M0–M8

A milestone is a set of demonstrations with recorded values, not a date. This chapter gives the shape of the
program, the rules for an exit, and one subsection per milestone with the same seven fields: purpose, artifact,
what it demonstrates, acceptance, kill gates decided, owner input wanted, and the decision to stop or re-plan.
Labels: thresholds repeated here are TARGETs and §40 governs them; week counts are DESIGN planning estimates;
North-Star numbers follow §7.

### 43.1 The shape of the program, and why M1 is a CPU studio

The first wedge is chosen for the same reason FrankenMining chose its own: start where value is deliverable with
the fewest unproven dependencies. **M1 is a design studio on the CPU referee tier, with the first mission slice.** It
needs only FrankenSim, asupersync and FrankenSQLite (§33.7). It already demonstrates the thesis in small: a typed
design, static analyses from Lie theory, a synthesized controller, a rollout on the transactional referee,
structured telemetry, and a mission query answered over a family of designs with a certificate that an independent
auditor re-checks, all through one verb registry. GPUs arrive at M2 on top of something that already works.

Three further reasons belong to this version of the plan.

1. **The result is not in the step.** §2.3 shows that an infinitely fast environment step cannot deliver the
   ten-fold ratio. The parts of the thesis that no GPU can rescue (what an answer is, how it is checked, how an
   amendment withdraws it) are exercised at M1 on fixtures whose answers are known exactly (NS-13, NS-22).
2. **The rival is measured while M1 is built.** M0 and M1 time the incumbent loop on `trj` (§2.7), so M2's engine
   work is funded against a measured denominator and not against a published one.
3. **A CPU studio survives every admission failure.** If the GPU, symbolic and proof foundations all failed
   admission, M1 would still ship (§33.7).

The order of evidence follows §2.7: measure the rival (M0, M1), put the mission slice on the CPU (M1), run the
rank-agreement experiment as soon as two rungs exist (a pilot on incumbent tools by M3, on our tiers at M4), hold a
partial ten-fold gate (M3), and run the tournament (M7).

| M | Name | Critical path | Planning estimate, elapsed weeks for a swarm | Exit is defined by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M0 | Spine and airlock | Yes | 2 | The admission records, one kernel on three backends, and the incumbent phase ledger on `trj` |
| M1 | Referee studio and first mission slice, CPU only | Yes | 5 | NS-01, NS-07 and the docking scenario demonstrated; the schedule gate (BET-12, §40.5) met |
| M2 | Batch, backends, families | Yes | 6 | Kill decisions for the kernel toolchain, contact, Metal and mixed batches recorded as ADRs |
| M3 | Places, tasks, adversaries, qualification | Yes | 6 | The partial ten-fold gate (GATE-TENFOLD-06) recorded, whatever the ratio |
| M4 | Amortized control, co-design, mission queries at scale | Yes | 8 | Rank agreement measured; the family-policy bets decided |
| M5 | Proofs, reality, manufacture | No; may overlap M4 | 6 | The Reality lane has a record or a recorded no-claim |
| M6 | Frontier physics | No | Per epic, 2 to 6 each | Per-epic plans and kill gates |
| M7 | The ten-fold tournament | Yes; needs M4, not M5 or M6 | 6, including a two-week freeze and rehearsal | The measured ratio published with its phase ledger (GATE-TENFOLD-07) |
| M8 | Frontier delivery | No | Per epic | Per-epic plans and stop rules |

The estimates exist to make BET-12 testable. They are not acceptance evidence and no gate cites them. The critical
path M0 to M4 and M7 sums to 33 weeks. M0 plus M1 is 7 weeks, so the schedule gate asks its question if they take
more than 10.5 weeks for the cause BET-12 names. M5 does not gate M7: a sealed stratum that needs a mechanism of M5
or M6 which has not landed is declared `not run` in the tournament report, with the reason.

### 43.2 Exit rules, and the dependency firewall in brief

An exit is recorded by a fresh-context session that did not implement the milestone (§38). It requires all of the
following.

- **Every gate of the milestone has a recorded value.** A failing value is a record. A kill gate that fired is
  recorded as an ADR with the fallback now in force, and the capability is described by the fallback's name
  from then on (§0.2).
- **Every demonstration runs from a clean checkout**, through `frob --json` and, where the registry exposes the
  verb to agents, through `frob-mcp`.
- **GATE-GAUNT-01 holds**: every gate that passed has a registered negative control that it catches.
- **Every report prints its `reality:` line** (GATE-GROUND-01, from M1 onward).
- **The risk register has been read** (§41.4), and the open questions due have been answered or have taken their
  defaults (§42.1).

A gate may pass before its milestone. It may not move later without an ADR. §40 fixes each gate's milestone and
threshold; the lists below name the key gates, and where a list and the register differ, the register governs. A
milestone does not exit on a count of gates. Its exit line in §43.1 is the observable. An admission is never
inherited: a foundation or an airlock group first used at a milestone is admitted at that milestone, by its own
record, at the pin of that day (§33.6). At most four [M] items are active at once in any milestone (D-6).

The dependency firewall is detailed in §33.7. In brief:

| M | Needs | Uses if admitted | If a foundation is missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| M0 | Nothing is relied on. The one toolchain T is chosen. FrankenSim, asupersync, FrankenSQLite, FrankenTorch's Metal gateway, `cudarc`, FrankenSymPy, fastmcp_rust and franken_numpy are admitted. The two P0 upstream work items are done in their repositories: FD-FMCP-01 (fastmcp_rust onto T) and FD-ASUP-01 (one asupersync version) | — | A failed admission is the result, and its fallback is decided here |
| M1 | FrankenSim (referee, geometry, ledger, memo store), asupersync (jobs, lab runtime), FrankenSQLite (ledger) | FrankenSymPy, fastmcp_rust, franken_numpy, frankenscipy | CLI only; no kernel certificates. The mission slice is unaffected, because `frob-verify` uses the standard library alone |
| M2 | FrankenSim (parity oracle), asupersync (device jobs), `cudarc`, FrankenTorch (Metal backend, gradient oracle), FrankenSymPy (derived kernels), franken_numpy (small-matrix oracle) | — | The no-GPU variant of §43.5; KILL-KIR; KILL-METAL |
| M3 | FrankenSim (optimizers, racing, statistics, spectral), asupersync (daemon), FrankenSQLite (qualification ledger), fastmcp_rust (full MCP) | franken_numpy (the Gymnasium adapter), frankentui, franken_threed, drone-reconstruction schemas | Local implementations against the same known answers (OPEN-ATEL-3); KILL-MCP; KILL-TUI; plain Three.js |
| M4 | FrankenSim (optimizers, archive, surrogates), FrankenTorch (policy interchange), FrankenSymPy (exact synthesis lane), fastmcp_rust (mission tools) | — | The numerical lane of KILL-SYNTH-LINKAGE; policies are exchanged in the native checkpoint format only |
| M5 | FrankenSim (structural, variational, as-built, manufacture), FrankenSymPy (coverage), franken_lean (capsules) | Drone reconstruction (scan import) | KILL-LEMMA; KILL-REFLECT; KILL-INGEST; the Foundry kill gates |
| M6 | FrankenSim's multiphysics bridge | franken_textiles as a cloth oracle [M] | The epic is not funded |
| M7 | Every pin and T frozen for the length of the tournament | fastmcp_rust for rival access | A pin move or a toolchain train voids the runs it spans |
| M8 | — | franken_firmware as a pattern [M] | The epic is not funded |

### 43.3 M0: spine and airlock

- **Purpose.** Retire the risks that could invalidate the architecture or the thesis, with the smallest possible
  amount of code. Two questions are answered by measurement: can the foundations be consumed from outside their
  trees, and is the rival's loop what §2.2 composes from published figures. No subsystem is built out.
- **Artifact.**
  - `frob doctor` lists the admitted foundations with their records and the stack receipt.
    `DEPENDENCY_ADMISSION.md` holds every record, passing or failing, the toolchain matrix of §33.12 and the
    choice of T.
  - fastmcp_rust builds on T in its own repository, with its test suite and its MCP conformance checks passing
    (FD-FMCP-01). FrankenSim's constellation, FrankenTorch and fastmcp_rust pin one published asupersync version
    (FD-ASUP-01).
  - `frob sim run g1 --tier referee --seconds 2` produces a state digest equal to the one FrankenSim computes
    for itself. The same job through `frob-fsim-worker` returns equal chunk digests.
  - `frob spark probe` and `frob spark fingerprint` run on both device families. `K-cay-step` runs from one
    source on `batch-cpu`, CUDA and Metal. The exact and guarded predicate kernels give identical bytes on all
    three.
  - T-01, T-03 and T-04 have certificates that replay offline. The claim-product type and the no-authorization
    flags exist in `frob-core`, with compile-fail tests.
  - The M0 verbs answer through `frob --json` and through `frob-mcp`, which is built in the core graph on T,
    links `frob-verbs` and runs the verbs in process.
  - The incumbent phase ledger on `trj`: cold start, a parameter edit and a topology edit to the first step, and
    time to the return threshold on one and two cards, at pinned revisions, each with a disclosure block.
  - The plan-time pilots re-run in this repository and recorded for Appendix K: the stance enumeration, the
    docking grid, the pusher battery, the reachable-verdict enumeration of the fixed-n rule, the boundary screen
    in guarded single precision, the ceiling of the solver comparison, and the power of the draft decision rule.
- **Demonstrates.** No North-Star scenario is tagged M0. The milestone delivers the two measurements the program
  stands on: BET-04 (consumption by path) and the denominator of BET-13.
- **Acceptance.** Admission: INT-TOOLCHAIN-01, INT-FSIM-01, INT-FSIM-02 to -11, INT-FSIM-18, INT-ASUP-01,
  INT-FSQL-01, INT-FT-01, -02, INT-CUDA-01, INT-FSYM-01, -02, INT-FNP-01, -02, and INT-FMCP-01: `frob-mcp` builds
  in the core graph on T with one asupersync package, lists the tools generated from the verb registry and passes
  the MCP protocol smoke test over stdio and HTTP. Upstream: FD-FMCP-01 and FD-ASUP-01 have landed in their
  repositories, or KILL-MCP is decided.
  Marrow: GATE-MARROW-01 for SO(3) and SE(3). Spark: GATE-SPARK-00, -01, -07, -08. Lemma: GATE-LEMMA-00, -06.
  Tether: GATE-TETHER-03. Workspace: GATE-WS-01, -04. Parity baseline: the `trj` rows of GATE-SPARK-21 that need
  no agent, which the parity-baseline gate GATE-TENFOLD-01 reads into the first phase ledger (§40.5); the whole of
  GATE-SPARK-21 closes at M1, and its rows on this Mac close no later than M1. GATE-GAUNT-01.
- **Kill gates decided here.** KILL-FSIM, then rolling. Fallback (a): a pinned FrankenSim worker process per
  device that exchanges whole jobs, already exercised by INT-FSIM-18. Fallback (b), only if (a) fails: lift the
  minimal referee set with provenance. KILL-MCP, between M0 and M1: it fires only if INT-FMCP-01 cannot pass
  within the M0 budget after FD-FMCP-01 and FD-ASUP-01 have been attempted. Fallback 1: `frob-mcp` as its own
  workspace, talking to `frobd` over a local socket in newline-delimited JSON. Fallback 2: agents use the CLI,
  which is complete on its own. The choice of T and the `frob-units` decision follow the rules of §33.12 and
  §33.13 from the recorded matrix.
- **Owner input wanted.** OPEN-SPARK-1 and OPEN-SPARK-2 (the envelope classes); OPEN-PROG-1 before the first
  push; OPEN-SUITE-3 and OPEN-SUITE-5; the comparator revisions of OPEN-PERF-2.
- **Stop decision.** Re-plan before M1 if INT-FSIM-01 cannot pass within two weeks and the worker process also
  fails INT-FSIM-18, because the only route left is a lift from a closure of about 1.5 million lines (FACT,
  §33.2). Rewrite §2 before any work is funded against it if the measured ledger puts the ceilings of §2.3 under
  3 for every mission class of §2.6. Drop a device family from M2 if the probe shows that it can hold no
  controlled determinism class. None of these stops the CPU studio except the first.
- **Work packages.** WP-01 to WP-06, WP-34 to WP-37.

  mission class withdraws the speed claim for that class. Under 3 on every class, speed work is no longer
  funded, the product is positioned on replay, qualification, certificates and the evidence ledger, and the
  family-policy spend of M4 is decided again. Where the composed-incumbent arm is within a factor of 1.5, the
  layer ships over that engine for the stratum (BET-14). Separately: if GATE-QUAL-01 fails, nothing is called
  qualified, and confirmation falls back to fixed-n exact studies with a hard cap on submissions before any
  tournament is scheduled.
- **Work packages.** WP-23 to WP-27, WP-53 to WP-60.

### 43.7 M4: amortized control, co-design, mission queries at scale

- **Purpose.** Build the two levers that carry the thesis, deciding many designs per turn and training few of
  them, and extend mission queries from CPU fixtures to families on the GPU.
- **Artifact.**
  - Family policies per morphology class (`frob train family`, `frob policy apply`), inheritance along design
    edits (`frob train inherit`) and distillation (`frob train distill`).
  - The rank-agreement record per class and task family (`frob eval rank-agreement`) and the ladder that
    allocates by it (`frob opt cascade`), with the audit lane and the planted winner.
  - Equivariant policies under the observation-preserving subgroup; gait orbits with continuation
    (`frob gait orbit`, `frob gait continue`).
  - Optimization, racing and the quality-diversity archive (`frob opt start`, `frob opt archive`);
    `frob design bisect`; registered predictions; the co-design cascade and the decision cores DC-01 to DC-11.
  - Mission queries over design families on the GPU, with region certificates on small sub-boxes, monotone
    transport and product-system dominance; `frob result revalidate`.
  - Synthesis: `frob mission synthesize --strategy codesign`, `refine` and `linkage`.
  - Tyre laws, tracks, wheel-leg hybrids, moving surfaces and soil cards; the priced retrofit catalogue and
    its search (`frob scene retrofit`).
  - The energy-budget tier and runtime shields (`frob shield budget`, `frob shield fit`, `frob shield check`).
  - `frob experiment suggest` ranked by value of information; the agent-surface A/B; `frob solve run`; the fleet
    scheduler (`frob fleet plan`).
- **Demonstrates.** NS-05, NS-06, NS-08, NS-18, NS-19, NS-23, and NS-13 at scale.
- **Acceptance.** Cortex: GATE-CORTEX-03, -11, -12, -13, -14. Reflex, gaits and shields: GATE-REFLEX-04 for
  tracked and hybrid classes; GATE-REFLEX-06, -07, -08; GATE-GAIT-01, -02, -03; GATE-SHIELD-01 to -04. Atelier:
  GATE-ATEL-03, -07 to -10, -14, -15, -16, the bisect row of -04, and the rest of -02, -05, -11 and -13. Augur
  and Lemma: GATE-AUGUR-09, -11, -14 to -19; GATE-LEMMA-04 (repeated). Phylum, Nemesis and Autopsy:
  GATE-PHYLUM-06, -08; GATE-NEMESIS-07; GATE-AUTOPSY-08. Habitat, Traction, Spark and Marrow: GATE-HAB-11;
  GATE-TRAC-08; GATE-SPARK-13, -14; GATE-MARROW-04. Tether: GATE-TETHER-13. GATE-REFLEX-01 closes here for the
  tracked and hybrid archetypes. GATE-GAUNT-01. The register places GATE-HAB-11, GATE-SHIELD-01 and GATE-AUGUR-11
  here, with their mechanisms (§40.7).
- **Kill gates decided here.**
  - KILL-FAMILY: no family policy; specialists with inheritance from the nearest parent, and the baseline
    screens.
  - KILL-INHERIT and KILL-DISTILL: children train from the class prior or from scratch; distillation only from a
    privileged teacher.
  - KILL-RANK and KILL-LADDER: R1 is `uninformative` and every candidate that survives static analysis is scored
    on the higher rung; the fixed halving table allocates among trained candidates.
  - KILL-EQUIV: symmetry is used for augmentation and metamorphic testing only.
  - KILL-GAIT, KILL-MPC, KILL-RESIDUAL: orbits as diagnostics; the sampling controller as a debugging aid; no
    residual rung.
  - KILL-SHIELD and KILL-ENERGY: barrier rows become penalties and alarms, and nothing is called a shield; an
    energy claim that shows an exceedance is withdrawn and its monitor stays as an alarm.
  - KILL-RETROFIT: the catalogue stays as Nemesis's edit vocabulary and the search verb is withdrawn.
  - Also decided: KILL-VOI, KILL-REUSE, KILL-FDGRAD, KILL-ATLAS, KILL-ALTALGO, KILL-SOLVE, KILL-FLEET,
    KILL-SPECIALIZE, KILL-FAMILYLANE, KILL-RESPONSE, KILL-SOIL, KILL-MARROW-BLOCKS, KILL-SYNTH-CODESIGN,
    KILL-SYNTH-TRAJOPT, KILL-SYNTH-LINKAGE, KILL-AUGUR-CUTS, KILL-AUGUR-DOMINANCE, KILL-AUGUR-LABELS.
- **Owner input wanted.** OPEN-CORTEX-1 if still open. OPEN-SINEW-1 and the other catalogue questions.
  OPEN-SAFE-3. OPEN-TETHER-5. OPEN-NEMESIS-3. OPEN-PROG-5 before M5 closes.
- **Stop decision.** If KILL-RANK fires for every class and KILL-FAMILY fires as well, the lever "train few" is
  gone. The ceilings of §2.3 are then recomputed with the measured trained fraction, every class whose ceiling is
  under 3 leaves the speed claim, and the sealed suite of M7 is re-stratified before it is sealed. M7 still
  runs, because its result is published whatever it is. Specialized GPU work stops in any cell where the timing
  of slice 4 of §25.23 shows that transfers, authoring, training, checking or the rival's reuse rule out the
  target.
- **The variant with no family policy.** DESIGN: M4 can exit without one. It applies if OPEN-CORTEX-1 stays at
  its default, if the pre-funding pilot meets its falsifier, or if KILL-FAMILY fires. The rungs are then the
  static check, the baseline controller, the sampling controller, gait orbits, and per-design specialists that
  inherit from the nearest parent. The ladder runs per class in the mode its measured rank agreement permits
  (GATE-REFLEX-04), which is `uninformative` until a record exists (§28.10). GATE-CORTEX-11 is recorded as failed or
  `not run`, BET-15 as falsified or untested, NS-19 is not demonstrated, and §39 records the factor that was
  lost. Every other artifact of the milestone lands unchanged.
- **Work packages.** WP-28 to WP-30, WP-61 to WP-67.

### 43.8 M5: proofs, reality, manufacture

- **Purpose.** Strengthen what can be trusted and what can be built. None of it shortens the time to a decision
  (§2.5), so none of it gates M7.
- **Artifact.**
  - Certificate coverage across derived kernels (`frob prove kernel`, `frob prove bundle`); Lean theorem
    capsules re-checked by FrankenLean; the reflection pilot (`frob prove reflect`); replay of a qualification
    campaign by `frob-verify`.
  - The articulated variational integrator on the referee and the `strict` profile; the hard-contact batch law
    on `batch-cpu`.
  - Ground: `frob ground ingest`, `excite`, `identify`, `predict`, `score`, `band` and `kit`, exercised first on
    the synthetic rehearsal; the first real cell if data is admitted.
  - Real-place ingestion: `frob scene import`, `frob scene fit`, `frob scene probe-request`; asset-populated
    interiors, if their pilot funds them; the tree-operator route as a pilot.
  - Foundry: `frob foundry loads`, `size`, `optimize`, `check`, `tolerance` and `export`, ending in a `.fbuild`
    packet whose four flags are false.
- **Demonstrates.** NS-11, NS-12, NS-20, NS-21.
- **Acceptance.** Lemma: INT-FLN-01, -02; GATE-LEMMA-01, -02, -05; GATE-QUAL-03. Kinesis and Traction:
  GATE-TRAC-09 on `batch-cpu` (§18.17 admits those rows from M3; the GPU rows are M6). Habitat: GATE-HAB-03.
  Ground: GATE-GROUND-02 to -09; GATE-GROUND-10 is tied to no milestone and is recorded when data is admitted
  (§40.6). Foundry: GATE-FOUNDRY-01 to -10, with INT-FSIM-15 for the structure group. Admission: INT-FDGR-01 for
  scan import. Formats: GATE-WS-02 complete for all thirteen. GATE-GAUNT-01. Four of these are tagged M4 by their
  chapters and may pass there: GATE-FOUNDRY-01 to -03 and GATE-GROUND-03.
- **Kill gates decided here.** KILL-LEMMA: certificates become exact-rational randomized tests recorded as
  `Tested`. KILL-REFLECT: instance certificates stay `Certified` and reflection is parked. KILL-VARIATIONAL: the
  free-body step as oracle and the default integrator everywhere. KILL-HARDCONTACT: fixed-iteration island
  solvers with a residual flag, and the law kept as a specification and a model-form arm. KILL-GROUND,
  KILL-BAND, KILL-CLOCK, KILL-ASBUILT, KILL-KIT: Ground keeps admission, frozen predictions, direct measurements
  and time-free metrics, withdraws bands, and reports `reality: no-claim`. KILL-INGEST: a surveyed proxy
  authored in the interior grammar. KILL-DRESSING: structural proxies and static clutter only. KILL-LOADS,
  KILL-TOPOPT, KILL-FAB, KILL-TOLERANCE, KILL-PACKET: load cases declared by hand, beam sizing, advisory lints,
  worst-case boxes, and a packet reduced to a parts list, mass properties and STL. KILL-TREEOP and
  KILL-SKEL-PORT: the dense factorization and a cap of 64 degrees of freedom.
- **Owner input wanted.** OPEN-GAUNT-1 and OPEN-GROUND-2. OPEN-HAB-5. OPEN-FOUNDRY-2 and OPEN-SKEL-2.
- **Stop decision.** Nothing here stops the program: every lane has a fallback that ships under its own name,
  and the exit is a record or a recorded no-claim. Lanes stop singly. Work on Lemma beyond the coverage gate is
  not funded further before M7 if no consumed certificate has changed a decision by this exit (OPEN-LEMMA-5).
  Ground work beyond the rehearsal waits if no dataset has been admitted.
- **Work packages.** WP-31, WP-32, WP-68 to WP-72.

### 43.9 M6: frontier physics

- **Purpose.** Admit the physics that makes more failures visible, behind feature flags and off the critical
  path. Each epic needs its own short plan, its paper-scale pilot and its kill gate before work starts.
- **Artifact.** Epics, in the default order of funding: robot-advected films, payload slosh, and cable and rug
  proxies [F]; then Cosserat rods, cloth and coupled islands on the CPU referee for finalists [M]; soft soil at
  scale; the hard-contact law on devices; the tree-operator route and the mesh path on devices, where their
  pilots at M5 and M3 kept them [F]; tactile sensing [M]; the rotor port [M]; RGB and splat scenes; moving
  people; gradients through contact with their validity labels; the holonomy and symmetry-at-contact queries of
  §25; lifecycle compression [M].
- **Demonstrates.** No North-Star scenario is tagged M6. Each epic's plan names its own acceptance story, and
  the Frontier half of BET-36 is tested here.
- **Acceptance.** GATE-HAB-07, -08, -09; GATE-AUGUR-20, -21; the device rows of GATE-TRAC-09; GATE-FOUNDRY-12,
  which §31.19 tags M8 and which closes with its epic; INT-FSIM-17; INT-FTX-01, with the cloth oracle run as a
  worker process (§33.17); the known answers each epic's chapter lists.
- **Kill gates decided here.** KILL-LIVING: Solid and Frontier proxies only, and no islands. KILL-ADVECT: static
  film-friction patches, and advection is not built. KILL-SLOSH: rigid ballast with a spill metric. KILL-PROXY: Solid
  proxies in training. KILL-SINEW-ROTOR and KILL-SINEW-AGE: the
  rotor port is withdrawn; ageing factors are constants. KILL-LIFECYCLE: aged model variants at hand-specified
  wear states. KILL-AUGUR-PHASE and KILL-AUGUR-SYMEVENT: the forward diagnostic and per-event finite
  differences.
- **Owner input wanted.** OPEN-PROG-5 and OPEN-AUGUR-10: which epics are funded, in which order, under the cap of
  four active [M] items.
- **Stop decision.** An epic stops when its pilot's falsifier holds or its kill gate fires. The whole milestone
  pauses whenever M4 or M7 is slipping, since nothing here is on their path.
- **Work packages.** WP-33, WP-73 to WP-75.

### 43.10 M7: the ten-fold tournament

- **Purpose.** Measure the thesis against the strongest composed rival, and publish the measured result whatever
  it is.
- **Artifact.** The sealed suite in named strata. Every pin frozen. The rival arms: the strongest composed
  incumbent workflow, tuned on development fixtures and then frozen, and our own layer over the incumbent engine
  where the verbs allow it. Neutral adjudication with receipts released after both arms close. The report: per
  stratum, the ratio of restricted mean times with its interval, cold and warm runs separately, the crossover
  reuse count, a phase ledger for each arm that sums to wall-clock, the audit of every submitted certificate by
  `frob-verify`, the tie statement, and the count of certificates that changed a decision.
- **Demonstrates.** NS-24.
- **Acceptance.** The program gates of §40.5: GATE-TENFOLD-03, -04, -05 and -11 repeated before the sealed suite is
  opened; the tournament, GATE-TENFOLD-07; the replication kit, GATE-TENFOLD-08; suite hygiene, GATE-TENFOLD-12;
  and the recovery ratios of GATE-TENFOLD-13 on the sealed suite. Exit is the publication of the measured ratio
  with its phase ledger. GATE-GAUNT-01.
- **Kill gates decided here.** No mechanism is killed at M7. Three written rules are applied: the decision rule
  of BET-13 and its wording for each range of the ratio; the tie rule of BET-14; and disqualification of an arm
  from the scoped claim by one false certificate.
- **Owner input wanted.** OPEN-PROG-2, the neutral party and the adjudicating simulator, confirmed before the
  suite is sealed. OPEN-PROG-1. The envelope for the tournament itself (§44.2).
- **Stop decision.** A tournament is not stopped by an interim number. It is voided and re-run only for a breach
  of protocol: a pin moved during the freeze, sealed material read by an arm, or a rival arm changed after its
  freeze. After publication the positioning follows BET-13: the product is described by its measured ratio per
  stratum, and by auditability where the ratio is under 3.
- **Work packages.** WP-76, WP-77.

### 43.11 M8: frontier delivery

- **Purpose.** Deliver the Moonshot items that would make the product unlike anything else, each behind a flag
  and each with a stop rule. The plan works without every one of them.
- **Artifact.** Epics: facility co-design and multi-robot handoff (slice 5 of §25.23); skill transport with
  learned residuals; continuation-based synthesis on the CPU; firmware export; geometric-algebra tree policies
  at scale; reachable-set tables for shields; the fused per-world step kernel.
- **Demonstrates.** No North-Star scenario is tagged M8.
- **Acceptance.** GATE-AUGUR-22, -23, -24; GATE-REFLEX-09; GATE-CORTEX-17; GATE-SHIELD-05; GATE-FOUNDRY-11.
- **Kill gates decided here.** KILL-AUGUR-FACILITY: single-robot missions with priced world edits.
  KILL-AUGUR-TRANSPORT and KILL-SKILL: family policies and inheritance; the exact skill layer and its
  witnesses. KILL-SYNTH-CONT: the exact lane with multi-start recovery, labelled `Partial`. KILL-GATREE: the
  plain morphology transformer. KILL-TUBE: reduced-order barriers. KILL-FIRMWARE: controller parameters and
  test vectors, and no code. KILL-MEGA: the staged step plan, which is the design of record.
- **Owner input wanted.** Funding per epic, and an envelope of class E3 for any pretraining.
- **Stop decision.** Per epic, by its stop rule. An epic that has not passed its pilot within its planned weeks
  returns to the register of Appendix C and frees its slot under the cap.
- **Work packages.** WP-78 to WP-80.

### 43.12 No milestone is blocked by one failed bet

DESIGN: for every bet that a milestone tests, the milestone has an exit that does not need the bet to hold. The
fallback ships under its own name, and the lost capability is recorded.

| M | Bet or decision that could fail | The milestone still exits with |
|---|---|---|
| M0 | BET-04: FrankenSim is consumable by path | The worker process; the lift only if that fails |
| M0 | INT-FMCP-01 cannot pass within the M0 budget after FD-FMCP-01 and FD-ASUP-01 have been attempted | KILL-MCP: `frob-mcp` as its own workspace over a local socket to `frobd`; then the CLI, which is complete on its own |
| M1 | A symbolic, proof or GPU foundation fails admission | The same M1: it needs FrankenSim, asupersync and FrankenSQLite only |
| M1 | BET-19 on the first slice: a conventional program answers the docking query as well | That program behind the same verbs, schema and checker |
| M2 | OPEN-SPARK-1 unratified, or both device families fail | The no-GPU variant (§43.5) |
| M2 | BET-18: mixed batches lose | Per-family templates with per-world parameter variants |
| M2 | BET-09: Metal is not a rollout tier | CUDA trains; the Mac keeps the world bank, proof, replay and `batch-cpu` |
| M2 | BET-34: the referee covers too little | The `strict` profile as named adjudicator, with results that say so |
| M3 | BET-06: baselines fail on many morphologies | The sampling fallback and training for the classes that fail |
| M3 | BET-21: the blinded lane does not hold its error rate | Fixed-n exact confirmation with a cap on submissions |
| M3 | BET-22, BET-23: adversarial search or attribution underperforms | Randomization with shrinking and the guard; single-factor re-runs |
| M3 | No neutral party is named (OPEN-PROG-2) | A partial gate labelled `self-adjudicated` |
| M4 | BET-15, or no compute envelope (OPEN-CORTEX-1) | The variant with no family policy (§43.7) |
| M4 | BET-17: rank agreement is low | Cheap rungs that discard only; the fixed halving table |
| M4 | BET-20: region certificates decide too little | Dual witnesses, monotone bounds and sampled coverage labelled `Estimated` |
| M5 | BET-11: certificate coverage is unaffordable | Exact-rational randomized tests recorded as `Tested` |
| M5 | BET-28, or no data arrives | `reality: no-claim`, recorded as the state |
| M5 | BET-29: generative structure saves too little | Beam sizing and the structural margin analysis |
| M7 | BET-13: the ratio is under ten | The measured ratio, published per stratum with the wording BET-13 fixes |
| M7 | BET-14: the composed incumbent ties | The layer over that engine for the stratum, and a report that says so |

## 44. Work packages

A work package is the unit between a milestone and a bead: a deliverable with its crates, the gates that accept it
and the packages it waits for. "Depends on" is the coarse view of the bead graph in §45. After conversion to beads
this table is regenerated from the graph by transitive reduction, so the two cannot drift. WP-01 to WP-33 keep
their version 0.2 meaning; their crate and gate columns are extended to this version's content. WP-34 onward are
new. A tier tag on a package name marks Frontier or Moonshot content; a package tagged with two tiers also holds
Solid work, and the tier of each mechanism is in its chapter. The Frontier or Moonshot part of a package is funded
only after its paper-scale pilot is on record (§0.7), and its kill gate is decided at the milestone named in §43.
The gates column lists key gates; §40 holds the full assignment. Upstream work items (Appendix F) are not a package
of their own: each is a bead labelled `upstream` inside the package whose gate its switch-over rule re-runs, done in
the sibling's repository (§33.8). The two P0 items sit in WP-02 (FD-ASUP-01) and WP-06 (FD-FMCP-01).

## 45. The beads

These are the seed for conversion with `br`. Titles name the artifact. "Done when" is one observable, usually with a
negative control: a planted failure the bead must catch. Beads of M0 to M5 are tasks. Beads of M6, M7 and M8 are
epics, one per frontier item and one group for the ten-fold tournament; an epic is split into tasks when its milestone
opens, and part of its done-condition is that a short plan exists and its pilot has run (§0.7). Each milestone ends
with an exit review performed by a fresh-context session that did not implement the work. Every dependency points to a
lower-numbered bead. Every bead inherits §0.2 and the false-progress guards of §38.

How to read a row (DESIGN):

- **A gate identifier in "Done when"** means the gate's recorded value together with its caught negative control, as
  defined in the chapter that owns the gate and listed in §40. "Rows of", "on the referee" and "for the M2 verbs"
  restrict the bead to the part of the gate that can be measured when the bead closes. The gate's PASS is recorded
  when the last bead that cites it closes. Admission gates (INT-…) are read the same way, with the admission record of
  §33.6 as the value.
- **"Decided" after a kill gate** means that its trigger was evaluated on measured values and that the outcome, either
  way, is recorded as an ADR. A kill gate that fires replaces the bead's capability by the fallback named in advance.
  The bead then closes on the fallback, and its dependents are re-read against it (§45.11).
- **Numbers in a done-condition** are TARGET thresholds or exact known answers taken from the owning chapters. None is
  a measurement.
- **Placement.** A bead sits in the milestone that §43 assigns to its mechanism. Where a gate table names a different
  earliest milestone than the bead that closes the gate, §45.10 lists the difference, and the value is recorded when
  the bead closes.
- **Upstream work is bead work.** A change to a sibling is a bead of this graph with the label `upstream`, done in the
  sibling's repository under its own rules and mirrored as a bead in the sibling's tracker (§33.8). BD-037 opens the
  upstream work items of Appendix F, the two P0 items are part of BD-008 and BD-023, and every bead that stands on a
  sibling has an interim posture that holds until the upstream change lands.
- **Numbering.** The list is numbered from BD-001 so that the numbering is a topological order. BD-001 to BD-024 keep
  the subjects they had in version 0.2, with corrected content, so that §46 reads against the same numbers. Numbers
  above BD-024 are new assignments.

### 45.1 M0: spine and airlock

M0 retires the risks that could invalidate the architecture, with the smallest amount of code. Beyond the workspace,
the airlock and the one-kernel spike, it measures the rival before anything is built against it, re-runs the plan-time
pilots so that their numbers are this repository's own, and admits the four reported foundation defects as tests. M0
also chooses the one toolchain T of the whole build graph, brings fastmcp_rust onto it and aligns the consumed siblings
on one asupersync version, as upstream work in those repositories (§33.13). The MCP server is a member of the core
graph and runs verbs in process. `frob-cert` also builds alone: it has no dependency and its own stable compiler.

### 45.3 M2: batch, backends, families

M2 puts the batched step on `batch-cpu`, CUDA and Metal and decides by measurement the four questions the architecture
leaves open: whether the derivation toolchain carries the kernel arithmetic, whether the contact law is adequate,
whether Metal is a rollout tier, and whether mixed cohorts are the engine. The `strict` profile lands here (BD-161)
because it runs on the batched kernels; the strict rows of the M1 gates close with it.
