| 5 | `fs-mbd::Wrench` (`frankensim/crates/fs-mbd/src/lib.rs:1695–1701`) | A convention hazard, not a defect: the step's external wrench is `force_world` with `torque_body`, two frames in one value, unlike `fs_ga::Wrench` and unlike §11.1 | Confirmed by reading. The rigid-body type requires the body origin at the centre of mass (`lib.rs:582–595`) and applies the angular impulse as Δt·R̄·`torque_body` (`:1913`) | A body frame rotated by 90° about z: a body-frame force (1, 0, 0) N means a push along world y; copied unconverted into `force_world` it pushes along world x, with the same magnitude and energy, and nothing faults | The mixed-wrench probe of GATE-WS-06: a free body at R = R_z(90°) receives a pure world force and a pure body torque through the airlock, and the linear and angular momentum changes match to 10⁻¹²; the unconverted mutant fails | FD-FSIM-33 | `MixedWrench` in `frob-fsim` only, with exactly two constructors |

### F.3 What the upstream work items do not change

- M1 depends only on FrankenSim, asupersync and FrankenSQLite (§33.7). No upstream work item is on the M1 critical
  path.
- If no upstream work item has landed, the plan still ships: the referee lowers joints, owns its transaction and
  migrates witnesses; the Metal backend runs inside the gateway's present limits; and if the two P0 items cannot land
  within the M0 budget, KILL-MCP's fallbacks apply, `frob-mcp` as its own workspace over a local socket and then the
  CLI alone. The costs are named in the interim-posture column and in KILL-FSIM, KILL-METAL and KILL-MCP.
- An upstream change that lands is adopted only through its switch-over rule. A sibling's newer clean head is never
  rolled back locally, and neither a pin nor T moves during the ten-fold tournament (§39).

`registries/hazards/<archetype>.toml`; this table is their content at plan time.

**Every dimension below is `assumed`.** The ranges are generic values chosen to make scenes valid. No building code,
workplace regulation or product standard has been read for them, and none is cited. A row's provenance changes to
`norm: <citation>` or `measured: <dataset>` only when the source is recorded in Appendix H; a pack counts the `assumed`
dimensions it used (`dimensions_assumed` in its manifest); and a report that claims a scene is representative of real
buildings is refused while that count is non-zero (`FROB-REF-312`). OPEN-HAB-1 owns the search for cited norms. Rows

The known answer for a differential drive uses the closed form of F.2 row 2, not `fs-mbd::planar_drive`. Variants

## Appendix H. Source register

**Nothing in this plan was compiled, run or measured as FrankenRobotics.** No crate of this project exists. Every
statement about FrankenRobotics is DESIGN, HYPOTHESIS or TARGET. Every FACT is one of three things: a reading of local
source or documentation (H.2), a reading of a public source (H.3), or the result of a small program run at plan time
on a small model (H.5). A number taken from any of them is a FACT about its source and is re-read from the primary
source, or re-run at a pinned commit, before a gate cites it.

### H.1 Marks

Each public source carries the mark its planning record gave it. The marks say how the text reached the reader, not
how reliable the source is.

| Mark | Meaning |
|---|---|
| P | Read from the primary text: a PDF converted to text, a raw file at a release tag, or a raw documentation page |
| S | Reported through a summary: the page was read through a summarizing fetch tool, and quotes are short for that reason |
| F | Fetched during planning; the record does not say whether the text was raw or summarized. Treated as S |
| R | A search-engine summary only; the page was not opened |
| M | Recalled, not re-read |
| U | Cited with no mark recorded |

Where two records disagree the weaker mark is kept, except that a source re-read by the independent audits is P for
the figures those audits quote. Only P sources may be cited by a gate without a further reading; every other mark is
a reading task that the gate's bead performs first.

### H.4 Standard references cited from background knowledge and not re-fetched

Each MUST be confirmed against its primary source before a gate cites it.

- Carried: Featherstone, *Rigid Body Dynamics Algorithms*; Park, Bobrow and Ploen on Lie-group robot dynamics; Murray,
  Li and Sastry; Lynch and Park; Hervé on displacement subgroups; Iserles, Munthe-Kaas, Nørsett and Zanna on Lie-group
  methods; Marsden and West on variational integrators; Lee, Leok and McClamroch; Wensing, Kim and Slotine on
  physically consistent inertia; Todorov on convex contact; Bloch, Krishnaprasad, Marsden and Murray on nonholonomic
  systems; Hatton and Choset; Buono and Golubitsky; Lopes et al. on max-plus gait models; Hartley et al. on
  contact-aided invariant filtering; Bullo and Lewis; Lee, Liu, Park and Srinivasa on linear-time variational
  integrators; Kobilarov, Crane and Desbrun on Cayley-based Lie-group integrators.
- Added by the mission and synthesis chapters: Bretl and Lall on static equilibrium with friction; Orsolino et al. on
  feasible regions; Fadini et al. on co-design; the Flow* reachability tool; the Scenic scenario language;
  decision-region determination; ASID; saltation matrices; contact-size dependence in gel indentation; Merlet, and
  Neumaier, on interval methods in design; the nine-point, Stewart–Gough and 6R solution counts; Burmester theory;
  Smale's α-theory.
- Added by the numerics chapters: Demmel, van der Sluis and Higham on scaling; Sterbenz's lemma; Schwartz–Zippel
  identity testing; the Clopper–Pearson interval.
- Added by the scene and sensing chapters: the squeeze-film formula; viscous-spreading exponents; linear sloshing
  frequencies; the right-angle corridor result; small-time local controllability of car-like bases; the glTF camera
  convention.
- Added by the control chapter: a published technical specification for collaborative robots that states transient
  contact limits through transferred energy. It is named as context only. No conformity is assessed against it (§22.11).

### H.5 Paper-scale checks that were run at plan time

Every row is FACT about a small program on a small model. None used FrankenSim dynamics, FrankenSim contact or a real
sensor pipeline; the native runs executed one scalar decision kernel. The programs and their outputs are in the
planning reproduction archive: the single `.zip` file in `/Users/jemanuel/projects/franken_robotics/planning/`, 241,568
bytes, SHA-256 `0326e89d76b88a2aa7d198d53556f80ab131fe5a902113dd37f7f32e93b09a4f`. Its runner replays the
standard-library checks with `python3 -B verify.py` and the full set with `--all` (§25.22 gives the inner paths).

| Check | What it measured | Result | Cited in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Static stance family | Two exact classifiers of body–load feasibility; a projection against a lifted robust program | 11,520 of 11,520 states agree; half-width 3/14 m from both programs; a support-polygon-plus-capacity screen wrongly accepts 1,596 bodies | §25.13, C-32 |
| Stance falsifier | The same body under equal passive springs | (175, 115, 85, 25) N against a 160 N rating | §25.13 |
| Material probe | Generated probe, programmed expert and direct measurement over 900 cases and four laws | 675 of 675 in class, 0 of 225 on the withheld law; direct dwell 900 of 900 | §25.14 |
| Pad family | Minimum certified mass for a 75 N pull | 300 g and 240 g at centred readings only; an admitted reading drops the bound to 73.79 N | §25.14 |
| Sensor aliasing | Exact Bayes success with repeated binary reads | 27/32, 459/512, 3807/4096; a shared error bit stays at 3/4 | §20.12, C-19 |
| Docking, two gains | Exact three-tick docking with one velocity packet | ε < (U + ½)/4; of 561 cells, 344 admitted, 217 excluded, nine on the boundary; 51 linear programs agree | §20.16, §25.15 |
| Docking, three gains | Adding the gain 33/32 | Exact docking unsatisfiable; 34,590 positive labels per grid reverse | §20.16 |
| Specialized against composed solver | Ten fixtures, six corrupted certificates | 20 of 20 intervals match in each arm; six of six bad certificates rejected; median time ratio 1.345 warm and 1.088 cold | §2, §25.22 |
| Timing ceiling of that test | The part of the specialized batch that the solver does not touch | A residual of 575.7 µs (parsing, assembly, checking, serialization and harness, not separately timed), the 610.1 µs full median less the 34.4 µs solve-only median: a zero-cost solver would reach about 1.46 warm (842.8 ÷ 575.7) | §2, D-17 |
| Labels and deadlines | Payload-width frontier against number and timing of labels | 3/32, 7/32, 11/32 mm for one, two, three early labels; one label unsatisfiable, two satisfiable | §25.18 |
| Decision reuse | A semantic receipt against a dependency graph over four edit states | A tie; omitting one dependency inherits a stale promotion | §28.13 |
| Shared bus | Two fingers on one unit-current bus | Zero one-tick schedules, two two-tick schedules; an additive peak rule falsely prunes | §14.6, §31.12 |
| Admission fixtures | Exact counterexamples for mass support, design-dependent load, information, symmetric actions, dependent stage outcomes | Each prints its counterexample | §25.4.7 |
| Boundary screen on three GPUs | A 65,536-row docking-boundary screen on the M5 Ultra and both RTX 4090 | Unguarded single precision: 452 false admissions, 23,438 false exclusions; guarded with exact fallback: zero final errors, identical bytes; exact integer kernels: zero errors | §13.7, §24.5, §35 |
| Static against dynamic sill | Sampled statics against a planar dynamic scorer, 156 cases | 94 agree; 62 static rejections succeed dynamically; an audit found scorer defects (a latched dwell timer, no strike guard) | §19.12, §24.10 |
| Sampled wheel loop | Spectral radius of the one-tick map of a 75 mm wheel with a current target held for 10 ms | 1.4820 with target-current feed-forward, 0.9207 with measured-current feed-forward; an instantaneous-current model gives 2.6917 for both with the fixture's shaft damping (2.7075 without it); an explicit current-then-wheel update at 0.5 ms gives 1.497 where 0.921 is right | §24.10, §28.4 (A-22) |
| Winding feed-forward term | R·i_ref against R·i in the planar threshold pilot | 24 of 156 outcome labels change | §30.9 |
| Fixed-n rule enumeration | Every outcome of the paired rule at n = 64 and a five-point margin | 2,145 count pairs: 521 promote, 521 inferior, 1,103 inconclusive, no tie; a tie first reachable at n = 86 | §24.12, §28.6 |
| Power of the draft decision rule | Monte Carlo of the earlier ten-fold rule (log-normal run times, 5 to 20 seeds) | About 18% power against a true ratio of 10 | §39 |
| Half-precision conditioning | κ·u for contact Hessians of three robots after unit-diagonal scaling, with u = 2⁻¹¹ | κ·u ≥ 1 on a large share of contact states, so refinement from a half-precision factor does not converge | §21.20 |
| Humanoid conditioning | κ₂ of the humanoid contact Hessian over 201 poses | 3·10⁴ to 1·10⁵ raw and 2·10³ to 9·10³ scaled, at default contact impedance | §35 |
| CPU incumbent rate on this Mac | A reference quadruped at 2 ms, double precision, 36 threads, under background load | About 410,000 steps/s | §36 |
| Metal device query | Working-set limit and largest buffer on this Mac | About 222.7 GiB and 167.0 GiB | §21.16, §36 |
| Worked numbers of the body chapters | Thermal card, shell masses and gyration radii, orbit counts, voltage closed forms, bus ceiling, gear fixture, backlash impact, the single-precision predicate | Recomputed by script | §13 to §15 |
| Worked artifacts of Appendix L | The stance family of L.4 in exact rationals on a 81 × 31 grid against its closed form; the paving of L.4; the binomial bounds of L.9 | Zero mismatches; one inner, three unresolved and eight excluded cells; bounds 0.0432, 0.0504, 0.0425, 0.0505 | Appendix L |

What these checks do not establish is as important. Every strong baseline tied or won: a lifted linear program tied the
projection, a scenario-tree program tied the docking family, a dependency graph tied the receipt, and quantifier
elimination produced the composed-solver answers directly for 8 of 12 queries. No physical claim follows from any row:
the material laws are artificial, the loads stipulated, the plants scalar or planar.

### H.6 Not verified, and not relied on

- Absolute MuJoCo Warp or Newton throughput on an RTX 4090. The published absolute figures are for an RTX 6000 Ada and
  an RTX 5090; the parity baseline is measured on `trj` at M0 and M1 (GATE-SPARK-21).
- The RTX 4090's double-precision ratio from a primary source, its memory bandwidth, and peer access between the two
  cards (OPEN-SPARK-6).
- Whether Metal's single-precision division and square root are correctly rounded and whether subnormals are flushed
  (GATE-SPARK-01, -07 measure them). 64-bit integer atomics are reported absent on Metal, to be re-run by the
  fingerprint (§21.26).
- Bandwidth, launch costs and compile times of both machines. Only core counts, memory sizes and the two Metal limits
  of H.2 are recorded.
- Rigid-body simulation by an incumbent on Apple silicon at stated throughput. A search found no benchmark.
- The reference-robot figures used as published anchors for Parity at M3. They are at search-summary level (R).
- Licences of ProcTHOR-10K data, Replica and YCB, and of the retail and warehouse generators of Appendix G.
- Ratification status of glTF physics extensions.
- Every hazard dimension of Appendix G and every retrofit price. No norm, regulation, standard or price list was read.
- The reported numbers of the five foundation defects (Appendix F.2) beyond what reading the source confirms: the
  ratio 1.582459, the zero-translation run and the wrong in-bounds read were not re-executed.
- Sources marked M or U in H.3, and the 18 claims the second audit left pending.
- Any Lean result. No theorem card has been checked; FrankenLean's module status is taken from its own receipt.
- Any statement about a physical robot.

## Appendix I. Type sketches

DESIGN. These sketches fix intent, not signatures. Where a chapter prints a sketch of the same type, the chapter
governs and this appendix repeats it; where two chapters sketch one type differently, the sketch here is their union
and the difference is named in a note. Field types that are not defined here (`Qty`, `Ratio`, `Blake3`, `ModelId` and
the other identities of §11) are the obvious ones.

### I.1 Groups, frames, cones and ports

```rust
/// A Lie group with two retractions. Its laws are G0 property tests (§13.8), not comments.
pub trait LieGroup: Copy {
    type Algebra: LieAlgebra;
    const DIM: usize;
    fn identity() -> Self;
    fn compose(self, rhs: Self) -> Self;
    fn inverse(self) -> Self;
    fn exp(x: Self::Algebra) -> Self;              // deterministic elementary functions
    fn log(self) -> Self::Algebra;
    fn cay(x: Self::Algebra) -> Self;              // +, −, ×, ÷, √ only
    fn cay_inv(self) -> Self::Algebra;
    fn adjoint(self) -> <Self::Algebra as LieAlgebra>::Operator;   // Ad_g
}

pub trait LieAlgebra: Copy {
    type Dual: Copy;                               // 𝔤*: momenta, wrenches
    type Operator;                                 // linear maps on 𝔤
    fn bracket(self, rhs: Self) -> Self;
    fn ad(self) -> Self::Operator;
    fn coad(self, mu: Self::Dual) -> Self::Dual;   // ad*_x μ = (ad_x)ᵀ μ, no minus sign (§11.2)
    fn pair(self, mu: Self::Dual) -> Power;        // ⟨μ, x⟩, in watts
}

/// A joint: a product of one-parameter subgroups of SE(3) given by a screw basis (C-01, T-11).
pub struct JointSubgroup { class: HerveClass, screws: ScrewBasis, closed_under_bracket: bool }

/// `a_from_b`. Composition type-checks: Transform<A,B> * Transform<B,C> = Transform<A,C>.
pub struct Transform<A: Frame, B: Frame> { motor: fs_ga::Se3, _frames: PhantomData<(A, B)> }
pub struct TwistIn<F: Frame>  { xi: fs_ga::Twist,  _f: PhantomData<F> }
pub struct WrenchIn<F: Frame> { w:  fs_ga::Wrench, _f: PhantomData<F> }

/// Three maps, three types, so a wrench is never moved by the twist map (§11.2, §13.3).
pub struct TwistMap<A: Frame, B: Frame>(Transform<A, B>);          // Ad_g: a twist in b to a twist in a
pub struct WrenchPushforward<A: Frame, B: Frame>(Transform<A, B>); // Ad_g⁻ᵀ: a wrench in b to a wrench in a
pub struct WrenchPullback<A: Frame, B: Frame>(Transform<A, B>);    // Ad_gᵀ: a wrench in a to a wrench in b

/// A symmetric cone, by its Jordan algebra. Instances: the nonnegative orthant, the three-dimensional
/// friction cone, and the four-dimensional cone (normal, two tangential, spin) of §18.
pub trait Cone {
    type Point;
    fn jordan(a: &Self::Point, b: &Self::Point) -> Self::Point;
    fn spectral(a: &Self::Point) -> Spectrum;
    fn project(a: &Self::Point) -> Self::Point;    // T-07: P(x) ∈ 𝒦, P(x) − x ∈ 𝒦*, ⟨P(x), P(x) − x⟩ = 0
    fn barrier(a: &Self::Point) -> f64;
}

/// A convex contact potential whose negative gradient is the impulse (C-06).
pub trait ContactLaw { fn potential(&self, vc: ContactVelocity, p: &InterfaceCard) -> ConvexTerm; }

/// What a free tree limb presents to its parent at a mechanical port, at one instant (§14.6).
/// Positive semidefinite, never guaranteed definite: it cannot be inverted at the port.
pub struct LimbPortPacket { inertia: SymPsd6, bias: WrenchIn<PortFrame> }
```

### I.2 The claim product and evidence

```rust
/// The four evidence classes of §12. Combination takes the minimum.
pub enum EvidenceClass { Estimated, Tested, Certified, Proved }   // Ord: Estimated < Tested < Certified < Proved

/// Exactly one of the seven claims of §8.
pub enum ClaimKind { Proof, KnownAnswer, Parity, Fidelity, DesignComparison, Reality, Performance }

/// A typed leaf: evidence for one claim kind K. Its class is set only by the checker that produced it,
/// and no constructor of Evidence<Proof> exists outside frob-lemma (GATE-LEMMA-06).
pub struct Evidence<K> {
    class: EvidenceClass,             // private
    scope: Scope,                     // model, tier, domain, quantifier prefix
    assumptions: AssumptionSet,       // each with its polarity (C-18)
    receipts: Vec<ReceiptId>,         // certificate hashes, checker identities, study receipts
    flags: NoAuthorization,
    kind: PhantomData<K>,
}

/// What a result asserts, how strongly, about what, and that it authorizes nothing. Owned by frob-core;
/// carried in every output envelope (§32) and read from every bundle by frob-verify (§12).
pub struct ClaimProduct {
    kind: ClaimKind,
    class: EvidenceClass,             // minimum over inputs; no setter
    weakest: InputRef,                // the input that set the class: content hash and field path
    scope: Scope,                     // design family, world family, quantifier order, horizon, validity region
    tier: Tier,                       // lowest physics tier among the inputs
    determinism: DetClass,            // weakest of D0..D4 among the inputs
    reality: RealityScope,            // NoClaim, or the calibrated family a band was issued for
    conditions: FlagSet,              // union over inputs: tier-sensitive, controller-sensitive, model-conditional
    inputs: Vec<InputRef>,            // every consumed artifact, each with its own claim product
    authorization: NoAuthorization,
}

impl ClaimProduct {
    /// The only way to build a product from parts. Class, tier and determinism take the weakest; scope takes
    /// the intersection; conditions take the union; a mismatch of quantifier order is a refusal.
    pub fn combine(kind: ClaimKind, parts: &[ClaimProduct]) -> Result<ClaimProduct, Refusal>;
}

/// `False` is a unit type that serializes as the JSON literal false. No constructor, setter or deserializer
/// yields `true`; a reader rejects an artifact in which a flag is absent or true.
pub struct NoAuthorization {
    pub execution_authorized: False,
    pub hardware_safety_signoff: False,
    pub sim_to_real_certified: False,
}

/// Build packets add a fourth flag (§31.12).
pub struct PacketAuthorization { pub base: NoAuthorization, pub fabrication_released: False }

/// Reality status of a result (§30). Everything outside a calibrated cell is NoClaim.
pub enum RealityStatus { NoClaim, Synthetic, PublishedAnchor, Candidate, Calibrated, Retired }

// Three things do not exist, and a compile-fail test pins each: a conversion from ClaimProduct into a
// Proved value; a setter for `class`; a public constructor that takes a class as an argument.
```

Note. §8.2 writes the product as one struct with `combine`, and §12.2 writes it as a pair `ClaimProduct<A, B>` of
typed leaves whose class is the minimum. They are one mechanism: the pair is the two-input case of `combine`. The
serialized flags object is spelled `flags` in a bundle (§12.4), `authorization` in an envelope and a build packet
(§32.4, §31.12), and `no_authorization` in a verdict, a qualification receipt and a counterexample world (§24, §26).
The three field names inside it are the same everywhere.

### I.3 A mission query and its answer

```rust
/// A `.fmission` document (§25.3.2). Its canonical bytes hash to the MissionId.
pub struct MissionQuery {
    design_domain: DesignDomain,      // family, topologies, ports, isomorphisms, free and bound parameters, tolerances
    world: WorldFamily,               // nonempty; kind BoundedSet or Population; persistence per hidden parameter
    observation: Channel,             // fields, noise bounds, timing in the seven instants of §20
    policy_class: PolicyClass,        // Causal on the history of Y; indexing; authority; randomization
    horizon: Horizon,                 // Static | Time(Qty) | Ticks(u64) | TerminalModes(..)
    predicates: Predicates,           // accept, hard_loss, margins; atoms carry comparator and units
    quantifiers: Vec<Binder>,         // ordered; part of the MissionId
    objective: Option<Objective>,     // a declared cost and the claim wanted
    evidence: EvidenceProfile,        // Exact | Enclosed | Empirical, with accepted classes
    resolution: Resolution,           // largest unresolved set accepted, in a stated measure
    response: Vec<ResponsePart>,
    budget: Budget,                   // wall, CPU core, GPU, referee and checker seconds; sync_wait_ms
}

pub enum Binder { Exists { var: Var, scope: PolicyScope }, ForAll { var: Var },
                  Prob { var: Var, population: PopulationId, at_least: Ratio, confidence: Ratio } }

pub struct Cell { topology: TopologyId, chart: ChartId, bounds: Vec<Bound>,      // closed or open per end
                  units: Vec<Unit>, assumptions: AssumptionSet, policy_scope: PolicyScope }

pub enum Verdict { Inner(Vec<ProofRef>), Excluded(Vec<ProofRef>), Unresolved(Vec<Explanation>) }

pub enum Explanation { StraddlesThreshold, ModeSequenceUnenclosed, SolverFailure, BudgetExhausted,
                       CompetingMechanisms(Vec<MechanismRef>), NeedsMeasurement(MeasurementRef) }

pub struct Witness { proof: ProofRef, kind: ProofKind, at: ChartPoint, payload: WitnessPayload }

pub struct CostBounds { incumbent: Ratio, lower_bound: Ratio, unit: Unit, attained: bool, gap: Ratio }

/// The answer carries I ⊆ F ⊆ O as a list of cells. It is immutable and addressed `a:…`; a later query with
/// more budget produces a new answer that refines it.
pub struct Answer { mission: MissionId, cells: Vec<(Cell, Verdict)>, witnesses: Vec<Witness>,
                    cost: Option<CostBounds>, next_test: Option<NextTest>, claim: ClaimProduct, bundle: BundleHash }

impl Answer {
    pub fn inner(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Cell>;        // cells with a constructive witness
    pub fn excluded(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Cell>;     // cells with an exclusion proof
    pub fn unresolved(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Cell>;   // work still to do, each with its reason
    /// The outer set is the domain minus the excluded cells (INV-AUGUR-02): inner ∪ unresolved.
    pub fn outer(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Cell>;
}
```

### I.4 A proof object and a certificate bundle entry

`frob-mission` emits plain proof objects. `frob-lemma` writes them into `.frobcert` bundles against the schema of
§12.4 and shares no code with the reader. `frob-cert` reads a bundle with the standard library alone, and
`frob-verbs` runs the checker before an answer is returned.

```rust
/// A proof object as frob-mission emits it (§25.5). Numbers are exact rationals (reduced, positive
/// denominator) or outward-rounded intervals with a declared implementation and precision.
pub struct ProofObject {
    id: ProofRef,                     // "p0", "p1", … within one answer
    kind: ProofKind,                  // closed registry frob.cert.kinds/1
    cell: CellRef,
    establishes: Establishes,         // the prefix, horizon, policy class and cell the proof is about
    payload: ProofPayload,            // witness vectors, dual vectors, enclosures, policy tables
    side_conditions: Vec<ProofRef>,   // sub-certificates a rule requires
    primitive_equations: Vec<Equation>, // in Unicode text and as an expression DAG
    expects: Expected,                // Inner | Excluded
}

pub enum ProofKind { LpPrimal, LpFarkas, ConicFarkas, IntervalBox, TaylorBox, SosGram, FiniteGame, AliasPair,
                     MonotoneTransport, SymmetryTransport, Partition, Composition, ProductUnreachable,
                     TraceWitness, SampleCoverage }

/// One `.frobcert` file (schema frob.cert/1): everything needed to re-check one claim on a machine that has
/// neither the agent, a GPU nor the simulator.
pub struct Bundle {
    schema: SchemaId,                 // "frob.cert/1"
    claim: ClaimStatement,            // kind, class, quantifiers, horizon
    query: Embedded,                  // BLAKE3 and the canonical bytes of the statement it certifies
    definitions: Definitions,         // units, frame, clocks, ordered ports
    assumptions: Vec<Assumption>,     // each with `survives`: grow | shrink (C-18)
    plant: PlantRef,                  // model and policy class
    domain: Domain,                   // chart and cell
    proof: BundleProof,               // kind from the registry of §12.4, primitive equations, payload
    checker: CheckerRef,              // name and build
    expected_verdict: CheckVerdict,
    lineage: Lineage,                 // Merkle root; alpha_spend entries for qualification receipts
    flags: NoAuthorization,
}

/// What the auditor returns, with the first failing rule named.
pub enum CheckVerdict { Accept, Reject { rule: RuleId }, Unsupported { kind: String } }
```

Note: one closed registry names the proof kinds, `frob.cert.kinds/1`, in §12.4. §25.5.2 lists the rows of that
registry that mission answers use, under the same names, so a proof object's kind is the bundle's kind and
`frob-lemma` maps nothing when it writes a bundle.

| Kinds of `frob.cert.kinds/1` (§12.4) | Used by | Class |
|---|---|---|
| `lp-primal`, `lp-farkas`, `conic-farkas`, `interval-box`, `taylor-box`, `sos-gram`, `finite-game`, `alias-pair`, `monotone-transport`, `symmetry-transport`, `partition`, `composition`, `product-unreachable` | Mission answers (§25.5.2) | Certified |
| `trace-witness` | Mission answers: a replayed execution | At most Tested |
| `sample-coverage` | Mission answers: an empirical bound | Estimated; never a proof |
| `poly-identity`, `rational-ldlt`, `interval-root`, `complex-connectivity`, `tube-inclusion`, `rewrite-trace`, `orbit-count`, `group-enumeration`, `energy-budget`, `alpha-root`, `lean-capsule` | Kernel and analysis certificates | As §12.4 |

### I.5 A model variant and a shape class

```rust
/// The capacities one static step plan is built for (§17.4, §21.11). Its hash, the ShapeClassId, is part of
/// the StepPlanId. One kernel set and one launch graph exist per class per device.
pub struct ShapeClass {
    pub n_v: u16,                 // degree-of-freedom capacity: one of 12, 18, 24, 32, 48, 64 by default
    pub links: u16,               // link capacity
    pub depth: u8,                // maximum tree depth
    pub samples: u16,             // collision samples tested per world
    pub contacts: u16,            // C of §16.6
    pub rows: u16,                // R of §16.6
    pub actuators: u16,
    pub sensor_layout: SensorLayoutId,
    pub policy_layout: LayoutId,
    pub contact_law: LawId,
    pub precision: PrecisionProfile,   // default | stiff
    pub iterations: u8,           // the lockstep iteration count, a class constant
    pub single_structure: bool,   // P-A: one tree, unmasked path
}

/// One model variant: a read-only table per model slot, about 192 bytes per link (12 kB for a 64-link variant,
/// §21.11); collision sample lists are counted separately (§17.4).
pub struct ModelTable {
    pub model: ModelId,
    pub level_start: Vec<u16>,    // links sorted by depth; ranges per level
    pub parent: Vec<u16>,         // parent index, less than the link's own; padding links are roots of nothing
    pub placement: Vec<Se3Packed>,     // parent_from_joint
    pub screw: Vec<[f32; 18]>,    // screw basis S in ℝ^(6×3)
    pub screw_cols: Vec<u8>,      // k = 0 (padding), 1, 2 or 3 active columns: joint classes are data
    pub inertia: Vec<[f32; 10]>,  // zero for padding links
    pub limits: Vec<JointLimits>,
    pub actuator_slot: Vec<u16>,
    pub sample_range: Vec<(u16, u16)>,
}

/// A world is a row of indices into its bucket's tables, plus its address.
pub struct WorldSlots { pub model: u32, pub scene: u32, pub task: u32, pub job: u32, pub addr: WorldAddr }

/// One shape class on one device: one arena, one compiled kernel set, one step plan, one launch graph.
pub struct Bucket { class: ShapeClass, device: DeviceId, model_variants: u16, scene_variants: u16, worlds: u32 }

/// A slab is touched by the host only under an epoch-fenced lease (§21.10).
pub enum Access { Device, HostRead, HostWrite }
pub struct SlabLease { slab: SlabId, epoch: u64, access: Access }   // valid only while `epoch` is committed
```

Note. §17.4 spells the capacities `n_v`, `links`, `depth`, `samples`, `contacts`, `rows`, `actuators` and carries
`single_structure`; §21.11 spells them with a `_cap` suffix, adds `policy_layout`, `contact_law`, `precision` and
`iterations`, and names the world row `WorldRow` with 16-bit variant indices. The sketch above is the union under the
names of §17.4, which owns the type.

### I.6 A clock, a phase accumulator and the seven instants

```rust
/// Simulation time: an unsigned 64-bit count of quanta of 1/Q seconds, Q the least common multiple of the
/// denominators of every period in the run (§20.4.1). Admission refuses Q above 2⁴⁰.
pub struct Quanta(pub u64);

pub struct ClockSpec { period: Quanta, phase: Quanta, rate_error: Ratio, intra_step: IntraStep }
pub enum IntraStep { Split, Interpolate { bound: Bound }, Hold }

/// Integer addition and comparison only: determinism class D0, and no drift.
pub struct PhaseAccumulator { next_event: Quanta, period: Quanta }
impl PhaseAccumulator {
    /// At a boundary at time t: fire while next_event ≤ t, advancing by the period each time.
    pub fn fire(&mut self, t: Quanta) -> u32;
}

/// The seven instants (§20.4.2). Order constraints: sample ≤ exposure ≤ arrival; a packet is used by a
/// decision at t only if its arrival is at or before t; decision ≤ command ≤ actuation. The timestamp is
/// deliberately unconstrained: it is what the device believes.
pub enum Instant { Sample, Exposure, Timestamp, Arrival, Decision, Command, Actuation }

pub struct Packet {
    sensor: SensorId, seq: u32,
    t_sample: Quanta, t_exposure: Quanta, t_stamp: DeviceTime, t_arrival: Quanta,
    lateness: Quanta, mask: MaskRef, payload: BufRef,
}
pub struct Command { t_decision: Quanta, t_command: Quanta, t_actuation: Quanta, payload: BufRef }

/// Every observation exposes its age, decision minus sample, as an integer count of quanta.
pub struct Age(pub Quanta);
```

### I.7 The transactional step

```rust
/// Step profiles (§16). `Lockstep` is the fixed-step throughput profile; `Strict` and `Referee` are
/// transactional and event-located.
pub enum StepProfile { Lockstep, Strict, Referee }

/// Everything a retried interval must restore so that it equals a first attempt (INV-KIN-02): physical
/// state, contact feature memory and impulses, warm starts, actuator and thermal state, clock phases and
/// packet queues, controller and estimator state, terrain edits, energy-ledger accumulators, event
/// counters and the command cursor. Random streams are counter-based and have no state to restore.
pub struct RestoreSet { /* the fields above */ }

/// A candidate interval is built beside the committed state and becomes visible in one step.
pub struct Transaction<'a> {
    committed: &'a Committed,         // read through a named commit_epoch and nothing else
    interval: (Quanta, Quanta),       // a base interval [t0, t1), fixed by the schedule, never by the state
    checkpoint: RestoreSet,
    attempt: u8,                      // 0..=3; selects a numerical plan only (ADR-KIN-05)
    work: VecDeque<(Dyadic, Dyadic)>, // sub-intervals on the dyadic grid of the base interval, L ≤ 16
    events: u8,                       // at most 64 per base interval
}

pub enum StepOutcome {
    /// commit_epoch advances; state, impulses, sensor inputs, diagnostics and the attempt index are
    /// published together.
    Committed { epoch: u64, attempt: u8, events: Vec<EventRecord>, checks: CheckReport },
    /// After the last attempt the checkpoint is restored and nothing from the interval is published.
    /// A numerical failure is not a physical failure: the world is Faulted with cause numerical-fault.
    Faulted { refusal: Refusal /* FROB-REF-220 or -221 */ },
}

/// Noise that acts over an interval is defined on the dyadic tree of the base interval, so a retry can
/// refine a path and can never redraw it.
pub struct NoiseAddress { world: WorldAddr, base_interval: u64, stream: StreamId, level: u8, index: u32 }
```

### I.8 A requirement and its monitor

```rust
/// A comparison of two expressions of one dimension, with a scale of that dimension (§24.5).
pub struct Atom { id: Ident, cmp: Cmp, lhs: Expr, rhs: Expr, scale: Scale }
pub enum Cmp { Gt, Ge, Lt, Le, Eq }
pub enum Scale { Qty(Qty), Exact }                 // Exact: integer-valued signal, margin +1 or −1
pub enum Expr { Signal(SignalId), Qty(Qty), Op(ArithOp, Vec<Expr>), Delay(Qty, SignalId) }

pub struct Window { lo: Qty, hi: Qty, round: Option<Rounding> }   // closed; exact rational comparison of ticks
pub enum Past { Atom(Ident), And(Vec<Past>), Or(Vec<Past>), Not(Box<Past>),
                Historically(Window, Box<Past>), Once(Window, Box<Past>), Since(Window, Box<Past>, Box<Past>) }
pub enum Future { Past(Past), And(Vec<Future>), Or(Vec<Future>), Not(Box<Future>),
                  Always(Window, Box<Future>), Eventually(Window, Box<Future>),
                  Until(Window, Box<Future>, Box<Future>) }

pub struct Requirement {
    clock: ClockId,                    // each requirement names the clock it is evaluated on
    atoms: Vec<Atom>,
    online: Vec<(Ident, Past)>,        // compiled into kernels of the last stage of the batched step
    verdict: (Ident, Future),          // evaluated offline on the completed trace
    examples: Vec<(TraceRef, Label)>,  // at least two satisfied and two violated
}

/// Two monitors, one function. Online: fixed memory of 2·W values per operator node and world, no
/// data-dependent control flow. Offline: a two-pass evaluator on the CPU. Minimum, maximum and negation are
/// exact in floating point, so both return identical bits for identical atom values.
pub trait Monitor {
    fn margin(&self, tick: Tick) -> Margin;        // dimensionless; its sign agrees with the Boolean value
    fn decided_at(&self) -> Option<Tick>;          // the tick at which a prefix fixed the verdict
}

/// The unit that scorecards, studies and searches count (schema frob.verdict/1, stored in `.frun`).
pub struct VerdictRecord {
    task: TaskId, requirement: Ident, world: WorldAddr, model: ModelId, controller: ControllerId,
    verdict: VerdictValue,             // Satisfied | Violated | Undetermined | Invalid
    margin: f64, binding_atom: Ident, binding_time: Qty, decided_at: Qty, reason: Option<FailureClass>,
    coverage: Coverage,                // Sampled | Interval, with the count of missing samples
    boundary: BoundaryFlag,            // flagged inside the guard band of 2⁻²¹ and re-evaluated exactly
    atoms_min: Map<Ident, f64>, evidence: ClaimProduct, no_authorization: NoAuthorization, trace_digest: Blake3,
}
```

### I.9 A study, in two types

```rust
/// A registered plan to answer one comparative or absolute question. It declares its type when it is
/// created and keeps it (INV-ARENA-05). The two types are never mixed inside one study.
pub enum Study { Anytime(AnytimeStudy), FixedN(FixedNStudy) }

pub struct AnytimeStudy {
    null: Hypothesis, margin: Qty,
    span: LossSpan,                    // a bound on the paired difference, fixed before the first observation
    betting_rule: RuleId, level: Ratio, budget: Budget,
    // reports: the e-value, the confidence sequence, pairs used, the stopping reason
}

pub struct FixedNStudy {
    n: u32, rule: RuleId, level: Ratio, margin: Qty,
    preanalysis: PreAnalysis,          // computed before the first episode; a study without one is refused
    // reports: counts, the interval, the verdict, the pre-analysis hash. The verdict is computed once, at n.
}

/// Which verdicts are reachable at this n and level, and the power at declared alternatives.
pub struct PreAnalysis { outcomes: u64, reachable: Set<StudyVerdict>, power: Vec<(Alternative, Ratio)>, hash: Blake3 }
pub enum StudyVerdict { Promote, Inferior, PracticalTie, Inconclusive }

/// What `study.plan` returns: the content address of the resolved manifest. Planning runs no physics.
pub struct StudyPlan {
    designs: Vec<DesignId>, scene: SceneRef, task: TaskId, controller_arm: ControllerArm,
    seed_protocol: SeedProtocol,       // pairing by (world, replicate); clusters are the unit of inference
    budget: Budget, backend: BackendRequest, study: Study, estimate: CostEstimate,
}

/// The accounting identity every paired study satisfies:
/// a_only + b_only + both + neither + unscored = planned.
pub struct PairCounts { a_only: u32, b_only: u32, both: u32, neither: u32, unscored: u32, planned: u32 }
```

### I.10 A qualification request and its receipt

```rust
/// Request i of a campaign in the blinded lane (§24.13). Hashed into the ledger with an idempotency key
/// before any confirmation world exists (INV-QUAL-04).
pub struct QualifyRequest {
    campaign: CampaignId, index: u32,
    alpha_total: Ratio,
    alpha_i: Ratio,                    // α / [i·(i + 1)]; spent whether or not the answer is liked
    candidate: Arm, baseline: Arm,     // each a design and a controller
    task: TaskId, claim: String,
    study: Study,                      // for FixedN, the pre-analysis is computed at α_i
    tier_plan: TierPlan, clusters: u32, budget: Budget,
    commit: Commit,                    // ledger sequence (a string on the wire), hash, idempotency key
}

/// All the agent receives. Sealed until the campaign closes: world addresses, per-unit outcomes,
/// telemetry, stills.
pub struct QualifyReceipt {
    campaign: CampaignId, index: u32, alpha_i: Ratio, alpha_spent: Ratio,
    decision: Decision,                // Promoted | NotPromoted | Inconclusive
    units_used: u32, receipt_hash: Blake3, no_authorization: NoAuthorization,
}
```

### I.11 A counterexample world

```rust
/// A minimal counterexample world (`.fmcw`, schema frob.mcw/1; §26.7). It carries what replays it:
/// identities, edits, addresses and state digests (INV-NEMESIS-04).
pub struct CounterexampleWorld {
    id: WorldId, task: TaskId, requirement: Ident,
    candidate: Candidate,              // model, controller, policy
    base: BaseWorld,                   // a scene and a world address in which the candidate passes
    edits: Vec<WorldEdit>,             // op, path, from, to, and which aspects of the scene each changes
    minimality: Minimality,            // OneMinimal { pairs_exhausted } | NonMinimal(k); tests run; failing seeds
    failure: Failure,                  // class, binding atom, margin, time
    replay: Replay,                    // backend, determinism class, state digests
    promotion: Promotion,              // tier, reproduced, numerical variants tried
    oracle: OracleResult,              // solvable-causal with a witness controller, or the failed necessary condition
    legality: Legality,                // inside the profile; bounds touched, each with its provenance
    prior: Prior,                      // log₁₀ density ratio against the nominal world law
    neighbours_passing: Vec<WorldId>,  // the worlds with one edit removed
    evidence: ClaimProduct, no_authorization: NoAuthorization,
}
```

### I.12 An intervention and a fork

```rust
/// `do(factor := value)`. Each intervention changes one declared mechanism, and the model difference it
/// makes is stored with the fork (INV-AUTOPSY-02).
pub struct Intervention { factor: FactorPath, value: Value, mechanism: MechanismId, model_diff: Blake3 }

/// The classification every requested change receives before anything is restored. The five classes are
/// defined in §27.4, which owns the intervention semantics; the fork mechanism of §29.8 implements them.
pub enum ForkClass {
    Continuation,                                  // the null fork, a placebo, replay, teleport
    Exogenous,                                     // restart at the fork tick; nothing regenerated
    ContactAffecting,                              // fork tick; contact memory discarded; first solve cold; labelled
    Information,                                   // fork tick; packet queues and filter state re-initialized
    Structural,                                    // design parameters too: the authored initial condition, settled again
}

/// A fork is a parent episode, a fork tick and a change set. It never mutates its parent.
pub struct Fork {
    parent: EpisodeId, tick: Tick, changes: Vec<Intervention>,
    class: ForkClass, earliest_valid_tick: Tick, forced_by: Vec<FieldPath>,
    addr: WorldAddr,                               // the parent's address extended by a fork path
    null_replay: NullReplay,                       // Bitwise, or the record is unsound and nothing is attributed
}

pub struct Contrast { intervention: Intervention, rescued: (u32, u32), contrast: f64,
                      flip_rate: FlipRates /* at 10⁻¹² and at 10⁻⁷ */, label: CauseLabel }
pub enum CauseLabel { ButFor, Contributing, Joint, Alternative, PrecedesSnapshot, PrecisionSensitive,
                      ChaoticUnattributable, None }

/// Schema frob.autopsy.attribution/1. Class Estimated: a cause in the model at this tier, among the listed
/// factors.
pub struct Attribution { fork: ForkId, tier: Tier, precision: Precision, horizon: Qty, forks_run: u32,
                         null_replay: NullReplay, placebo: Placebo, contrasts: Vec<Contrast>,
                         pairs: Vec<PairContrast>, refused: Vec<RefusedIntervention>, evidence: ClaimProduct }
```

Note. §27.4 lists five classes and §29.8 three. The sketch nests the three intervention kinds of §27.4 inside the
middle class of §29.8 and treats "structural or design-parameter intervention" as `StructuralSubstitution`.

### I.13 A ladder rung and an allocation decision

```rust
/// Six rungs, each about an order of magnitude dearer than the one below, each allowed to decide only what
/// its evidence supports (§28.9).
pub enum Rung {
    R0Static,                          // design.check and the bound analyses: refuse or exclude; never ranks
    R1SharedPolicy,                    // a family policy zero-shot, or the baseline controller: discard
    R2FineTuned { fraction: Ratio },   // each fraction is its own rung for calibration
    R3Specialist,                      // one training run: rank finalists, as provisional
    R4Referee,                         // paired re-evaluation on the referee: establish, or label tier-sensitive
    R5RareFailure,                     // a failure-rate bound for finalists
}

/// What a lower rung may do in one stratum, from the rank-agreement ledger (§28.10): Selective when the
/// lower bound on top-weighted Kendall τ is at least 0.7, DiscardOnly between 0.5 and 0.7, Uninformative
/// below 0.5.
pub enum LadderMode { Selective, DiscardOnly, Uninformative }

pub enum AllocationRule {
    FixedTable { eta: u8 },            // successive halving with η = 3; the baseline and every fallback
    ConformalSurvivors { alpha: Ratio, q_hat: f64, audit_n: u32 },   // calibrated on the audit lane only
}

pub struct AllocationDecision {
    campaign: CampaignId, stratum: StratumId, from: Rung, to: Rung,
    rule: AllocationRule, mode: LadderMode,
    advanced: Vec<DesignId>, discarded: Vec<DesignId>,
    audit_lane: Vec<DesignId>,         // drawn by a keyed stream before any score exists; never cancelled
    rank_record: Option<RankAgreementId>,   // a rung without a record may not discard
    policy: DecisionPolicyId,          // the versioned decision rule, e.g. ("atelier.dc01.promote", 3)
    spend: Budget,
}
```

### I.14 A family policy and an inheritance map

```rust
/// The manifest and mapping table every checkpoint carries (schema frob.policy/1, in safetensors metadata).
pub struct PolicyManifest {
    network: NetworkSpec,              // kind, widths, recurrent
    action_law: ActionLaw,             // e.g. latent-then-limit
    discount: PhysicalDiscount,        // per second, not per step
    channels: Vec<ChannelMap>,         // matched by role, never by position or name order (INV-CORTEX-04)
    observation_schema: ObsSchema,     // actor, critic-only and normalizer digests
    trained_on: TrainedOn,             // task, scenes, randomization, tier, determinism, reset mode, donor
    group: GroupTying,                 // Γ_mech, Γ_obs and how the tying was imposed
}
pub struct ChannelMap { id: Ident, role: Role, unit: Unit, sign: i8, bounds: (Qty, Qty), rate: Ratio }

/// A family policy: one policy for a generator of designs, with one token per link.
pub struct FamilyPolicy {
    manifest: PolicyManifest, generator: GeneratorId, split: DesignSplit,
    envelope: SupportEnvelope,         // `policy.apply` refuses a design outside it
    rank_record: Option<RankAgreementId>,   // without one it is not a rung (FROB-REF-537)
}

/// How a child design's policy starts from its parent's, through the typed edit that joins them (§23.12).
/// A mapping that cannot be built is a refusal, not a guess (FROB-REF-531).
pub struct InheritanceMap {
    donor: PolicyId, child: DesignId, edit_path: Vec<EditId>,
    correspondences: Vec<Correspondence>,   // frames, actuator roles, sensors, contact roles, phase clocks
    unmatched: Vec<Role>,              // new channels start at zero; unmatched recurrent state is reset
    depth: u8,                         // a lineage resets on a schedule (default k = 5)
}
pub enum Transport { Adjoint, AdjointDual, GroupElement(GroupElem), Zero, Reset }
pub struct Correspondence { from: Role, to: Role, transport: Transport }
```

### I.15 An energy budget and a shield

```rust
/// A `.fenergy` document (schema frob.energy/1). Quantities are decimal strings so that no binary rounding
/// enters the predicate, which is evaluated in the exact-integer kernel class with declared unit scales.
pub struct EnergyBudget {
    boundary: BoundaryId,
    load_path: Vec<ComponentId>,       // every port that can inject power is listed or cut (FROB-REF-451)
    unit_scale: UnitScale,             // e.g. 1e-6 J and 1e-6 s
    terms: Terms,                      // kinetic_ub, drive, external[], stored[], reserve
    absorber: Absorber,                // card, w_abs, provenance
    premises: Premises,                // sources_complete, absorber_on_path
    claim: ClaimProduct,
}
impl EnergyBudget {
    /// Admit iff T_ub + E_drive + E_ext + E_stored + E_reserve ≤ W_abs, as integers at the declared scale.
    pub fn admits(&self, speed_reading: Qty) -> bool;
    /// (W_abs − T_ub − E_ext − E_stored − E_reserve) / P_max.
    pub fn longest_cutoff_delay(&self, speed_reading: Qty) -> Qty;
}

/// A runtime shield: a stage of the environment after the policy and before the actuators (§22.12).
pub struct Shield {
    rows: Vec<BarrierRow>,             // written on a template of 2 to 12 states
    margin: MeasuredMargin,            // ε̂, keyed by design class, policy identity, task family and tier
    backup: BackupController,          // damping injection, posture hold, or widen-lower-freeze
    monitors: Vec<AssumptionMonitor>,  // an alarm also triggers the backup
    budget: Option<EnergyBudget>,
}
pub enum ShieldEvent { Projected { rows: u8 }, Alarm(MonitorId), Backup(BackupKind), Uncovered, MarginRefused }
```

### I.16 A calibration record

```rust
/// What `ground.identify` writes (§30.9). A fit whose electrical-to-mechanical energy residual exceeds
/// the instrument bound is marked wrong-reason and cannot be admitted.
pub struct CalibrationRecord {
    dataset: DatasetId,                // a `.frun` bundle of origin real, with licence, rights and splits
    cell: CellKey,                     // unit, surface, envelope: one robot calibrates one robot
    prior: CardVersion,
    windows: WindowDef,                // traces enter as windows of summary features
    passes: Vec<Pass>,                 // A linear; B output error; C nonsmooth parameters, delay profiled
    posterior: Posterior,              // mean, joint covariance, delay profile with its 95% set
    misfit: (f64, f64),                // before and after
    residual_autocorrelation: Vec<f64>,     // at control-rate lags
    energy_check: EnergyCheck,         // the energy ledger evaluated on the real log
    discrepancy_floor: Variance,       // never reported below the model-form variance
    status: CardStatus,                // Candidate until a frozen prediction covers on sealed data
    labels: Vec<GroundLabel>,          // e.g. WrongReason, RankingFalsified
}
pub enum CardStatus { Candidate, Admitted, Rejected }
```

### I.17 A build packet

```rust
/// The manifest of a `.fbuild` directory, written atomically and addressed by the manifest hash (§31.12).
pub struct BuildPacket {
    schema: SchemaId, design: DesignId, model: ModelId,
    qualification: Option<VerdictId>,
    authorization: PacketAuthorization,     // four flags, all false, no setter
    reality: RealityStatus,            // NoClaim until Ground supplies data
    review: ReviewStatus,              // NoClaim until a review, a quotation or an inspection is imported
    units: UnitSystem, exploratory: bool,
    files: Vec<(Path, Blake3)>,        // parts, geometry, tolerances, mass, harness, schedule, structure, fab, certs
}
```

Note. §31.12 names the schema `frob.fbuild/1` and the format registry of §34.9 names it `frob.build/1`; likewise
`frob.fscene/1` and `frob.fclear/1` in §19 against `frob.scene/1` and `frob.clearance/1` in §34.9. The registry of
§34.9 owns schema names.

### I.18 Backends, the environment, the record

```rust
/// Where kernels run. `batch-cpu` implements it with Rust symbols.
pub trait KernelBackend {
    fn compile(&mut self, lib: &KernelLibrary) -> Result<CompiledLibrary, Refusal>;
    fn allocate(&mut self, layout: &BufferLayout) -> Result<BufferSet, Refusal>;
    fn plan(&mut self, stages: &[Stage], class: &ShapeClass) -> Result<StepPlan, Refusal>;
    fn launch(&mut self, plan: &StepPlan, bufs: &mut BufferSet, cx: &Cx<'_>) -> Result<Receipt, Refusal>;
}

/// The vectorized environment. Buffers stay on the device. Explicit reset is the default (§23.3).
pub trait VecEnv {
    fn spec(&self) -> &TaskProgram;
    fn reset(&mut self, mask: &WorldMask, seeds: &SeedPlan, cx: &Cx<'_>) -> Result<ResetView<'_>, Refusal>;
    fn step(&mut self, actions: ActionView<'_>, cx: &Cx<'_>) -> Result<StepView<'_>, Refusal>;
    fn snapshot(&self, worlds: &[WorldId]) -> Result<Snapshot, Refusal>;
    fn restore(&mut self, snapshot: &Snapshot) -> Result<(), Refusal>;
}

pub struct StepView<'a> {
    pub obs: TensorView<'a>,             // after the transition; for an ended world, its final observation
    pub reward: TensorView<'a>,          // integrated over the control interval
    pub dt_sim: TensorView<'a>,          // simulated duration of the interval, per world
    pub terminated: MaskView<'a>,        // success, failure, or an intrinsic mission deadline
    pub truncated: MaskView<'a>,         // an external collection limit on a continuing task
    pub invalid: MaskView<'a>,           // numerical failure: a study error, not a transition
    pub needs_reset: MaskView<'a>,       // terminated | truncated | invalid
    pub applied_action: TensorView<'a>,  // after the limiter and any shield
    pub final_obs: Option<TensorView<'a>>, // masked-autoreset mode only; `obs` then holds post-reset values
    pub info: InfoView<'a>,              // sample ages, validity masks, control layer, shield events
}

/// A world's record is published in fixed logical chunks. The key names no device, shard, slot or retry.
pub struct ChunkKey { run: RunId, world: u32, episode: u32, stream: StreamId, index: u32 }
pub struct ChunkRecord {
    key: ChunkKey,
    content: Blake3,        // hash of the column file bytes
    prev: Blake3,           // chain digest of chunk index − 1; zero for index 0
    chain: Blake3,          // H(prev ‖ content ‖ key)
    state_digest: u128,     // in-kernel digest of the world's state at the chunk's last tick
    lease_gen: u64,         // fencing token of the writer
    commit_seq: u64,        // assigned inside the publishing transaction; a string on the wire
    gaps: Vec<Gap>,         // dropped intervals, each with a reason
}

/// The artifact graph (§29.13). Trace identifiers and wall-clock times never enter a content hash.
pub struct ClaimId(Blake3);            // BLAKE3(claim type ‖ subject identities ‖ statement ‖ scope)
pub struct EvidenceId(Blake3);         // BLAKE3(kind ‖ payload hash)
pub struct DecisionPolicyId { name: DottedName, version: u32 }   // a decision rule, not a control policy
pub struct TraceId(u128);              // time-ordered identifier of the execution that produced an item
```

## Appendix J. Verb registry

The registry is `registries/verbs.toml`, owned by `frob-verbs`. The CLI, the daemon protocol, the MCP tool
definitions, the schemas, the refusal table and `robot-docs` are generated from it, so the surfaces cannot drift
(GATE-TETHER-02 diffs the served `tools/list` against it). Kinds: `read` returns stored or cheaply computed facts and
changes nothing; `run` spends compute, takes an idempotency key and a budget, accepts the bounded synchronous wait
(`sync_wait_ms`) and otherwise returns a job handle with exit code 8; `mutate` creates or changes a named object in the
caller's namespace and takes an idempotency key and an expected parent; `admin` cancels, stops, evicts or deletes and
needs a capability scope.

### J.1 One entry

```toml
[[verb]]
name = "design.check"
cluster = "design"
kind = "read"
tier = "S"
capabilities = ["design:read"]
input_schema = "frob.design.check.in/1"
output_schema = "frob.design.check.out/1"
refusals = ["FROB-REF-101", "FROB-REF-104", "FROB-REF-107", "FROB-REF-110"]
idempotent = true
cost_model = "static: under 2 s for template-sized designs"
first_milestone = "M1"
task_clusters = ["author", "places"]
examples = ["frob design check quad-a --json"]
```

A `run` verb adds its per-surface wait default (wait to completion on the CLI; 5,000 ms on MCP, at most 30,000). No
verb has a second spelling (J.4). The MCP tool name is the verb name with `.` and `-` replaced by `_`
(`telemetry.inspect-pixel` becomes `telemetry_inspect_pixel`); no registry name contains an underscore, and a lint
checks that the map is one-to-one (§32.12.3).

Five more were second names for a mechanism that an owner chapter registers under another name, or had no owner, and

from the defining chapter otherwise; where a verb has two milestones the first is the one at which a reduced form

### J.4 One name per verb

The registry holds no alias. Every verb is registered under the name its owner chapter gives it, §32.6 lists the
same names, and a lint refuses a second spelling of a registered verb. Where two chapters once named one mechanism,
the owner's name is the registered one and the other name is not a verb:

| Mechanism | Registered verb | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| The separating pair of worlds | `mission.separate`; its search machinery is §26's | §25.3.1 |
| Forks and their classification | `run.fork`; the classes are those of §27.4 | §29.8 |
| First divergence of two runs | `telemetry.divergence` | §29.8 |
| Interventions and attribution | `autopsy.intervene`, then `autopsy.attribute` | §27.14 |
| The screening audit | `nemesis.audit`; the cascade applies it | §26.10 |
| A bound on a failure rate; the hard-world set | `nemesis.bound`; `nemesis.hardset` | §26.12 |
| The model-form rank check (A-19) | `fidelity.modelform` | §16.9 |
| The rank-agreement record, for rungs and for tier pairs | `eval.rank-agreement` | §28.10 |
| The pre-analysis of a fixed-n study | `eval.preanalyze`; `study.plan` calls it | §24.12 |
| Certificate bundles | `prove.bundle`, `prove.verify`, `prove.list` | §12 |
| Calibration | `ground.ingest`, `ground.identify`, `ground.score` | §30.16 |
| Structure and the build packet | `foundry.size`, `foundry.optimize`, `foundry.check`, `foundry.export` (`--with-firmware` under its feature) | §31.15 |
| The co-design cascade and its one-call form | `opt.cascade`; `solve.run` is the agent-facing orchestration verb that calls it | §28.8, §32.6.2 |
| Transport | `mission.transport` for a certified claim through an interface map [F]; `skill.transport` for a skill artifact with a learned residual [M] | §25.3.1, §22.10 |
| The self-contained replay | `telemetry.export-html`, in the telemetry cluster; the viewer text is §32.15 | §29.12 |

### J.5 What an agent sees: task clusters of at most seven tools

A registry cluster is a namespace and can be large: `scene` has thirteen verbs in J.2, `eval` nine, `telemetry`
nine. What an agent sees is a **task cluster**: at most seven tools chosen for one activity, declared in the registry
beside the verbs (§32.12.4). A verb may sit in several task clusters and a lint requires every verb to sit in at least
one. Three base tools are always listed and are not counted: `session_focus`, `job_wait`, `job_cancel`. An agent
switches with `session_focus {cluster}`; focus changes context size, never authority, which is the capability token.
TARGET: the definitions of the base tools and one task cluster occupy at most 12 kB of `tools/list`.

| The agent's task | Task cluster | Tools listed |
|---|---|---|
| Find out what exists (default) | `orient` | `capabilities`, `doctor`, `robot_docs`, `schema`, `design_templates`, `scene_list`, `session_show` |
| Make and change a design | `author` | `design_new`, `design_show`, `design_edit`, `design_diff`, `design_check`, `design_import`, `control_synth` |
| Ask static questions | `analyze-body`, `analyze-motion`, `analyze-budget` | The analyses of §28.4, at most seven per cluster |
| Estimate, run, look | `simulate` | `sim_estimate`, `sim_run`, `sim_replay`, `run_fork`, `telemetry_summary`, `telemetry_failures`, `telemetry_stills` |
| Find why a run failed | `diagnose` | `explain_run`, `autopsy_intervene`, `autopsy_attribute`, `autopsy_show`, `telemetry_query`, `telemetry_inspect_pixel`, `telemetry_energy` |
| Compare designs in paired studies | `compare` | `study_plan`, `study_submit`, `study_status`, `study_compare`, `eval_promote`, `experiment_suggest`, `predict_register` |
| Ask which designs can do a mission | `mission` | `mission_new`, `mission_check`, `mission_synthesize`, `mission_refute`, `mission_distinguish`, `mission_show`, `result_revalidate` |
| Attack a design with adversarial worlds | `attack` | `nemesis_search`, `nemesis_shrink`, `mission_separate`, `nemesis_bound`, `nemesis_oracle`, `nemesis_hardset`, `scene_show` |
| Qualify a design and bundle its certificates | `qualify` | `eval_qualify`, `eval_scorecard`, `eval_ledger`, `prove_bundle`, `prove_verify`, `report_design`, `prove_list` |
| Train a policy | `learn` | `train_start`, `train_status`, `train_stop`, `train_export`, `eval_run`, `sim_estimate`, `telemetry_summary` |
| Make and inspect places | `places` | `scene_gen`, `scene_import`, `scene_compile`, `scene_list`, `scene_show`, `telemetry_stills`, `design_check` |
| Search a design space | `search` | `opt_start`, `opt_status`, `opt_archive`, `design_bisect`, `design_blame`, `solve_run`, `experiment_suggest` |
| Calibrate against reality | `reality` | `ground_ingest`, `ground_identify`, `ground_predict`, `ground_score`, `ground_band`, `predict_report`, `report_run` |
| Size structure and write a build packet | `make` | `foundry_size`, `foundry_optimize`, `foundry_check`, `foundry_tolerance`, `foundry_export`, `prove_bundle`, `report_design` |
| Watch jobs, artifacts, devices, the session | `operate` | The job, artifact, device and session verbs; the registry holds the assignment |

The fourteen named rows are the principal clusters of §32.12.4; with the two further analysis clusters and `operate`
there are seventeen. Verbs of the subsystem clusters that no principal row lists (`phylum`, `fidelity`, `contact`,
`sense`, `gait`, `skill`, `shield`, `task`, `module`, `actuator`, `spark`, `fleet`, and the family-policy and ladder
verbs) are assigned by the registry to further task clusters of at most seven. DESIGN, a starting assignment that the
registry lint checks: `families` (the seven `phylum` verbs); `fidelity` (its five verbs with `eval_promote` and
`eval_rank_agreement`); `audit` (`task_audit`, `eval_items`, `module_characterize`, `sense_visibility`,
`control_lift`, the verbs of J.3 that later subsections define); `contact`
(its seven verbs); `sensing` (the seven `sense` verbs); `gaits` (the four `gait` verbs with `control_ladder`,
`control_mpc` and `control_symmetry`); `shield` (the four `shield` verbs with `skill_compile`, `skill_check` and
`skill_show`); `tasks` (the seven `task` verbs); `devices` (the seven `spark` verbs); `inherit` (`train_family`,
`train_inherit`, `train_distill`, `policy_apply`, `eval_detect`, `fidelity_modelform`, `eval_rank_agreement`);
`ladder` (`opt_cascade`, `nemesis_audit`, `eval_rank_agreement`, `cores_show`, `report_campaign`, `explain_compare`,
`predict_report`).

This appendix is the provenance of the plan: what was reviewed, by whom, what was found, and what changed. It
also holds the plan-time checks that chapters cite as "FACT, Appendix K". Artifacts are under `planning/` in the
repository.

| 2 | Where design time goes; what incumbents already do; mechanisms from other fields; hardware envelopes; backcast and pre-mortem | Five independent passes, each given a neutral case file and one question | 94 atomic claims | Every claim sent to audit; none adopted on its author's word |
| 3 | 76 of those claims | Two independent auditors, re-reading primary sources and redoing arithmetic | 31 verified, 39 partially supported with corrected statements, 2 hypothesis-grade, 2 rejected, 2 non-material; 18 not reached | Thirteen claimed differentiators withdrawn; thirteen reworded with their conditions; performance targets re-based on published incumbent figures; the unit error between world-steps and env-steps fixed; the ten-fold metric defined against an incumbent arm |
| 4 | Ideas for a ten-fold plan | Three agents of different model families: thirty ideas each, cross-scoring, reactions, steelman and blind-spot rounds | Seven ideas scored as strong by every scorer; thirteen killed on score; several blind spots named | Survivors placed in chapters at the tier their evidence supports (Appendix B); kills recorded with their refutations (Appendix C) |

### K.3 Plan-time checks

Chapters cite these as "FACT, Appendix K". They are paper-scale: static, scalar or toy-dynamics programs with
preregistered expectations. They were run by the authors of one of the two other plans and are recorded with
receipts in the reproduction bundle named in Appendix H. This program re-derived several of their values by hand
or by script during rounds 8, 11 and 12 and did not re-execute the bundle. **None of them uses FrankenSim
dynamics, contact or a real sensor pipeline; the integrated system remains a hypothesis.**

| Check | Result as recorded | What it supports |
|---|---|---|
| Stance family | 11,520 of 11,520 classifications agree with the exact classifier; minimum half-width 3/14 m | The family-answer fixture of §25 |
| Material probe | 675 of 675 correct in class; 225 of 225 reversed under a delayed law; direct dwell 900 of 900 | A probe that is perfect in class can reverse on held-out cases (§25) |
| Sensor alias | 27 of 32, 459 of 512, 3,807 of 4,096; the common-mode case stays at 0.75 | Observation aliasing bounds what a better body can do (§20, §25) |
| Docking | Feasible if and only if ε < (U + ½)/4; 561 of 561 agreement with a linear program | The docking fixture (§20, §24) |
| Docking with three gains | Exact docking unsatisfiable; 34,590 of 34,590 labels reverse | A finite tolerance is part of the mission (§25) |
| Solver pilot (pusher) | 20 of 20 correct on both arms; 1.345 times warm and 1.088 times cold; a residual of 575.7 µs that the solver does not touch; ceiling about 1.46 | Compute the ceiling before a speed test (§0.7, §36) |
| Sill, planar and static | 94 of 156 agreement; a change of winding law flips 24 of 156 | Model form changes rankings (§16) |
| Reuse and deadline | A correctly keyed dependency graph ties a semantic receipt on these cases | Memoization is hygiene, not a lever (§28) |
| Integer predicates on devices | Identical labels on an M5 and on two RTX 4090; the host integer path was fastest | Exact-integer kernels for strict predicates (§21, §35) |

Checks made by this program's own investigators during round 5, with scripts that were not retained and must be
re-run before a gate cites them: CPU reference rates for a humanoid in double precision on this machine;
condition numbers of sampled contact Hessians against half-precision round-off (the refutation of half-precision
solves, Appendix C); the Metal working-set limit and largest single buffer (§36).

### K.4 What remains unsettled

The open disagreements are listed at the end of §0.8, each with the test that settles it. Three matter most:
whether a short program over an incumbent engine recovers most of the gain (the recovery ratio of §39); whether
cheap evaluation rungs rank designs as trained specialists do (the rank-agreement experiment of §23 and §28);
and whether design missions are dominated by training or by agent turns and diagnosis (the phase ledger of §39).
Nothing in this plan should be read as having answered them.

### K.5 Limits of this record

Eighteen audited-claim candidates were never audited. The idea duel's synthesis was compiled by an agent of the
same model family as one duellist. The first verdict register was adjudicated from evidence gathered by
investigators of one model family; the challenge round is what corrected it. Web sources were often read through
a summarizing fetch, so quoted figures must be re-read from the primary source before a gate cites them
(Appendix H marks which). The reviews of rounds 9 and 10 covered the chapters as they stood before rounds 11 and
12 inserted 66 subsections; those insertions have had no independent review.

## Appendix L. Worked artifacts

Nine artifacts for one story: a quadruped that carries a tray through a commercial-kitchen galley and sets it down at
a pass counter. They are DESIGN specimens. Every number is illustrative of the format and is not a result; where an
artifact contains arithmetic, the arithmetic is exact and was recomputed for this appendix (Appendix H.5). Identities
are abbreviated (`d:7a3e…`). Each artifact uses the schema of the chapter that owns it. Where a chapter fixes the
contents of a section and not the spelling of its fields, the artifact says so and the spellings shown are proposals
confined to the listed contents.

The story in one paragraph. A static mission query asks which stance half-widths and knee ratios can support the
loaded tray; its answer has an inner set, an outer set and a band of unresolved cells (L.4). A design is created at
the centre of an inner cell (L.1), with its leg as a reusable module (L.2). The dynamic task is the tray delivery
(L.3). A search for adversarial worlds finds a failure and shrinks it to three edits (L.6); an interventional autopsy
says which of them can be undone to rescue the run (L.9). After one design edit a paired study compares the versions
(L.8), an energy budget bounds what a stop at the counter can deliver (L.5), the blinded lane qualifies the design
(L.9), and the certificates and the receipt travel in one bundle (L.7).

### L.1 A `.fbot` design: `quad-tray`

Schema `frob.design/1` (§14.4). The design is written as authored; the canonical form sorts keys, removes white space
and writes out every default (§14.4, seven rules). The half-width 1/7 m has no terminating decimal and is therefore
written as a ratio (rule 3).

What the compiler derives and checks (§14.9, §14.11): twelve actuated coordinates; feet at (±1/5, ±1/7) m in the
nominal stance; Γ_mech = C₂ × C₂ from the two nested `mirror` constructors, with the centred tray preserving both
mirrors; Γ_obs = C₂ because the forward lidar breaks the fore–aft mirror. The archetype is `quad-mammal` (Appendix
G.4). Fills are explicit on every body (there is no default fill), and inertia is derived from Region, fill and
material.

Schema `frob.module/1` (§14.6). The module is the leg of L.1 extracted by a typed edit, referenced by content hash as

      { "joint": {"class": "R", "axis": [1,0,0], "limits": ["-45 deg", "45 deg"]},  "actuator": "qdd-m",
