```json
  "contract": {
    "guarantees": { "mass": ["1.6 kg", "2.4 kg"], "port_inertia": "sym-psd-6",
                    "bus_demand": {"peak": "38 A", "profile": "per-task, time-resolved"},
                    "heat_to_sink": {"continuous_max": "60 W"} },
    "assumes": { "bus_voltage": ["18 V", "25.2 V"], "sink_conductance_min": "0.4 W/K" },
    "digest": "b3:9a4e…" } }
```

The port contract, read against L.1 (§14.6).

| Port | Kind | Effort and flow | What joining it to `quad-tray` checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mount` | `mech` | Wrench and twist at `hip_mount` | Twists identified in the common frame, wrenches balance; power positive into the module |
| `bus` | `elec` | Voltage and current | The bus nominal of 22.2 V lies in the assumed [18, 25.2] V; currents balance at the node |
| `sink` | `thermal` | Temperature and heat rate | Four modules each assume 0.4 W/K; the shared sink offers 1.6 W/K, so the assumption is met with nothing to spare |
| `state` | `signal` | A typed message, 1,000 Hz, latency at most 1 ms | One producer, any number of typed consumers; carries no power |
| `sole` | `contact` | Meets the world under the `foot-patch` law | Listed because the module's effect on the robot cannot be summarized at its mount port alone |

Two readings of the contract are fixed by §14.6 and are easy to get wrong. First, four legs with a peak demand of 38 A
each add to 152 A against a bus limit of 60 A, and that sum excludes nothing: a contract that carries only peaks can
admit and cannot exclude, so the bus analysis of §15.10 runs on the time-resolved profiles before any design is
excluded on electrical grounds. Second, the limb port packet is 27 scalars (a symmetric positive-semidefinite 6 × 6
inertia and a bias wrench) and does not describe a leg whose foot is in contact; contact couples every limb through
the base. A leaf-local substitution of this module reuses the sibling legs' kernels and local analyses and invalidates
static stability, the baseline controller, every rollout and every whole-robot certificate.

One field is not fixed by §14.6: how an entry of `params` names its target inside `body`. The specimen writes the
default values in place; a lever in a `.fbot` names its target by `path`.

### L.3 An `.ftask`: kitchen tray delivery

Format FMT-FTASK, schema `frob.task/1` (§24.4), shown in the S-expression view. §24.4 fixes the nine section names and
their contents and fixes the grammar of `requirements`; the keywords inside the other eight sections are proposals
confined to those contents. The `TaskId` is `t:kitchen-tray@88c1…`.

```lisp
(task "kitchen-tray" :schema "frob.task/1"
  (interface
    (ports (mech base) (elec bus) (payload tray))
    (observation proprio-and-scan :frame base :rate 50 Hz
      (joint-pos 12 rad) (joint-vel 12 rad/s) (base-gyro 3 rad/s) (gravity-dir 3 1)
      (scan 64 m) (goal-vec 2 m) (sample-age 2 s))
    (action joint-targets 12 rad :rate 50 Hz :law latent-then-limit))
  (clocks
    (physics 1/500 s :phase 0 s) (imu 1/500 s :phase 0 s) (policy 1/50 s :phase 0 s)
    (lidar 1/10 s :phase 1/20 s) (req 1/50 s :phase 0 s))
  (terms
    (obs joint-pos    :unit rad   :noise encoder-14b :delay 1 ms :rep trivial)
    (obs base-gyro    :unit rad/s :noise imu-generic :delay 2 ms :rep pseudovector)
    (obs scan         :unit m     :noise lidar-2d-generic :delay 30 ms :rep permutation)
    (reward progress  :unit 1/s   :rep invariant)        ; integrated over simulated time
    (reward tray-calm :unit 1/s   :rep invariant)
    (terminate success :on (decided delivered satisfied))
    (terminate failure :on (decided delivered violated)))
  (signals
    (dist_to_pass     m     :kind state            :clock physics :reduce last)
    (base_speed       m/s   :kind state            :clock physics :reduce max)
    (tilt             deg   :kind interval-extremum :clock physics :reduce max)
    (tray_tilt        deg   :kind interval-extremum :clock physics :reduce max)
    (tray_acc         m/s^2 :kind interval-extremum :clock physics :reduce max)
    (clearance_min    m     :kind interval-extremum :clock physics :reduce min)
    (winding_temp_max K     :kind state            :clock physics :reduce max)
    (spill_events     1     :kind count            :clock physics :reduce last))
  (requirements
    (atom at-pass    (>= (- 0.15 m dist_to_pass) 0 m)        :scale 0.15 m)
    (atom settled    (>= (- 0.05 m/s base_speed) 0 m/s)      :scale 0.05 m/s)
    (atom upright    (>= (- 12 deg tilt) 0 deg)              :scale 12 deg)
    (atom tray-level (>= (- 8 deg tray_tilt) 0 deg)          :scale 8 deg)
    (atom gentle     (>= (- 3 m/s^2 tray_acc) 0 m/s^2)       :scale 3 m/s^2)
    (atom clear      (>  clearance_min 0 m)                  :scale 0.05 m)
    (atom cool       (>= (- 383 K winding_temp_max) 0 K)     :scale 20 K)
    (atom no-spill   (=  spill_events 0)                     :exact)
    (online placed   (H (0 s 1 s) (and at-pass settled tray-level)))
    (online carrying (and upright tray-level gentle))
    (verdict delivered (U (0 s 20 s) (and upright tray-level gentle clear cool no-spill) placed))
    (example trace:b3:1c0a… satisfied) (example trace:b3:77e2… satisfied)
    (example trace:b3:a04f… violated)  (example trace:b3:5d19… violated))
  (randomization
    (draw floor-friction :from card:rubber-60a/tile:uncertainty :stream world.material)
    (draw film           :from registry:hazards/commercial-kitchen:wet-floor :stream world.film)
    (draw closer-torque  :from registry:hazards/commercial-kitchen:swing-door :stream world.fixture)
    (draw tray-fill      :from registry:hazards/commercial-kitchen:hot-liquid :stream world.payload)
    (draw imu-bias       :from card:imu-generic:uncertainty :stream sensor.imu))
  (reset
    (settled-pose :count 64 :speed-below 1e-3 :for 0.2 s :penetration-max 0.5 mm :first-impulse-within 5 %))
  (world
    (scenes :family kitchen-commercial/galley :split split:b3:60d3… :group-by building)
    (horizon 22 s))
  (study
    (default :type fixed-n :n 64 :margin 0.05 :rule paired-clopper-pearson/1 :level 0.05)
    (budget :gpu-s 600)))
```

What `task.check` establishes for this file (§24.5), each a refusal if it fails.

| Check | Here |
|---|---|
| Every atom has a scale of its own dimension or is `:exact` | Seven scaled atoms; `no-spill` is `:exact` on a count |
| Signals crossing clocks declare a reduction | Every signal is reduced from the 1/500 s physics clock to the 1/50 s requirement clock |
| Window bounds are multiples of the requirement period | 1 s and 20 s are 50 and 1,000 ticks of 1/50 s |
| Online signals are past-time | `placed` uses `H`; `carrying` is a conjunction of atoms |
| The horizon covers the reach of the verdict | Reach 20 s, horizon 22 s |
| Labelled examples exist and the monitors agree with them | Two satisfied and two violated traces |
| The mutation check | Reversing a comparator or deleting an atom changes at least one example's label |

The until-form says that the six carrying conditions hold at every tick before the tray is placed, and that placement
completes within 20 s. Placement cannot latch: `H` over 1 s is false the tick any of its three conditions lapses.
Margins are dimensionless: a tilt of 17.04° gives (12 − 17.04)/12 = −0.42 for `upright`, which is the binding atom of
the counterexample in L.6. The lidar clock at 1/10 s with a phase of 1/20 s is not an integer multiple of anything
else in the file and needs no special case (§20.4).

### L.4 An `.fmission` query: which stances and knee ratios can carry the tray

Schema `frob.mission/1` (§25.3.2). The query is static and exact: it asks for the designs that can hold the loaded
tray in a four-foot stance over the whole declared load envelope, with every foot inside its rating and every knee
inside its continuous torque. It does not ask whether the robot can walk; the task of L.3 and the studies that follow
ask that.

```json
{
  "schema": "frob.mission/1",
  "name": "tray-stance-and-knee",
  "verb": "mission.synthesize",
  "design_domain": {
    "family": "template:quad-mammal@1",
    "topologies": ["rect4"],
    "ports": ["foot.pp", "foot.pm", "foot.mp", "foot.mm"],
    "isomorphisms": ["mirror-x", "mirror-y"],
    "free": [
      { "name": "v", "meaning": "1 / half_width", "unit": "1/m", "chart": "inverse-length", "box": ["4", "12"] },
      { "name": "r", "meaning": "knee belt ratio", "unit": "1", "chart": "linear", "box": ["1", "5/2"] }
    ],
    "bound": [
      { "name": "u", "meaning": "1 / half_length", "unit": "1/m", "value": "5" },
      { "name": "cap", "meaning": "normal-force rating per foot, port order", "unit": "N",
        "value": ["88", "88", "88", "88"] },
      { "name": "lam", "meaning": "knee lever arm in the loaded crouch", "unit": "m", "value": "1/10" },
      { "name": "tau_c", "meaning": "continuous knee torque at the motor", "unit": "N*m", "value": "4" }
    ],
    "tolerances": []
  },
  "world": {
    "kind": "bounded-set",
    "family": "static-tray-envelope@1",
    "frame": { "origin": "footprint-centre", "axes": "x-forward, y-left, z-up", "handedness": "right" },
    "parameters": [
      { "name": "W", "meaning": "total vertical load", "unit": "N", "value": "160" },
      { "name": "P", "meaning": "first moment (Σ xᵢ·fᵢ, Σ yᵢ·fᵢ) of the support forces", "unit": "N*m",
        "hull": [["16", "12"], ["16", "-12"], ["-16", "12"], ["-16", "-12"]] }
    ],
    "hidden": [],
    "persistence": {}
  },
  "observation": {
    "channel": "payload-wrench@1",
    "fields": ["W", "P"],
    "noise": "none",
    "timing": { "arrival": "before-decision", "clock": "static" }
  },
  "policy_class": {
    "kind": "causal",
    "indexed_by": "nominal-design",
    "authority": "independent-normal-force",
    "randomization": "none",
    "decision_makers": ["allocator"]
  },
  "horizon": { "kind": "static" },
  "predicates": {
    "accept": [
      { "id": "force-balance",  "expr": "Σ fᵢ = W" },
      { "id": "moment-balance", "expr": "Σ qᵢ·fᵢ = P" },
      { "id": "unilateral",     "expr": "fᵢ ≥ 0" },
      { "id": "rating",         "expr": "fᵢ ≤ capᵢ" },
      { "id": "knee-hold",      "expr": "lam·fᵢ ≤ r·tau_c" }
    ],
    "hard_loss": [],
    "margins": []
  },
  "quantifiers": [
    { "q": "exists", "var": "policy", "scope": "per-nominal-design" },
    { "q": "forall", "var": "world" },
    { "q": "forall", "var": "execution" }
  ],
  "objective": { "minimize": "1 / v", "unit": "m", "claim": "minimum-with-matching-lower-bound" },
  "evidence": { "profile": "exact", "arithmetic": "rational", "accept_classes": ["certified"] },
  "resolution": { "max_unresolved": { "measure": "area-fraction", "chart": "v, r", "value": "1/4" },
                  "mandatory": ["interior", "exterior"] },
  "response": ["inner", "excluded", "unresolved", "witnesses", "cost_bounds", "candidate_cost_gap",
               "next_test", "certificate"],
  "budget": { "wall_s": 60, "cpu_core_s": 60, "gpu_s": 0, "referee_s": 0, "checker_s": 10, "sync_wait_ms": 2000 }
}
```

**The answer by hand.** Order the feet [++, +−, −+, −−] at (±1/u, ±1/v). With α = P_x·u/4 and β = P_y·v/4, every
allocation that balances force and both moments is

  f = (W/4 + α + β + t,  W/4 + α − β − t,  W/4 − α + β − t,  W/4 − α − β + t)

for one free scalar t. At the vertex P = (16, 12) N·m, W/4 = 40 N, α = 20 N and β = 3v N, so
f = (60 + 3v + t, 60 − 3v − t, 20 + 3v − t, 20 − 3v + t). The last foot cannot pull: f₋₋ ≥ 0 forces t ≥ 3v − 20, and
then f₊₊ ≥ 40 + 6v. Both `rating` and `knee-hold` bound f₊₊ from above, by 88 N and by r·τ_c/λ = 40·r N. Taking
t = 3v − 20 gives f = (40 + 6v, 80 − 6v, 40, 0), which is the witness family, affine in v. The same holds at the other
three vertices by the two mirrors. Hence:

  a design (v, r) is feasible  ⟺  40 + 6v ≤ min(88, 40·r)  ⟺  v ≤ 8 and r ≥ 1 + 3v/20.

The narrowest feasible body has v = 8, a half-width of 1/8 m, and needs r ≥ 11/5. At v = 8, r = 11/5 and P = (16, 12)
the forces are (88, 32, 40, 0) N: they sum to 160 N, give Σ xᵢ·fᵢ = (1/5)·(88 + 32 − 40 − 0) = 16 N·m and
Σ yᵢ·fᵢ = (1/8)·(88 − 32 + 40 − 0) = 12 N·m, and the knee torque is (1/10)·88 = 8.8 N·m against 2.2·4 = 8.8 N·m. In
right-handed axes with +z upward the support torque is Σ rᵢ × (0, 0, fᵢ) = (P_y, −P_x, 0) = (12, −16, 0) N·m; a packet
that passes (16, 12) directly as the torque must be rejected. The exclusion has a dual witness: with y = (0, ½, ½) on
the three balance equations, yᵀA = (1, 0, 0, −1), so f₊₊ − f₋₋ = 40 + 6v on every balanced allocation, while
f₊₊ − f₋₋ ≤ min(88, 40·r) on every admissible one.

**What a first pass returns.** The engine paves the box with cells and decides each from its corners, since
feasibility is monotone (decreasing in v, increasing in r). With four cells in v and three in r:

| Cell | v | r | Worst corner feasible | Best corner feasible | Verdict | Proof |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| c:01 | [4, 6] | [1, 3/2] | No | No: 64 > 60 at (4, 3/2) | Excluded | `lp-farkas`, knee |
| c:02 | [4, 6] | (3/2, 2) | No | Yes | Unresolved: straddles the threshold | — |
| c:03 | [4, 6] | [2, 5/2] | Yes: 76 ≤ 80 at (6, 2) | Yes | Inner | `lp-primal`, affine in v |
| c:04 | (6, 8] | [1, 3/2] | No | No: more than 76 against 60 | Excluded | `lp-farkas`, knee |
| c:05 | (6, 8] | (3/2, 2) | No | Yes | Unresolved: straddles the threshold | — |
| c:06 | (6, 8] | [2, 5/2] | No: 88 > 80 at (8, 2) | Yes | Unresolved: straddles the threshold | — |
| c:07 to c:09 | (8, 10] | all three | No | No: more than 88 against 88 | Excluded | `lp-farkas`, rating |
| c:10 to c:12 | (10, 12] | all three | No | No | Excluded | `lp-farkas`, rating |

One inner cell, three unresolved, eight excluded. The outer set is the domain minus the excluded cells: c:02, c:03,
c:05 and c:06. The unresolved area is 3 of 12 equal cells, which meets the declared resolution of 1/4. The objective
is not yet settled: the best certified design has half-width 1/6 m, the outer set reaches 1/8 m, and the gap is 1/24 m,
so the first answer is a feasible candidate with a gap and not a minimum. A refinement that splits c:06 at r = 11/5
makes c:06a = (6, 8] × [11/5, 5/2] inner (worst corner 88 ≤ 88) and leaves c:06b = (6, 8] × [2, 11/5) unresolved;
the incumbent and the lower bound then meet at 1/8 m. The design of L.1 sits at the centre of c:06a, at v = 7 and
r = 47/20, where the peak foot force is 82 N against 88 N and the knee torque 8.2 N·m against 9.4 N·m.

What the answer does not say. It is a Proof claim of class Certified about the declared model: independent control of
the four normal forces, a load wrench observed before allocation, point feet, a static stance. Under equal passive
springs the same body carries different forces, and the certificate does not transfer (§25.13). It says nothing about
walking, slipping or the door.

### L.5 An `.fenergy` budget: the stop at the pass counter

Schema `frob.energy/1` (§22.11). The boundary is a bumper at the pass counter. The budget bounds the energy the robot
can deliver to that boundary during a stop, whatever the contact sequence and the friction.

```json
{
  "schema": "frob.energy/1",
  "boundary": "pass_counter_stop",
  "load_path": ["torso", "tray", "leg_fl", "leg_fr", "leg_rl", "leg_rr"],
  "unit_scale": { "energy": "1e-6 J", "time": "1e-6 s" },
  "terms": {
    "kinetic_ub": { "mass_cap_kg": "18", "speed_error_mps": "0.02", "includes_reflected_inertia": true },
    "drive": { "p_max_w": "40", "cutoff_delay_s": "0.030" },
    "external": [{ "source": "gravity", "bound_j": "0.11", "basis": "slope <= 0.02 over 0.030 m" }],
    "stored": [{ "source": "leg_series_compliance", "bound_j": "0.15" }],
    "reserve_j": "0.10"
  },
  "absorber": { "card": "bumper-150N-30mm", "w_abs_j": "4.50", "provenance": "assumed" },
  "premises": { "sources_complete": "port-graph-digest", "absorber_on_path": "declared-guide" },
  "claim": { "class": "Estimated", "reality": "no-claim", "flags": "the no-authorization flags of §12" }
}
```

The arithmetic, at a monitor reading of 0.50 m/s at the boundary, in integers of 10⁻⁶ J.

| Term | Calculation | Value |
|---|---|---|
| T_ub | ½ · 18 kg · (0.50 + 0.02)² m²/s² | 2,433,600 |
| E_drive | 40 W · 0.030 s | 1,200,000 |
| E_ext | gravity: 18 · 9.81 · 0.030 · 0.02 = 0.106 J, bounded by 0.11 J | 110,000 |
| E_stored | leg series compliance | 150,000 |
| E_reserve | at least the ledger's residual bound over the window | 100,000 |
| Sum | | 3,993,600 |
| W_abs | 150 N over 30 mm | 4,500,000 |

The predicate 3,993,600 ≤ 4,500,000 holds with a margin of 506,400, that is 0.506 J. The longest admissible cutoff
delay is (4.50 − 2.4336 − 0.11 − 0.15 − 0.10) / 40 = 42.7 ms against the declared 30 ms. The claim is `Estimated`, not
`Certified`, because the absorber envelope is `assumed`: the arithmetic is exact and the weakest input sets the class.
One bench measurement of the bumper and one of the drive would raise it for every later policy on this hardware, since
no term depends on the policy. The budget answers an energy question. It supports no statement about peak force, about
clamping after the stop, or about contacts that bypass the bumper.

### L.6 An `.fmcw`: a minimal counterexample world of three edits

Format FMT-FMCW, schema `frob.mcw/1` (§26.7). `nemesis.shrink` reduced a failing world of seven edits to three. Remove
any one and the tray is delivered.

```json
{ "schema": "frob.mcw/1", "id": "w:3fa9…", "task": "t:kitchen-tray@88c1…", "requirement": "delivered",
  "candidate": {"model": "m:5d20…", "controller": "c:2be8…", "policy": "p:6f1a…"},
  "base": {"scene": "s:kitchen-17@a4e0…", "world": {"run_seed": 901, "world": 5120, "episode": 3}},
  "edits": [
    {"op": "set", "path": "/floor/patch[galley-2]/film", "from": "dry", "to": "grease", "changes": ["material"]},
    {"op": "set", "path": "/fixtures/door[pass]/closer_torque", "from": "14 N·m", "to": "19 N·m",
     "changes": ["fixture"]},
    {"op": "set", "path": "/payloads/tray/fill", "from": "0.50", "to": "0.80", "changes": ["payload"]} ],
  "minimality": {"kind": "1-minimal", "pairs_exhausted": true, "tests": 42, "seeds_failing": "55/64"},
  "failure": {"class": "slip", "binding_atom": "upright", "margin": -0.42, "time_s": "11.3"},
  "replay": {"backend": "gpu-cuda", "class": "D2", "state_digests": "b3:0c55…"},
  "promotion": {"tier": "referee", "reproduced": true,
                "variants": ["half-step", "iterations-x2", "law-2", "tol-div-10"]},
  "oracle": {"class": "solvable-causal", "controller": "c:77e1…", "margin": 0.18, "trace": "b3:a9d2…"},
  "legality": {"inside": true, "touched": [{"bound": "closer_torque", "provenance": "assumed"},
                                           {"bound": "tray_fill", "provenance": "assumed"}]},
  "prior": {"log10_density_ratio": -4.6},
  "neighbours_passing": ["w:51b0…", "w:e7c4…", "w:0a9d…"],
  "evidence": {"class": "Tested", "tier": "referee", "standing": "established"},
  "authorization": {"execution_authorized": false, "hardware_safety_signoff": false,
                       "sim_to_real_certified": false} }
```

How to read it.

- **Three edits, three mechanisms.** A grease film on one floor patch, a swing door that closes harder, and a fuller
  tray. Each edit declares the aspect of the scene it changes, so each can serve as one intervention in L.9.
- **Minimal means 1-minimal.** Removing any single edit loses the failure; the three passing neighbours are those
  worlds. The original list had seven edits, so every subset of one or two was also tested (7 + 21 = 28 of the 42
  tests): no single edit and no pair fails, and this world is minimum among pairs. It is not called the closest
  failure.
- **The failure is the same failure.** A subset counts only if it violates the same atom (`upright`) with the same
  class (`slip`) on at least 48 of 64 paired seeds; here 55.
- **It is not an artifact of the fast tier.** The failure reproduces on the referee and under four numerical variants.
- **It is not an impossible world.** The oracle found a causal controller that delivers the tray in this world with a
  margin of 0.18, so the world is solvable and the failure belongs to the candidate.
- **Two of its bounds are `assumed`.** The closer torque and the fill level sit inside the legality profile, at values
  whose ranges no cited norm supports (Appendix G.3). A report says so.
- **It carries what replays it.** A file that does not replay with identical digests on its originating backend is
  invalid.

qualification receipt. The listing is what `prove.list` prints for it; each row is one claim that `frob-verify`
re-checks with the standard library alone.

| Entry | Claim kind | Class | Domain | Bundle proof kind | Proof object | Payload | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| e1 | `family-inclusion` | Certified | c:03: v ∈ [4, 6], r ∈ [2, 5/2] | `lp-primal` | p0, `lp-primal` | Forces affine in v at four load vertices, checked at v = 4 and v = 6 | accept |
| e2 | `family-inclusion` | Certified | c:06a: v ∈ (6, 8], r ∈ [11/5, 5/2] | `lp-primal` | p4, `lp-primal` | The same family, checked at v = 6 and v = 8 | accept |
| e3 | `family-exclusion` | Certified | c:01, c:04: v ∈ [4, 8], r ∈ [1, 3/2] | `lp-farkas` | p1, `lp-farkas` | y = (0, ½, ½); 40 + 6v > 40·r on the cells, least gap 4 N at (4, 3/2) | accept |
| e4 | `family-exclusion` | Certified | c:07 to c:12: v ∈ (8, 12], every r | `lp-farkas` | p2, `lp-farkas` | y = (0, ½, ½); 40 + 6v > 88 for v > 8 | accept |
| e5 | `partition` | Certified | The whole box [4, 12] × [1, 5/2] | `partition` | p3, `partition` | Thirteen cells; union equals the box; interiors disjoint; open and closed ends as listed | accept |
| e6 | `qualification-receipt` | Tested | Campaign `q:kitchen-tray/1`, index 1 | `sample-coverage` | — | 2 failures of 200 sealed clusters; bound 0.0357 at α₁ = 0.025; levels spent 0.025 of 0.05 | accept |

Entry e2 in full, in the container form of §12.4. A cell with two coordinates lists one rational per coordinate in
`lo` and `hi`.

What the auditor recomputes for e2: at each of the eight listed force vectors, the vertical sum (160 N), both first
moments against the vertex (±16, ±12) N·m at the stated v, every capacity (at most 88 N) and every knee bound at the
worst ratio of the cell (88·(1/10) = 8.8 ≤ (11/5)·4 = 8.8 N·m); that the forces are affine in v between the two ends,
so the checks at v = 6 and v = 8 cover the cell; that the four vertices span the declared load hull; that the lower end
in v is open as the partition entry says; and that the information the allocator is assumed to have is in the
observation contract. Mutations that must each cause rejection: a swapped foot order with unchanged forces; (16, 12)
passed as the torque; an unreported positive force floor; a passive-authority tag; a cell end certified closed where
the partition lists it open; a flag missing or true.

Two notes on spelling. The mission answer names its proofs by the kinds of §25.5.2 and the bundle by the kinds of
§12.4; the correspondence is in Appendix I.4. §12.4 writes one claim per bundle file, while a mission answer cites one
bundle hash; here the per-claim entries share one `lineage.merkle_root`, and that root is the hash the answer cites.
The payload keys `argument`, `forces_newton_at_v8` and `forces_newton_at_v6` extend the one-vertex `forces_newton` of
the specimen in §12.4 to a cell.

### L.8 A study plan

A fixed-n exact study comparing the design before and after the foot edit of L.9 on the task of L.3. §32.6.1 and
§24.12 fix what a plan binds (designs, scene, task, seed protocol, budget, backend, one study type, and for fixed-n
the pre-analysis); no chapter prints the fields of `frob.plan/1`, so the spellings below are proposals confined to
those contents. This is the `result` of `study.plan`; planning runs no physics.

```json
{ "schema": "frob.plan/1", "plan": "plan:b3:52e8…",
  "question": "B delivers the tray more often than A by more than 0.05",
  "designs": { "A": "d:7a3e…", "B": "d:c05b…" },
  "controller_arm": "shared: baseline controller re-synthesized per design, equal resources",
  "task": "t:kitchen-tray@88c1…", "requirement": "delivered",
  "scenes": { "family": "kitchen-commercial/galley", "split": "split:b3:60d3…", "part": "development" },
  "seed_protocol": { "pair_by": ["world", "replicate"], "unit": "building", "addresses": "philox:plan-key" },
  "backend": "strict:gpu-cuda", "determinism": "D2", "promote_to": "referee",
  "study": { "type": "fixed-n", "n": 64, "margin": "0.05", "level": "0.05",
             "rule": "paired-clopper-pearson/1" },
  "preanalysis": { "outcomes": 2145,
                   "reachable": { "promote": 521, "inferior": 521, "inconclusive": 1103 },
                   "unreachable": ["practical-tie"],
                   "note": "perfect concordance gives [-0.0662, +0.0662]; a tie first becomes reachable at n = 86",
                   "least_b_at_a_0": 15, "hash": "b3:5d10…" },
  "estimate": { "gpu_s": 96, "interval_90": [78, 121], "referee_cpu_core_s": 410 },
  "budget": { "gpu_s": 150, "cpu_core_s": 600 } }
```

How the plan is read and used.

1. **The type is declared and kept.** A fixed-n study computes its verdict once, at 64 complete pairs. No e-process may
   stop it; it may stop early only when every completion of the unresolved pairs gives the same verdict.
2. **The pre-analysis is the reason to plan before spending.** With 64 pairs and a five-point margin there are
   C(66, 2) = 2,145 outcomes. A practical tie is unreachable, because even perfect concordance leaves the interval
   [−0.0662, +0.0662]. A request that named "tie" among its verdicts would be refused (`FROB-REF-532`).
3. **The unit is the building.** Episodes that share a building share a generator draw, so pairs are formed per
   building and the 64 units are 64 buildings.
4. **Pairing needs a controlled determinism class.** Both arms run at D2 on one backend; under an uncontrolled class
   the paired statistic is refused.
5. **The submitted object cannot drift.** `study.submit` takes the plan address and an idempotency key.

A result consistent with the plan, from `study.compare`: b = 19 pairs where only B delivers, a = 2 where only A does,
40 where both do, 3 where neither does, none unscored; 19 + 2 + 40 + 3 + 0 = 64. The simultaneous interval on the
difference of discordant probabilities is [0.0554, 0.4392]; its lower end exceeds 0.05, so the rule promotes B and
`study.compare` reports the metric as `settled`. The result stays `provisional` until it is promoted to the referee.
It is a development result. It is not a qualification.

### L.9 An agent session over MCP

One agent, one session, the tools of six task clusters. Requests are `tools/call` with the tool name and its
arguments; responses are the `structuredContent` of the result, which is the envelope `frob.envelope/1`, abridged to
the fields that matter at each step. The token arrives from the environment (stdio transport, §32.12.9). Argument names
follow the CLI flags of §32.16 and §27.12. Tool names are those of the task clusters of §32.12.4; where one is an
alias, the registry verb of Appendix J.4 produces the result.

```text

→ tools/list
← session_focus, job_wait, job_cancel                                  (base tools, always listed)
  capabilities, doctor, robot_docs, schema, design_templates, scene_list, session_show     (cluster orient)

── offline, on a machine with neither the agent, a GPU nor the simulator ───────────────────────────────
$ frob-verify quad-tray.frobcert
accept   6 of 6 entries; class of the bundle: Tested (weakest entry e6); all three authorization flags false
```

What the session shows, as rules and not as illustrations.

1. **Seven tools at a time.** The agent changes focus eight times and never sees more than seven task tools and three
   base tools. Focus changes what is listed, not what is permitted: the token's scopes are fixed at the first call.
2. **Inner and outer sets are different answers.** The inner set holds the cells with a constructive witness; the
   outer set is the domain minus what was excluded. The agent builds from an inner cell and treats the three
   unresolved cells as work, not as candidates.
3. **A minimum needs a matching lower bound.** The first answer is reported as a feasible candidate with a gap of
   1/24 m. Only the refined answer, in which incumbent and lower bound meet at 1/8 m, states a minimum, and it warns
   that the boundary design has no reserve. The agent takes the cell centre.
4. **A long tool returns a handle.** The first search returns exit 8 with a job, a denominator and a poll interval;
   `job_wait` holds it with bounded waits. A dropped connection would be recovered with `job.find` and the key
   `nem-1`: one job and one charge exist, or none do.
5. **A certified static answer does not make the robot walk.** The search finds three failing worlds for a design that
   lies inside a certified cell. The two facts are about different claims, and the envelope of each says which.
6. **A counterexample is shrunk before it is argued about.** Seven edits become three, with passing neighbours and a
   solvability witness.
7. **Attribution is interventional and labelled.** Two single interventions each rescue the run, so both are labelled
   `alternative`; the placebo flips 2 of 64 forks, well under the 0.2 threshold above which nothing is named. The fill
   level is a property the payload carried from the first tick, so an intervention on it at the fork is refused with
   the earliest valid tick, zero. The attribution is `Estimated` and is a cause in the model.
8. **An edit puts evidence in question, by read set.** The mission answer survives the foot edit because it never read
   the foot region; four dynamic results do not.
9. **"None found" is not a certificate.** The second search says so in its result.
10. **Qualification spends error budget.** The dry run shows the level α₁ = 0.05/2 and what is reachable: at 200
    sealed clusters the one-sided exact bound admits at most 3 failures (0.0432 at 3, 0.0504 at 4). The committed
    request observes 2 failures, bound 0.0357, and is promoted. A second submission would run at α₂ = 0.05/6 and
    admit at most 2 (0.0425 at 2, 0.0505 at 3), so a retry costs power. The agent receives a receipt and nothing per
    world, and no scope in its token can read the sealed clusters before the campaign closes (`FROB-REF-840`).
11. **The weakest input sets the class.** The bundle holds five Certified entries and one Tested receipt; the product
    is Tested. Every exported object carries the three flags, all false: the bundle authorizes nothing.

## Appendix M. Known-answer suite

This appendix is the printed form of the known-answer registry of `frob-conformance` (§38.6). It compiles every
known answer that a chapter states: 835 rows, numbered KA-001 to KA-835, grouped by chapter in the order of the
outline. A row is a case with a truth that a test can compare against, the tolerance of the comparison, the tier
and site on which it runs, and the negative control that must make it fail. The registry is the authority; this
table is generated from it and is never edited by hand (ADR-GAUNT-02).

### M.1 How to read the suite

**Columns.**

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| KA | The row's number. Numbers are append-only: a row is never renumbered and a number is never reused (INV-GAUNT-07) |
| Where stated | The subsection or construction that states the case, with the invariant, proof obligation or gate that owns it where the chapter names one. The mark "≡ KA-nnn" means the row uses the same fixture as an earlier row in another chapter (ADR-GAUNT-06): one tests the mathematics, the other the subsystem. Marks are printed where two rows share printed constants; the registry holds the complete map |
| The case | The fixture: bodies, parameters, inputs |
| The truth | The formula or value, with the derivation steps the chapter gives. Values are carried as the chapter prints them and are not improved in transit (§38.6, rule 5) |
| Tolerance | `exact` for integers, rationals, Booleans, verdicts, labels and digests; a stated value, with the gate that states it; "to the printed digits" for half a unit in the last digit printed; `to set` where the chapter states none (OPEN-GAUNT-2) |
| Tier | The Gauntlet tier and the execution site, as `G<k> · <site>`. Tiers are those of §38.2. Sites: `host` (exact or double-precision arithmetic in a test), `auditor` (`frob-verify`), `referee`, `strict` (`batch-cpu` under the `strict` profile), `lockstep` (the throughput tiers under the `lockstep` profile), `cuda`, `metal`, `daemon`, `all tiers`. "Synthetic" and "simulated" qualify a site that runs on planted data or under the simulation runtime |
| Negative control | The mutation or planted failure that the row must catch, as the chapter states it; `none stated` where it states none (OPEN-GAUNT-3) |

**Labels.** Fixture constants are DESIGN choices. A truth derived from them by hand is DESIGN arithmetic with a
derivation file under `docs/derivations/`. A truth that quotes a planning pilot, a sibling's source or a publication
is FACT, to be re-run or re-read from its primary source before a gate cites it; such rows say so. A threshold
inside a row (a pass count, a percentage, a bound of a gate) is the TARGET of the gate named beside it. No row is a
measurement of this project: nothing here has been run on FrankenRobotics code.

**Rules.**

1. A row runs first on the weakest site that can decide it and then on every tier its gate names.
2. A row whose tier is G3 is a relation with an exact expected equality; it is also registered in §38.7. A row
   whose tier is G4 or G5 has a truth of the form "zero violations" or "equal digests".
3. A fixture stated by a construction of §10 and again by its owning chapter has a row in each place. The
   derivation file is shared.
4. A row printed with `to set` or `none stated` is an obligation, not a test: it cannot support a gate until the
   missing part is registered (GATE-GAUNT-02).
5. A row whose printed value disagrees with its own formula keeps the printed value and is listed in M.38.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

By tier: G0 135 rows, G1 591, G2 16, G3 36, G4 19, G5 38. Rows that share a fixture with an earlier row in
another chapter and are marked "≡": 14.

Gaps, each an obligation on the owning chapter and none a defect of the suite's arithmetic:

- **Controls.** 325 rows state no negative control. A further handful state a boundary behaviour where a mutation is
  needed: "a 4 mm film is refused" (§19.18), "with a 29 m budget the witness is rejected" and "a tree refuses
  localization" (§20.20). OPEN-GAUNT-3.
- **Tolerances.** 133 rows state no tolerance, or only part of one, for a real-valued truth. OPEN-GAUNT-2.
- **Truths named and not written.** §14 to §16 name closed forms for the pendulum period, the precession of a top,
  the pole of the two-wheeled balancer and the hydraulic cylinder, and do not write them; the rows that cite them
  carry no value until the derivation files exist. §14.13 sends the track rejection fixture to a belt-law known
  answer of §18 that §18.16 does not list under that name; the nearest row is the skid-steer base under exact
  no-slip, with yaw rate zero.
- **Chapters without rows.** §3, §5 and §6 state no known answers.
- **Illustrative cards.** Two rows of §15 and §18 serve one formula with different illustrative cards (a backlash
  gap closing at 0.577 rad/s with 0.0115 J against 17.5 ms and 0.083 rad/s; a critical current of 31.9 A against
  35.8 A in C-38, where G = 0.5 W/K). Both are internally consistent; the registry keeps both fixtures under
  separate identities.

carry the corrected values; the "Printed" column records what was first printed. Rows 4, 8, 10 and 11 stand as
remarks, and the gate that cites each reads the derivation file once OPEN-GAUNT-6 is closed. None changes a
verdict of a fixture.

## Appendix N. Counterexample catalogue

The plan's rule is that a plausible shortcut ships with the smallest hand-checkable case that breaks it (§3, §9).
This appendix compiles every such case that a chapter states: 384 entries, numbered CX-001 to CX-384, grouped by
chapter in the order of the outline. Each entry is the seed of at least one record in the negative-control registry
(§38.11): the shortcut is planted as a mutation or as an input, and the gates of the rule it protects must catch
it.

### N.1 How to read the catalogue

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| CX | The entry's number, append-only (INV-GAUNT-07) |
| The tempting shortcut | The argument or implementation choice that looks right |
| The smallest case that breaks it | The case, with its numbers, as the chapter states it. "No numeric case is given in the chapter" marks an entry whose refutation is stated in words only |
| The rule it protects | The invariant, decision, proof obligation, refusal code, gate or construction rule that exists because of the case |
| Defined in | The subsection or construction that states it. The mark "≡ CX-nnn" means the entry uses the same fixture as an earlier entry in another chapter |

**Rules.**

1. The same case may appear in more than one chapter, each time protecting a different rule: the two-latch task
   protects a construction in §10, an analysis in the body chapters and the controller in §22. Each statement keeps its
   entry, because the registry holds one control per protected rule and each must be caught by that rule's gates.
2. A case is carried with the chapter's numbers. Where a number is FACT from a planning pilot or from a sibling's
   source, the entry says so in its text or its chapter does; such a case is re-run in this repository before it is
   registered as a control.
3. An entry with no numeric case is an obligation on its chapter: a control needs a concrete planted defect or
   input (N.35).
4. A counterexample found in use (a false certificate, a false promotion, a withdrawn result) is appended here and
   becomes a permanent control (§25.5.5, §38.11).

### N.2 Part 0. Document control

| CX | The tempting shortcut | The smallest case that breaks it | The rule it protects | Defined in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CX-001 | Run a speed comparison first and account for the shared work afterwards | A composed solver took 1.345× the time of a specialized one (1.088× cold). The specialized batch held a residual of 575.7 µs that the solver does not touch (parsing, assembly, checking, serialization and harness, not separately timed), so no solver could have shown more than about 1.46× (842.8 ÷ 575.7): the test could not have confirmed the claim it was run to test | The ceiling implied by the work both arms share is computed before a speed comparison is locked, and the test is refused if the ceiling is below the claimed ratio (D-10) | §0.7; §2.3 item 6; §2.5 |
| CX-002 | Treat a closed bead as an accepted capability | A sibling project (FrankenMining) recorded 87 beads closed within 12 seconds with one shared close reason, serving figures from a stand-in | A bead closes with a typed reason that cites its own test, and gates require a live-dependency proof (§38) | §0.7 |

### N.3 §2 The ten-fold thesis

| CX | The tempting shortcut | The smallest case that breaks it | The rule it protects | Defined in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CX-003 | Declare ten-fold when the point estimate is at least 10 on every brief | A draft rule of that form confirmed a true ratio of 10 in at most 18% of simulated campaigns | The decision rule is specified in §39 on a pooled ratio of restricted mean times, and its power against a true ratio of 10 is computed before the sealed suite is opened; the result on the sealed suite is a finite-suite result, and a population claim needs at least 32 independent mission families (§39.20) | §2.1 |
| CX-004 | Seek the ten-fold in a faster simulator step | At a fixed sample count an infinitely fast environment step speeds training by at most 1/(1 − s): about 7.7× for a rough-terrain humanoid (s = 87%), 6.7× for a hand, 1.9× for a cart-pole, and about 1.4× from physics alone on another stack | Engine throughput is a parity requirement and not the source of the ten-fold (§36) | §2.3 item 1 |
| CX-005 | Decide one design per agent turn and rely on a fast cycle | With the same agent latency t in both arms and about 300 s of incumbent training, one design per turn gives at most (300 + t)/t: 3.5–6× for t between 60 and 120 s, and 4.4–7.8× against the 410 s one-card figure, even if the candidate spent no compute at all. A 120 s cycle with no training is 3.0–3.5× an incumbent quadruped cycle of 360–420 s | The unit of dispatch is a family: many designs are decided per turn (§17, §28) | §2.3 items 2 and 3 |
| CX-006 | Rely on pruning bad designs to cut compute per decision | Compute ratio C ÷ (c + c_T·f) with C = 410 GPU-s, c = 38 GPU-s, c_T = 410 GPU-s: about 10.8× at f = 0; ten needs f ≤ 0.7%; no f reaches ten if the cheap rung costs more than 41 GPU-s. If 16% of candidates fail trivially, pruning them cuts trainings by at most 1.19× | A cheaper cheap rung, many designs per rung, or a cheaper training rung is required; static checks are valued for feedback in seconds, not for pruning | §2.2; §2.3 item 4; §2.5 |
| CX-007 | Multiply a pruning ratio by a GPU speedup | If a fraction f of the strong baseline's matched wall time is improved by a factor r with overhead h, the speedup is at most 1/(1 − f + f/r + h): about 13.5× at f = 0.97, r = 40, h = 0.02, and infinite acceleration of 85% of the time cannot reach ten | The three terms are measured on the rival's critical path, and a pruning ratio is never multiplied by a speedup measured on work the pruning already removed (D-10) | §2.3 item 5 |
| CX-008 | Report speed on the missions that finished | If the candidate misses a fraction q of deadlines then R ≤ 1/q: with 12% unfinished the ratio cannot exceed 25/3 ≈ 8.33, and an arm that leaves one mission in eight unresolved cannot show ten-fold | Restricted mean time charges the deadline H for an unresolved mission; a failure is a failed cell and never an excluded cell (§8.3 rule 2) | §2.1; §2.3 item 7 |
| CX-009 | Use a sampling controller as the evaluator because it needs no training | The most sample-efficient published controller costs about 4 × 10³ times a policy rollout per simulated second: a battery of 256 twenty-second episodes takes about 86 minutes of a device against about 1.3 s for a policy | The sampling controller is a screening rung, a fallback and a source of demonstrations; it never stands in for a trained policy as acceptance evidence, and its own episodes are accepted only under the delivered-controller lane of §22.8 (BET-27) | §2.5 |

| CX-038 | Score an estimator after fitting a scale | A 2 m estimate of a 1 m motion has zero residual after a factor of ½ | A metric gravity-referenced estimate is aligned with one translation and one yaw per trajectory and never with a fitted scale | C-13 |
| CX-039 | File a reassociation as a bit-exact rewrite | In `f32` with a = 10⁸, b = −10⁸, c = 1: (a + b) + c is 1 and a + (b + c) is 0 | Rewrite classes: class E changes no bit and ships a replayable trace; class R (reassociation, distribution, fused multiply-add) makes a different kernel with a new identity; the trace checker rejects the misfiled rewrite (T-27) | C-14 |
| CX-040 | Freeze a fixed-n decision rule without listing the verdicts it can return | Two-sided exact Clopper–Pearson rule at n = 64 with a ±5 point indifference band: perfect concordance gives [−0.0662, +0.0662], so no outcome can return a tie. The recorded rule with 64 pairs could return three of its four verdicts; the fourth was first reachable at 86 pairs | A fixed-n study ships a pre-analysis of reachable verdicts (T-26); a study that needs an unreachable verdict is refused at admission | C-15; §0.7 |
| CX-041 | Use the reset Jacobian as the derivative across an event | Bouncing ball, state (y, v), reset (y, −r·v), impact speed v⁻ < 0: the saltation matrix is [[−r, 0], [−(1 + r)·g/v⁻, −r]] with determinant r². The reset Jacobian diag(1, −r) has the wrong sign in the first entry, omits the coupling in the second row, and for r = 1 has determinant −1 where the elastic bounce preserves area with determinant +1 | Event derivatives use the saltation matrix and carry the label `saltation` (D-15) | C-16 |
| CX-042 | Transport a derivative across an event by a symmetry without checking that the relabeling commutes with the event | Two bouncing balls and the swap of their labels satisfy D h(x⁺)·Ξ_e(x⁻) = Ξ_{h·e}(h·x⁻)·D h(x⁻) when the restitutions are equal and violate it by terms proportional to r_L − r_R when they differ | A symmetry is used across an event only where the commuting identity holds | C-16 |
| CX-043 | Return a derivative at a grazing event | A ball whose apex touches a ceiling: the guard is not crossed transversally, and the query returns `refused`, not a matrix | Refusal near grazing, at an ambiguous event order, across an active-set change or at frictional degeneracy (FROB-REF-263) | C-16 |
| CX-044 | Certify the convex hull of two feasible designs | Feet at (±1 − e, ±1) m, each capped at 0.5 N, carry a load W at the origin; the positive-x pair must supply W·(1 + e)/2. The designs (e, W) = (0, 1.9) and (0.9, 1) each need 0.95 N and are feasible; their midpoint (0.45, 1.45) needs 841/800 N from a pair capped at 1 N | An inner cell needs a witness for the whole cell; only a union of proved inner cells is inner; the midpoint must be excluded from every inner set (BET-20) | C-17 ≡ CX-010 |
| CX-045 | Accept one policy per world as evidence that one policy works for all worlds (∀w ∃π offered for ∃π ∀w) | Docking fixture with the packet arriving late, gains g ∈ {1, 2}: with first command p the remaining commands must be (1/g − 2p, p − 1/g), which differ by ½ between the gains. Each world alone has a successful open-loop command and no single command succeeds in both | Quantifiers are part of the claim; evidence for an easier quantifier order is rejected by type and by the auditor (D-12; §8.3 rule 8; FROB-REF-826) | C-17; C-19 |
| CX-046 | Evaluate a strict requirement with a non-strict comparator, or by an infimum | At U = ¾ and ε = 5/16 the docking residual is exactly zero and the strict predicate fails: with p = 5/8 both worlds can report 15/16 while needing −¼ and −¾. On 0 < w ≤ 1 every realization has w > 0 although the infimum is 0 | Strict, non-strict and equality atoms are evaluated with their declared comparators; a uniform positive margin is a separate, stronger request; strict decisions are computed exactly (D-18) | C-17; C-19 |
| CX-047 | Multiply stage pass rates to get the mission pass rate | Among 20 equally likely worlds two stages each pass in 19. The mission passes in 18 worlds if the failing worlds differ and in 19 if they coincide | A chance constraint preserves the joint law across stages or allocates failure budgets that sum to the allowance; a product bound needs conditional success at every reached history | C-17 |
| CX-048 | Intersect per-world answers to obtain the joint answer | F(V) ⊆ ⋂ over w ∈ V of F({w}), and the gap is what the controller cannot observe in time: in the docking fixture with a late packet each of the worlds g = 1 and g = 2 is solvable alone and the joint query has no solution | The joint query is answered as stated; per-world evidence is not combined by intersection (D-9, D-12) | C-18 |
| CX-049 | Keep an inclusion when the world set grows | Docking family: enlarging W by one hidden gain 33/32 keeps every exclusion and forces a recheck of every inclusion. The inclusion at (U, ε) = (¾, 1/64) reverses, because the reading (65/64)·p is possible under gains 1 and 33/32 for every first command p; the least worst-case terminal error becomes 1/65 m | Verdicts have polarity: an inner certificate survives when W shrinks, Π grows or A weakens, and must be rechecked on the opposite moves; an exclusion is the reverse | C-18 |
| CX-050 | Trust a cache key or a dependency record to mean the verdict still holds | A dependency graph with one edge omitted returns a promotion that fresh replay contradicts | Reuse needs a recorded implication; the stale-verdict control must be caught by the shadow recompute (D-11; BET-33) | C-18 |
| CX-051 | Take pairwise compatibility as joint compatibility | Commands (x, y) ∈ [0, 1]² with three variants requiring x ≥ 2/3, y ≥ 2/3 and x + y ≤ 1: every pair of sets intersects and the triple does not. Pairwise compatibility would have authorized one shared controller; two labels suffice and one is impossible | The label count is a colouring of the hypergraph whose edges are the inclusion-minimal collections with empty intersection | C-19 |
| CX-052 | Count repeated sensor reads as independent evidence | A binary probe correct with probability ¾ gives 27/32 with three independent reads, 459/512 with five and 3807/4096 with seven, and stays at ¾ after any number of reads that share one fault bit | Error dependence, not per-read accuracy, sets the value of redundancy | C-19 |
| CX-053 | Expect more training to overcome a sensing limit | Docking fixture: if the only informative packet arrives after the third command is committed, no causal policy docks in both worlds for any U and ε; the two worlds deliver identical packet histories up to the commitment deadline and need disjoint commands | An indistinguishability witness ends a policy search before it is paid for (`mission.refute`) | C-19 |
| CX-054 | Specify sensor accuracy separately from actuator authority and the probing command | Docking fixture at U = ¾: the probe p = ¼ tolerates ε < 1/8 and the probe p = 5/8 tolerates ε < 5/16 on the same actuator; in general ε < (U + ½)/4 | Sensor, actuator and delivery time appear in one design inequality; the probe and the feedback are chosen together | C-19 |
| CX-055 | Read a full-rank local observability Gramian as distinguishability | Range anchors at (−1, 0) and (1, 0) both read √2 from (0, 1) and from (0, −1). With unit variances the information matrix is the identity at both points, yet a controller that must pick the side fails. A third anchor at (0, 2) reads 1 or 3, and closed reading intervals of half-width ε separate exactly when ε < 1 | Every calibration and placement analysis also runs a global ambiguity search | C-20 |
| CX-056 | Two designs whose geometric ratios match are dynamically similar, so a verdict moves between them | Scale a body by λ at constant density: mass × λ³, static joint torque × λ⁴. With a motor whose torque scales as λ³ the group τ_max/(m₀·g·ℓ₀) falls as 1/λ, so a design that stands at one size fails at twice the size. A fixed latency has delay group ∝ λ^(−½): it doubles at one quarter of the size | Every dimensionless group must match before a verdict is transported; differing groups are reported by name (C-21, D-11) | C-21 |
| CX-057 | A physical constant may sit in a kernel as a pure number | Scale lengths × 4, times × 2, masses × 2 with gravity unchanged. A homogeneous kernel reproduces every significand bit and branch; a kernel with a hidden dimensional constant differs on its first step | Dimensional homogeneity of every kernel (T-09); the power-of-two similarity test | C-21 |
| CX-058 | Quotient a campaign by the mechanical symmetry group Γ_mech of the chassis | Ten leg types on a hexapod: dihedral symmetry of order 12 gives 86,185 classes. With a front-only lidar only the sagittal mirror survives and there are 500,500 classes; counting with Γ_mech merges designs that the closed loop distinguishes | The acting group of a campaign is Γ_obs, never Γ_mech alone (C-22, C-09) | C-22 |
| CX-059 | Designs that agree on some mission observables can be merged | Eight ballast slugs enter the dynamics through count, Σx and Σx². Slots {1, 4} and {2, 3} have equal count and equal Σx = 5 but Σx² = 17 and 13: they are different rigid bodies | A projection class requires equality over all active observables, and merged pairs must replay bit-identically (C-22) | C-22 |
| CX-060 | A design-conditioned policy may read its tokens in file order | Exchange two legs in the description of one robot: the robot is unchanged and the actions change. FACT (source register): a published morphology-conditioned policy lost most of its return when the same robots were re-described in equivalent conventions | A family policy is natural under re-description, σ(d′) = φ·σ(d); permutation-equivariant tokens (C-23) | C-23 |
| CX-061 | More equivariance is better: make the policy equivariant under all rotations | A rotation about a horizontal axis does not preserve gravity. The rigid motions that do are rotations about the vertical, translations and reflections through vertical planes, and the layers are equivariant under those only | The gravity control of C-24: a horizontal-axis rotation must not be a symmetry of the policy | C-24 |
| CX-062 | Audit a small share of worlds on the high tier and correct by inverse weights; the cheap prediction only has to be roughly right | With Y ∈ {0, 1}, a prediction wrong by a constant ½ and audit probability 0.1, the added variance is (1 − p)/p·(Y − m)² = 9 × ¼ = 2.25, worse than auditing everything. The estimate stays unbiased; the cost is variance | Tier correction is funded only where the measured ρ supports it (kill below 0.7); p_min bounds the weights (C-25) | C-25 |
| CX-063 | Calibrate the conformal margin on the designs that were promoted, since those are the ones that ran both rungs | On a fixture where the residual abs(y_hi − ĝ(y_lo)) correlates with the cheap score, q̂ computed from promoted designs only under-covers | The audit set is drawn by keyed randomness before any score exists and run at fixed n (C-26) | C-26 |
| CX-064 | A dozen audit designs are enough for a 95% conformal margin | The index is ⌈(n + 1)·(1 − α)⌉: n = 39 gives the 38th smallest residual; n = 18 gives 19, which exceeds n. Fewer than 19 audit designs cannot support α = 0.05 | Minimum audit-set size for a declared α (C-26) | C-26 |
| CX-065 | A defensive mixture proposal makes certifying the absence of failures cheaper | With q = β·p + (1 − β)·q′ the weights are at most 1/β, and zero observed failures certify only p ≤ ln(1/δ)/(β·n). At δ = 0.05 and p* = 10⁻⁴ crude sampling needs about 3·10⁴ nominal episodes, and the mixture needs that many on its nominal share | Certification and exploration are two lanes that never mix (D-16); no sampler discounts certified absence (C-27) | C-27 |
| CX-066 | Forking a world at a splitting level multiplies the evidence | A fork without fresh randomness is an identical copy: children that share the parent's streams reproduce the parent's trajectory bit for bit and add nothing | Child streams are keyed by child world addresses; duplicate children are detected (C-27, §11.1) | C-27 |
| CX-067 | The shrunk failing world is the smallest one, and its size measures distance to failure | Edit 1 (a grease patch) fails the design; edit 2 (a rug over the patch) masks it. {1} fails and {1, 2} passes, so failure is not monotone in the edit set. With eight edits and failure exactly when 3 and 6 are present the search returns {3, 6}, which is 1-minimal by construction and nothing more | A result is reported as 1-minimal under the tested edit relation; no distance to a boundary is claimed (C-28, §12.3) | C-28 |
| CX-068 | Any world in which the design fails is a counterexample | A doorway narrower than the body fails every controller: it is a useless trap and says nothing about the design | A counterexample is kept only with a solvability witness from the candidate's own body, actuators and mission constraints (C-28) | C-28 |
| CX-069 | A large Shapley value identifies a necessary cause | Two interventions A and B. Case 1: either alone prevents the failure, v({A}) = v({B}) = v({A, B}) = 1. Case 2: only both together prevent it, v({A}) = v({B}) = 0, v({A, B}) = 1. Both give φ = (½, ½); case 1 has two but-for causes with PN = 1 and case 2 has none | A cause is named by the probability of necessity against the placebo flip rate; Shapley is a budgeted summary (C-29) | C-29 |
| CX-070 | An intervention that flips the outcome is a cause | On a fixture where every last-place nudge of an unrelated state flips the outcome, any intervention appears to prevent the failure | The placebo fork: c is a cause only when PN(c) exceeds the placebo flip rate ρ₀; otherwise the report is `chaotic: unattributable` (C-29) | C-29 |
| CX-071 | A design-parameter change can be tested by forking at a snapshot just before the failure | For a gear ratio or a mass, the thermal state, the estimator state and the policy's history at the snapshot would all differ under the changed design, and an intervention at a snapshot answers a question about the continuation only | Design-parameter interventions re-run from the episode start on the same streams; a fork is refused when the controller cannot adapt without retraining (C-29) | C-29 |
| CX-072 | The robustness of a conjunction is the minimum of the raw margins | A clearance of 0.02 m and a thermal margin of 15 K: the minimum is 0.02 (clearance binds) in metres and kelvin, and 15 (the thermal margin binds) in millimetres and kelvin. With declared scales 0.10 m and 10 K the values are 0.2 and 1.5 and clearance binds in every unit system | Every atom has a declared scale of its own dimension; robustness is ρ = ψ/s (C-30) | C-30 |
| CX-073 | When an episode ends early, evaluate "always" over the samples that exist | An episode that ends at 30 s under G_[0, 45 s]: the minimum over 30 s can be positive although the requirement was never tested on the last 15 s | A window the trace does not cover yields `undetermined`, never a truncated minimum (C-30, §24.5) | C-30 |
| CX-074 | Project the action onto the barrier row, then clip to the actuator box | R = I, u_π = (1, 0), box [0, 1]², row u₁ + u₂ ≥ 1.5. Projection ignoring the box gives (1.25, 0.25), outside the box; clipping gives (1, 0.25), with u₁ + u₂ = 1.25 < 1.5. The breakpoint method gives (1, 0.5) | The one-row filter is solved exactly inside the box; multi-row solves carry a mandatory KKT check with a passive fallback (C-31) | C-31 |
| CX-075 | For every disturbance there is a safe action, so the filter is safe | A certificate proved in the order ∀w ∃u lets the action be chosen after the disturbance and the estimation error are seen, which the controller cannot do | The quantifier order is ∃u ∀(w, e); a certificate in the other order is rejected (C-31, FROB-REF-826) | C-31 |
| CX-076 | An energy budget may leave out small sources | Lifting 8 kg over a 12 mm sill needs 8 × 9.81 × 0.012 = 0.94176 J, above a 0.90 J budget, so the family is excluded; 0.05 J of approach kinetic energy (0.95 J) removes the exclusion. In the stop budget (0.64 + 0.50 + 0.25 + 0.10 = 1.49 J of 2.00 J) a missing gravity term over the stroke makes the checker reject | A budget has a term for every source on the declared load path (T-28); the omitted-term control | C-31 |
| CX-077 | The first moment of the load can be passed where the support torque is expected | With +z up the support torque is (P_y, −P_x, 0). P = (60, 30) N·m with the stance forces gives (30, −60, 0) N·m; a packet that passes (60, 30) as the torque has the wrong components and sign | Every field of a bundle is typed with frame, origin, sign and unit (§12.4, FROB-REF-829) | C-32 |
| CX-078 | An inclusion proved for independently commanded foot forces holds for the same robot on a passive suspension | Stance fixture at b = ¼ m with a 160 N cap: active allocation gives (155, 135, 105, 5) N, inside the cap; equal passive springs give (175, 115, 85, 25) N, above it | A typed result states its authority model; the assumption `authority` travels with the certificate (C-32) | C-32 |
| CX-079 | Centre of mass inside the support polygon and total foot capacity above the weight means the stance is feasible | Stance fixture at b = 1/5 m: the centre of mass (150 mm, 75 mm) lies inside the feet at (±1/3, ±1/5) m and total capacity is 4 × 160 = 640 N against 400 N, yet the moment equations give f₊₊ − f₋₋ = 165 N with f₊₊ ≤ 160 N and f₋₋ ≥ 0. FACT (planning pilot, to be re-run): the test accepted 1,596 bodies the exact model rejects | The stance family is decided by the exact model with per-foot bounds and a dual witness (C-32, T-22) | C-32 |
| CX-080 | A region certificate can be had by paving the whole design box | 10⁴ boxes are 13 bisections, less than one cut per axis in 20 dimensions: a uniform box keeps 0.64 of each side (0.41 in 10 dimensions) | Certificates are issued per constraint on sub-boxes of about six parameters or fewer and assembled by products, monotonicity and witnesses (C-32, C-17) | C-32 |
| CX-081 | Clearance can be tested with one scalar radius | A thin rod of length L turns a right-angle corner between corridors of width a exactly when L ≤ 2√2·a. The circumscribed-disc test, L ≤ a, refuses every rod between a and 2.83·a although each passes; the inscribed-disc test accepts rods longer than 2.83·a, which jam | Clearance is certified from both sides on complexes in SE(2), with a reported band (C-33) | C-33 |
| CX-082 | A linkage that closes at every target pose reaches them all | Links 4 (ground), 1 (crank), 3.5 (coupler), 3 (rocker): 1 + 4 ≤ 3.5 + 3, so the crank turns fully and the two assembly circuits are disjoint. A candidate whose target poses lie on different circuits satisfies closure at each pose and cannot move between them without disassembly | The circuit and branch certificate of lane 1 (C-34) | C-34 |
| CX-083 | Every tracked root passed the α-test, so the solution set is complete | An α-test proves a nearby nonsingular root and nothing about completeness. The Stewart–Gough forward problem has 40 solutions: a run that certifies fewer, or loses a path, has not found them all | A result is `Complete` only when the certified count equals an independent generic count with no lost path; otherwise `Partial(certified, lost)` (C-34) | C-34 |
| CX-084 | Rainflow counting can be run window by window | The history 0, 10, 0 split into the windows [0, 10] and [10, 0] holds one full cycle of range 10; a counter that drops residues at window ends counts none | The residue of open half-cycles is carried between windows (C-35) | C-35 |
| CX-085 | Rare overload cycles can be dropped from a fatigue history | With m = 3, 10⁶ cycles at a life of 2·10⁶ give D = 0.5; 10³ cycles at five times the amplitude (life 16,000) add 0.0625: 0.1% of the cycles carry 11% of the damage | Load cases are the recorded envelope over qualified missions; the damage sum keeps every cycle (C-35) | C-35 |
| CX-086 | Momentum conservation is the test of a step for any system with a symmetry | Chaplygin sleigh: v̇ = a·ω², ω̇ = −m·a·v·ω/(I + m·a²). The energy ½·m·v² + ½·(I + m·a²)·ω² is constant, since m·v·(a·ω²) − m·a·v·ω·ω = 0, while the direction of linear momentum turns | The momentum test of C-04 is not applied to nonholonomic systems; they are tested by energy (C-36) | C-36 |
| CX-087 | If the variational step conserves momentum, its implicit solve is right | Evaluate step 2 with the differential at +hξ_k instead of −hξ_k (the other trivialization). Momentum stays exact, because the transport of step 3 conserves it for any ξ; the energy bound and reversibility are lost | The variational step is tested by bounded energy error (÷4 when h is halved) and by reversal, never by momentum alone (C-36) | C-36 |
| CX-088 | Model every wheel as an ideal rolling constraint | Four fixed wheels as ideal rows return ω = 0 under any command: a skid-steer base cannot turn. With cone-bounded rows it turns with its lateral multipliers on their cones | Rolling rows carry traction limits; ideal rolling is a limit of the same solve (C-36, C-07) | C-36 |
| CX-089 | Sliding friction and torsional friction are independent rows with their own coefficients | At v_t = r·ω_n the coupled law gives a tangential friction magnitude of μ·λ_n/√2; the uncoupled model gives μ·λ_n. A spinning contact resists sliding less | One four-dimensional cone for sliding and spin (C-37) | C-37 |
| CX-090 | Heat entering the winding is a loss, and the node's temperature rise is stored energy | A ledger that books the same heat as both stored and lost shows a deficit equal to that heat | H + U changes only by port power and by the heat that leaves to ambient; ledger closure in all three modes (C-38) | C-38 |
| CX-091 | A passing second-law check shows the thermal model is right | The check has content only as a sign check on each assigned loss: it cannot fail for a correct model. Its one catch: a regenerative mode with a negated copper loss gives σ < 0 | The entropy balance is a derived report, used as a sign control and not as validation (C-38) | C-38 |
| CX-092 | Any measurement of the mechanism will identify it; fit a richer curve | Laws μ₁(v) = 0.5 and μ₂(v) = 0.3 + 0.4·v agree at 0.5 m/s and imply opposite designs at the mission speed of 1.5 m/s (0.5 against 0.9). A probe at 0.5 m/s separates nothing at any precision; a probe at 1.0 m/s reads 0.5 or 0.7 and separates them exactly when the reading error is below 0.1 | A probe is chosen so that the reading sets of the decision blocks are disjoint over the nuisance intervals (C-39) | C-39 |
| CX-093 | A probe that separates the admitted mechanisms settles the design decision | A third law that follows μ₁ up to 1.0 m/s and departs later defeats the 1.0 m/s probe. FACT (planning pilot, to be re-run): a probe synthesized for three admitted laws chose correctly in 675 of 675 in-class cases; a fourth law reversed all 225 held-out decisions; direct measurement at mission dwell was right in 900 of 900 | A probe certificate is conditional on the admitted set ℳ and says so; direct measurement at mission conditions is always an admitted probe (C-39) | C-39 |
| CX-094 | Dominance can be checked by enclosing each design's outcomes separately and comparing | z ∈ [0, 1]; A succeeds when z ≥ 3/5 and B when z ≥ 2/5. Separate enclosures give {0, 1} for each and admit all four pairs, including (success, failure), which no shared z produces | Dominance is unreachability of (success, failure) in the product system on shared inputs (C-40) | C-40 |
| CX-095 | A product enclosure that covers each design's outcome set covers the joint outcomes | A product whose internal branches are wrongly tied reaches only (0, 0) and (1, 1). Its projections cover both marginal outcome sets, and it hides a reachable (1, 0) | The checker demands joint coverage; one mislabeled branch invalidates the certificate (C-40) | C-40 |
| CX-096 | Pair two designs by seed and tick, and the worlds match | Two tyres on different paths over a patterned floor meet different friction at the same tick. A product coupled by tick and not by position reports a false regression or hides a true one | Shared inputs are compiled at physical coordinates: one space-indexed field read at each robot's contact point (C-40) | C-40 |
| CX-097 | "B never loses to A" means B meets the mission | In the same fixture neither design is guaranteed: A fails for z < 3/5 and B for z < 2/5, while the paired verdict of no loss holds on the whole interval | The answer carries the paired verdict and each design's absolute verdict separately (C-40) | C-40 |

### N.8 §11 Conventions

| CX | The tempting shortcut | The smallest case that breaks it | The rule it protects | Defined in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CX-098 | The coadjoint in the Euler–Poincaré equation carries a minus sign: μ̇ = −ad_ξᵀ μ | Force-free body with the origin at the centre of mass. With ad*_ξ = ad_ξᵀ: v̇ = v × ω, so d(R·v)/dt = R·(ω × v + v̇) = 0 and the world-frame velocity is constant. With the opposite sign d(R·v)/dt = 2R·(ω × v): a free body changes its velocity with no force | ad*_ξ = ad_ξᵀ with μ̇ = ad*_ξ μ + w; the map −ad_ξᵀ is never written ad* (§11.2, T-16, PO-MARROW-01) | §11.2 |
| CX-099 | A wrench changes frame by the same matrix as a twist | R = I, p = (1, 0, 0) m, wrench (0, (0, 0, 1) N) in b. The pushforward Ad_g⁻ᵀ gives torque p × f = (0, −1, 0) N·m and the same force. The twist map Ad_g gives zero torque: the moment arm is lost, and the planar fixture of C-04 fails | Three typed frame maps, `TwistMap`, `WrenchPushforward`, `WrenchPullback`; no function accepts one where another is expected (§11.3) | §11.3 |
| CX-100 | Angular velocity mirrors like any other vector | Sagittal mirror P = diag(1, −1, 1). Axial vectors map by det(P)·P = −P: the yaw axis e_z goes to −e_z, so a robot turning left becomes a robot turning right, and the pitch axis e_y maps to itself. Treated as polar, the yaw rate is left unchanged | Polar vectors map by P and axial vectors by det(P)·P; the step-equivariance test of T-10 (§11.4) | §11.4 |
| CX-101 | A body with no declared wall thickness can default to a solid of its outer shape | A thin spherical shell of radius r has I = (2/3)·m·r², a solid ball (2/5)·m·r²; for an enclosure the solid default is wrong in mass by an order of magnitude (C-03 gives a case with a factor of 18.8) | The shell rule; a solid body above the plausibility bound of its part class is refused unless the fill is declared (FROB-REF-168, §11.5) | §11.5 |
| CX-102 | The curvature of the connection is ∂ᵢ𝔸ⱼ − ∂ⱼ𝔸ᵢ + [𝔸ᵢ, 𝔸ⱼ] | Constant connection 𝔸₁ = e_x, 𝔸₂ = e_y on SO(3): the curl vanishes, (D𝔸)₁₂ = −[e_x, e_y] = −e_z, and a small loop of area da rotates the body by +da about z, as exp(−a·e_x)·exp(−b·e_y)·exp(a·e_x)·exp(b·e_y) ≈ exp(a·b·e_z) confirms. The + formula predicts −da, wrong by twice the answer | (D𝔸)ᵢⱼ = ∂ᵢ𝔸ⱼ − ∂ⱼ𝔸ᵢ − [𝔸ᵢ, 𝔸ⱼ] with ξ = −𝔸(s)·ṡ (§11.6, T-20; the wrong-sign control of C-08) | §11.6 |
| CX-103 | A 30 Hz policy on 400 Hz physics can run every thirteenth physics step | L = 1,200 base units per second; physics every 3 units, policy every 40. The policy tick at unit 40 falls one unit after the physics boundary at 39 and two before the one at 42; thirteen steps are 39 units, a period of 32.5 ms instead of 33⅓ ms | Rational periods with integer phase accumulators; a process need not be a multiple of the physics step, and no period is rounded (§11.7) | §11.7 |
| CX-104 | A force sensor reading is the force at the sample instant, and an impact on a window boundary can go to either window | An impact of 0.2 N·s inside a 10 ms exposure contributes 20 N to that window's average and nothing to its neighbour; an impact at exactly instant b belongs to the window ending at b | A reading is a functional of the history over the half-open window (a, b]; each impulse is added once and divided by the exposure (§11.8) | §11.8 |
| CX-105 | A decision may use any packet whose timestamp is earlier than the decision | The timestamp is a label written on the sensor's own clock and is unconstrained by causality. In the docking fixture of C-19 the same packet is on time when its arrival precedes the second decision and worthless when it follows the third command, whatever its timestamp | A decision uses only packets whose arrival is not later than the decision; a packet is never visible before its arrival (§11.8) | §11.8 |

### N.9 §12 Lemma: proofs, certificates, the offline auditor

| CX | The tempting shortcut | The smallest case that breaks it | The rule it protects | Defined in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CX-106 | A bundle whose hashes are all consistent is a valid certificate | A bundle with an unknown proof kind and consistent hashes: every digest matches and no checker implements the argument. | CX-107 | A certificate that checks can be offered for any query about the same model | The docking cell (U, ε) = (¾, ¼) with the packet on time is accepted for the inclusion; the same bundle with its quantifiers reordered is rejected, although every hash is still consistent | The quantifier prefix, domain and assumption set of a certificate must match the query (FROB-REF-826) | §12.4, §12.7 |
| CX-108 | A witness is valid if its numbers are right, whatever order they are listed in | Stance specimen: forces (160, 130, 110, 0) N are typed to the port order [++, +−, −+, −−]. ### N.10 §13 Marrow: the algebraic core

| CX | The tempting shortcut | The smallest case that breaks it | The rule it protects | Defined in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CX-116 | A free-body integrator that conserves kinetic energy has the right coadjoint sign (equivalently: ad* is "the negative transpose" of ad) | Inertia diag(1, 2, 3) kg·m², ω = (1, 1, 0) rad/s, π = (1, 2, 0). Correct law: π̇ = π × ω = (0, 0, −1). Reversed sign: (0, 0, +1). Both give ω·π̇ = 0, so kinetic energy is conserved either way. The body-frame rate of spatial angular momentum π̇ + ω × π is (0, 0, 0) with the correct sign and (0, 0, 2) with the wrong one | ADR-MARROW-05 (two coadjoints, each with its own type and sign); the free-body and coadjoint-pair laws of §13.8; the mutation rule (each convention guarded by at least three fixtures); GATE-MARROW-04 | §13.3, §13.10 |
| CX-117 | The lower three rows of a space screw Jacobian are the point Jacobian of the tool | Planar 2R arm, links 0.4 m and 0.3 m, angles 0 and π/2, tool force (10, 0) N. The point Jacobian is [[−0.3, −0.3], [0.4, 0.0]] m/rad and gives joint torques (−3, −3) N·m; the lower rows of the space screw Jacobian give (0, 0) | Frame-typed Jacobians and wrench maps (`WrenchPushforward` against `WrenchPullback`, §13.3); the planar 2R known answer | §13.10 |
| CX-118 | A mechanically symmetric robot may tie policy weights, augment data or deduplicate designs under its mechanical group | A quadruped built fore-aft and left-right symmetric has Γ_mech = C₂ × C₂ of order 4. One forward lidar on the torso is fixed by the left-right mirror and moved by the fore-aft mirror and the half-turn, so Γ_obs = C₂ of order 2. A policy tied under C₂ × C₂ must walk backwards as the mirror image of walking forwards while seeing only forwards | ADR-MARROW-06; PO-MARROW-04; GATE-MARROW-03; FROB-REF-109 for a false declaration | §13.4 |
| CX-119 | A failed search over symmetric (tied, deterministic) policies shows the task is infeasible | Two identical latches, of which exactly one must be closed. At an observation fixed by the mirror a deterministic equivariant controller must issue an action fixed by the mirror, so it commands both latches alike, and both matching commands fail. A controller that draws one latch at random is equivariant in law and succeeds | A failed search excludes only the policy class searched; `frob-algebra` exposes fixed subspaces so that A-03 lists the observations at which tying forces tied actions | §13.4 |
| CX-120 | A task that is symmetric in law may be reduced by symmetry inside each world | A quadruped crossing a patch that is slippery on one side only. The world distribution can be mirror-invariant in law, which licenses augmentation; no single world is mirror-invariant, which forbids reduction inside it | Reduction inside one world uses Stab(context), not Γ_obs; the table of uses in §13.4 | §13.4 |
| CX-121 | If the encoder permutation of a symmetry still exists, the symmetry still holds | Changing one foot's sole material leaves the encoder permutation intact and breaks the transition symmetry: the representation exists and the group element does not | Γ_mech preserves contact laws and interface cards; both facts are recorded by A-03; GATE-MARROW-03 lists a changed sole material among its planted asymmetries | §13.4 |
| CX-122 | Every irreducible block of an equivariant layer takes one real scalar per pair of copies | C₃ permuting three legs cyclically. The equivariant maps ℝ³ → ℝ³ are the circulants, three parameters: the trivial block plus one two-dimensional block of complex type, 1 + 2 = 3. Giving the two-dimensional block one scalar yields two parameters and only the symmetric circulants, which are the D₃-equivariant maps; x ↦ (x₂ − x₃, x₃ − x₁, x₁ − x₂) becomes unrepresentable | ADR-MARROW-07 (real and complex blocks, Reynolds operator as oracle); PO-MARROW-05; the blocks law of §13.8 | §13.5 |
| CX-123 | A strict inequality that selects a discrete outcome can be evaluated in plain single precision | The single-precision numbers nearest 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5 in x² + y² ≤ z². In single precision the two sides are equal, so the plain test reports the point inside the cone. The exact value of x² + y² − z² for those stored numbers is +1.19 × 10⁻⁸: the point is outside. A fused multiply-add gives a third rounding sequence | ADR-MARROW-08; the `Guarded` class with its exact integer fallback; the `frob-kir` lint against `Plain` predicates on selects whose arms differ; GATE-MARROW-05 | §13.7 |
| CX-124 | A mirrored revolute joint can be written with the mirrored axis P·a and keep its coordinate | For a reflection (det P = −1) an axis is an axial vector and maps to det(P)·P·a. A design that writes P·a instead must negate the coordinate, its limits, and its encoder and gear signs; hiding the sign inside a rigid transform is how mirrored encoders read backwards | ADR-MARROW-09 (a reflection is an `Isometry` with an explicit determinant, not a `Transform`); the reflections law of §13.8; the planted mutation "a missing parity sign on a mirrored axis" | §13.2, §13.3 |

| CX-127 | A declared inertia that passes pseudo-inertia positivity is physically possible for its part | A 1 kg part with principal moments 0.008 kg·m² each, declared inside a sphere of radius 0.10 m: the mass-weighted mean squared distance tr(I_C)/(2m) is 0.012 m², above R² = 0.010 m². | CX-129 | A limb's port inertia is positive definite, so it can be inverted at the port and can stand for a limb in contact | Eliminating a joint with axis s gives I − I·s·(sᵀI·s)⁻¹·sᵀI, which sends s to zero; with I the identity and s the first basis vector the packet is diag(0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1). A chain of massless parents is singular, and contact rows couple every limb through the base | The `SymPsd6` type of `LimbPortPacket`; PO-SKEL-04; the three consumer rules of §14.6; stage 2 refuses massless chains; KILL-SKEL-PORT | §14.6 |

A third beacon at (0, 2) reads 1 and 3 and separates them when the range error is below 1 | Stage 8 alias search (`aliased-passive`, `aliased-all-probes`); FROB-REF-120; the bound (1 + TV)/2; KILL-SKEL-ALIAS | §14.11 |
